acceptance_criteria: Using the bridge variant selected in 03.5, Rust code prepares a packet and the generated static JS adapter submits a correctly rendered simple frame (a textured, transformed mesh using AffineRows) in Safari and Chrome; device creation negotiates required features/limits and records the capability record; error scopes are pushed/popped without intervening awaits and results awaited afterwards; the same work issued by direct JS WebGPU produces identical pixels; command transfer, copies, initialization and per-frame synchronization costs are measured and recorded.

title: First integrated counterexample suite on the bridge (red-A/blue-B, bundle reset, layout, ABA)
description:
## Full scope

First integrated counterexample suite on the bridge: red-A/blue-B queue-write snapshot, bundle-then-direct-draw state reset, AffineRows vs mat4x3 end to end, memory growth and reentry under borrow, stale handle publication, delayed worker response after ID reuse, separate native-context ownership

## Summary

The mandatory counterexamples that the plan says must be in "the first integrated tests" (§11.7), implemented against the real bridge before any renderer abstraction is built.

## Background (plan §6.7, §8.2 "Bundle reuse has a structural contract", §7.5, §6.5, §6.6, §6.9, §11.7, §14.8, §23 [S33], [S37]; AGENTS.md "Mandatory Counterexample Suite")

| Counterexample | Guards against |
|---|---|
| Red-A / blue-B queue-write snapshot | Treating queue writes as per-draw snapshots: two `writeBuffer` calls before one submission make both recorded draws read the second value |
| Bundle-then-direct-draw state reset | Falsely warm binding/pipeline caches after `executeBundles` (state resets even for an empty bundle list) |
| `AffineRows` vs `mat4x3` layout | Silent 48/64-byte layout corruption |
| Growth/reentry under borrow | Views surviving memory growth or callbacks during a live borrow |
| Stale handle publication | A delayed result publishing into a recycled slot |
| Delayed worker response after ID reuse | ABA handle collisions |
| Separate native-context ownership | Assuming `WebGLTexture`/`GPUTexture` interchange or shared realms |

## Technical approach

- Red-A/blue-B: render to target A with the shared uniform = red; mutate to blue; render to target B; submit one combined schedule built through the bridge using per-use versioned slices; assert A red, B blue. Add a "wrong implementation" toggle that uses one slot to prove the test detects the failure.
- Bundle-then-direct: record a bundle binding pipeline P1/group G1; in a pass, `executeBundles([bundle])` then issue a direct draw needing P2/G2; with the adapter's state cache deliberately un-invalidated the draw must fail validation or render wrong; with the fix it renders right. Include the empty-bundle-list variant.
- AffineRows end-to-end: upload a known matrix as rows; vertex shader transforms `(x,y,z,1)`; read back; compare with CPU `Matrix4` result; include a `mat4x3` fixture expected to be rejected by the schema writer.
- Growth/reentry: force `memory.grow` inside a borrow scope in debug (expect detection) and outside (expect view rebuild and correct data).
- Stale handle / ID reuse: allocate a texture handle, retire it, allocate again in the same slot, deliver a delayed result addressed to the old generation; assert it is discarded with a logged generation mismatch (same mechanism as 02.3, now for GPU handles with device generation).
- Native-context ownership: create an exact-GL renderer (04.3) and a new-backend device; assert resources are tracked in separate groups and that an attempted cross-use is reported, with the only supported path being a real copy (deferred to F3D-17.4).

## Success criteria

- Seven named tests pass; each has a mutation variant proving detection; they run in the forced-new-backend lane and in benchmark mode.

## Test plan

- Unit: none new (integrated suite).
- E2E: seven named tests in `tests/e2e/counterexamples/` on Chrome and Safari, each with a mutation variant (`--wrong-impl`) that must fail; wired into the forced-new-backend lane and benchmark mode (never skipped).
- Logging: each test logs observed pixel values/versions/generations and the expected ones, tagged `owner: new-backend` (GPU cases) or `owner: exact-backend` (native-context case); archived under `evidence/05.7/`.
- Failure artifacts: target readbacks as images, the packet dump for the failing submission.

## Considerations

- These tests are part of the measured optimized path (§14.8): later beads must not add a "benchmark mode" that skips them.
acceptance_criteria: Named regression tests exist and pass on Safari and Chrome for each counterexample; each test demonstrably fails when its guard is disabled (mutation check); the tests are wired into the forced-new-backend lane and are never disabled in benchmark mode.

title: F3D-06: Packed transforms with complete public state/materialization
description:
## What this epic delivers

The CPU side of the execution core: fixed-size math with JavaScript numeric semantics, packed scene state with dirty propagation, a versioned dependency graph, synchronous materialization of public state, a BVH for synchronous queries, and attribute upload histories. Plan §19 F3D-06 depends on 05; acceptance: "Matrices/attributes, synchronous queries, clone/serialize/export after updates". Blocked by kill gate 1 because the plan forbids building the engine before real browser execution is proven.

## Why (plan §5.2, §5.4, §5.8, §5.10, §6.2, §7.1–7.7)

Data layout matters more than elegant notation: separate hot numeric arrays from cold names/user data/handlers; use SoA or small AoSoA blocks; preserve stable public identity through handles. Transform correctness: special-case rigid/uniform-scale only after proving conditions; hierarchies produce shear; negative scale flips orientation; never normalize user-authored transforms. Public observations are semantic: `AnimationMixer.update()`, explicit matrix updates, ray queries and callbacks can synchronously observe results before `renderer.render()`.

## Children

1. `f3d-math`: fixed-size types, f64 public semantics, JS numeric lowering, transcendental differential tests, scalar + simd128 with measured crossover.
2. `f3d-scene` packed transforms: hierarchy order, dirty roots, intervals, reparenting, manual flags, proven fast paths.
3. Semantic dependency graph and versioning.
4. Public state materialization and identity preservation.
5. BVH and the synchronous raycast contract.
6. Attribute CPU/upload/GPU-visible histories.
7. Adversarial and property tests for math and scene.

## Success criteria for the epic

All children closed; both crates ship `CONTRACT.md`; line counts reported against 12,000 (math) and 25,000 (scene).

## No-claim boundary

Packed state is a private representation. It changes no public contract, and this epic claims no speedup.
acceptance_criteria: f3d-math and f3d-scene provide packed, versioned scene state whose public observations (matrices, attributes, Euler/quaternion relationship, synchronous queries, clone/serialize/export) match pinned upstream after packed updates; the attribute CPU/upload/GPU-visible histories follow r186 WebGLAttributes semantics; adversarial and property tests pass.

title: f3d-math: fixed-size types, f64 public semantics, JS numeric lowering, simd128 with crossover
description:
## Full scope

f3d-math crate: fixed-size vector/quaternion/matrix/affine types with f64 public semantics, explicit JavaScript numeric lowering, transcendental differential tests against the browser, scalar reference plus simd128 batches with measured crossover

## Summary

The numerical foundation with the plan's numeric-fidelity rules built in.

## Background (plan §5.4, §7.1, §7.3, §7.5, §23 [S47]; AGENTS.md "Numeric fidelity")

- "Use `f64` or retained JavaScript for observable scalar operations; convert to GPU representations at the same admitted boundaries as the reference. Preserve signed zero, exceptional values, operation ordering where observable, and relevant rounding behavior. JavaScript integer coercions, shift counts, remainder, and `Math.min`/`Math.max` behavior need explicit lowering; Rust casts and similarly named arithmetic methods are not substitutes."
- "Transcendental functions require differential testing: sharing an `f64` type alone does not prove agreement with a browser's math implementation."
- Representations: quaternion for local rotation (unit fast path only when established); TRS for local transforms; packed 3×4 affine for world; 4×4 for projection; correct inverse-transpose for normals.
- "Use safe portable SIMD on the pinned nightly where its Wasm code generation is favorable, and keep a scalar reference. Inspect the emitted `simd128` code and benchmark it in the actual target browsers."

## Technical approach

- Types mirror Three.js public math semantics one-to-one (method names may differ; behavior must not): `Matrix4.compose/decompose`, `Euler.setFromQuaternion` for every order, `Quaternion.slerp`, `Matrix3.getNormalMatrix`, `Box3`, `Sphere`, `Ray`, `Plane`, `Triangle`, `Color` with color management hooks.
- A `jsnum` module: `to_int32`, `to_uint32`, `js_rem`, `js_shift`, `js_min`, `js_max`, `js_round` etc., each with spec-cited tests.
- Differential harness: a browser page computes `Math.sin/cos/tan/atan2/pow/exp/log` over a fixed input set (including edge values) and exports results; Rust tests compare bit patterns and document any differences; where the browser differs from Rust's libm, either match via the browser (retained JS for that op) or record the tolerance per op.
- Batch kernels (transform compose, matrix multiply, normal matrix, bounds transform) with `#[cfg(target_feature = "simd128")]` variants and scalar defaults; a benchmark page measures crossover per browser; emitted Wasm inspected once and noted.

## Success criteria

- Upstream math unit tests (routed through F3D-18a when ready) pass for retained JS; for the Rust kernels, a differential test suite against `three` math over random and edge inputs passes bit-for-bit for non-transcendental ops and within documented tolerance for transcendental ones.
- Crossover numbers recorded per browser.
- `f3d-math/CONTRACT.md` is written before any other crate depends on `f3d-math` (AGENTS.md "Documentation and Contracts"): purpose and position in the dependency direction, public types and semantics, invariants, implementation ownership route, error model, determinism and numeric-fidelity class, cancellation behavior, unsafe boundary if any, feature flags, conformance tests, and no-claim boundaries.

## Test plan

- Unit: per-type differential tests against pinned `three` math (run in Node, exported vectors as fixtures) over random and edge inputs (signed zero, NaN, Infinity, denormals, extreme magnitudes) asserting bit-identical results for non-transcendental ops; `jsnum` spec-cited tests (`ToInt32`, shift masks, `%` sign rules, `Math.min/max` with NaN and -0); simd128-vs-scalar equality property tests.
- E2E: browser differential page `tests/e2e/math/transcendentals.mjs` on Chrome and Safari computing `sin/cos/tan/atan2/pow/exp/log` over the fixed input set; results compared bit-for-bit against the Rust build and any difference recorded per op with the chosen policy (retained JS or documented tolerance); crossover benchmark page records scalar vs SIMD timings per batch size.
- Logging: mismatch tables `{op, input, browser_bits, rust_bits, ulp}` at `error`; crossover `metric` events `{kernel, n, scalar_ms, simd_ms}`; archived under `evidence/06.1/<browser>/`.
- Failure artifacts: the mismatch table and the emitted Wasm disassembly excerpt for the affected kernel.

## Considerations

- Dual-quaternion skinning is a separate opt-in path (§7.2); not here.
- Do not canonicalize or repair pathological inputs in the default path (§7.4).
acceptance_criteria: f3d-math provides Vec2/3/4, Quat, Euler (all orders), Mat3/Mat4, Affine3x4 (AffineRows-compatible), Color and bounds/ray/plane/triangle primitives with f64 public-facing semantics; JS Number behaviors (signed zero, NaN/Infinity propagation, ToInt32 coercions, shift counts, remainder, Math.min/max NaN and -0 rules) are implemented explicitly and tested; transcendental results are differentially tested against browser Math on the target browsers; a scalar reference exists for every simd128 batch kernel with the crossover size measured in the actual browsers.

title: f3d-scene packed transforms: hierarchy order, dirty roots, intervals, proven fast paths
description:
## Full scope

f3d-scene packed transforms: SoA/AoSoA hot arrays with cold data separated, stable parent-before-child order, dirty roots and compact affected intervals, reparenting invalidation, manual-update flags honored, rigid/uniform-scale fast paths only after proven preconditions

## Summary

The packed scene representation behind the public objects, built to preserve every observable upstream transform behavior.

## Background (plan §5.2, §7.3, §7.4; §6.2)

- "Avoid recursively recomputing the whole tree each frame. Maintain a stable parent-before-child order, dirty roots, and compact affected intervals where the topology permits them. Reparenting invalidates the relevant topology segment. Public manual-update flags continue to control when updates are observable."
- "Special-case rigid and uniform-scale transforms only after proving the necessary conditions. A hierarchy can produce shear even when individual nodes are authored as TRS. Negative scale changes orientation; singular transforms require explicit reference-compatible behavior."
- "Do not normalize, repair, or canonicalize user-authored transforms merely to make optimization easier."
- Preserve `position`, `quaternion`, `rotation`, `scale`, matrix update flags, layers, visibility, render ordering per pinned upstream; preserve the observable Euler/quaternion relationship (which is materialization, 06.4).

## Technical approach

- Arenas (05.1) for nodes: `local_trs`, `local_matrix`, `world_matrix` (Affine3x4 plus a full 4×4 slot when non-affine), flags (`matrix_auto_update`, `matrix_world_needs_update`, `visible`, `layers`, `frustum_culled`, `render_order`), parent/children indices; cold data (name, userData, callbacks) stays on the JS object.
- Order maintenance: an array of node indices in DFS order with subtree extents; insert/remove/reparent update extents incrementally (or rebuild the affected subtree range).
- Propagation: `update_world_matrices(dirty_roots)` processes intervals, respecting upstream's `updateMatrixWorld(force)` semantics: a parent update forces children; `matrixWorldAutoUpdate=false` nodes are skipped exactly as upstream.
- Fast-path admission: per subtree, track "all descendants rigid/uniform-scale" bits maintained on write; fall back to general affine when unknown.
- Versioning hooks: each node's local/world version increments on write/propagate (feeds 06.3).

## Success criteria

- Differential tests against upstream `Object3D.updateMatrixWorld` on random hierarchies with random reparenting, negative scales, shear-producing trees, `matrixAutoUpdate=false` nodes and singular scales: bit-identical world matrices (f64).
- Interval propagation touches only dirty subtrees (assert via counters).
- `f3d-scene/CONTRACT.md` is written before any other crate depends on `f3d-scene` (AGENTS.md "Documentation and Contracts"): purpose and position in the dependency direction, public types and semantics, invariants, implementation ownership route, error model, determinism and numeric-fidelity class, cancellation behavior, unsafe boundary if any, feature flags, conformance tests, and no-claim boundaries.

## Test plan

- Unit: property tests over random hierarchies and operation sequences (set TRS, reparent, toggle `matrixAutoUpdate`, negative/zero/non-uniform scale, deep shear-producing trees) comparing world matrices bit-for-bit (f64) with a Node oracle running pinned `Object3D.updateMatrixWorld`; interval-propagation counter tests (nodes visited == dirty subtree size).
- E2E: `tests/e2e/scene/hierarchy.mjs` drives H1/H3 scene graphs through scripted edits in the browser and compares `matrixWorld` observations at checkpoints with upstream.
- Logging: per-propagation `metric` events `{dirty_roots, nodes_visited, total_nodes, intervals}`; first mismatch logged with node path, expected and actual elements; archived under `evidence/06.2/`.
- Failure artifacts: the minimized hierarchy and op sequence (property-test shrink output).

## Considerations

- Public identity is preserved through handles; public objects are not the storage layout (§7.3).
acceptance_criteria: f3d-scene stores local TRS, local/world matrices and flags in packed arrays keyed by handles; world-matrix propagation walks a maintained parent-before-child order updating only dirty intervals; reparenting invalidates the affected topology segment; matrixAutoUpdate/matrixWorldNeedsUpdate semantics match upstream observably; negative scale, shear from hierarchy and singular matrices produce upstream-identical results; fast paths are guarded by proven per-subtree conditions.

title: Semantic dependency graph and versioning by category
description:
## Full scope

Semantic dependency graph and versioning: separate dependency categories, per-dependency versions, consumed-version records, generation counters and dirty bitsets, precomputed dependency closures for common update classes

## Summary

Make "removing a question from the frame loop" concrete: the compiled program knows exactly what depends on what, with cheap versions instead of rediscovery.

## Background (plan §4.10, §6.2)

"Represent dependency categories separately... A color change should not invalidate a mesh's world transform. A camera change should not cause a static geometry upload. A texture content update should not require recompiling its sampling code when type/layout are unchanged. Each dependency has a version. A derived result records the versions it consumed. Recompute only when one changes. Use compact generation counters and dirty bitsets; avoid cryptographic hashing of live state every frame. The compiler may precompute the affected dependency closure for common update classes. Dynamic insertion, removal, reparenting, and resource-layout changes rebuild only the affected structural plan."

## Technical approach

- `f3d-scene::deps`: a `DependencyKind` enum with the listed categories; per-entity per-kind `DataVersion` (05.5); a `DirtySet` per kind implemented as a bitset over arena indices; write paths bump versions and set bits.
- Derived results (world matrix, bounds, packed uniform blocks, draw buckets) store `ConsumedVersions` and a `derive()` that checks before recomputing.
- Precomputed closures: for update classes the compiler recognizes (many transforms from time; material color sweep; camera orbit), a static table of "which derived results are affected" so the frame path only clears those bits.
- Structural changes (insert/remove/reparent/layout change) route through a `StructuralEvent` that marks plan segments for rebuild (consumed by F3D-07/08).

## Success criteria

- Tests assert the three non-invalidation examples from the plan; property tests assert derived results are recomputed iff a consumed version changed.
- Frame-path cost is O(dirty), with counters proving no full scans on quiet frames.

## Test plan

- Unit: tests for the three non-invalidation examples (color change leaves world transform untouched; camera change triggers no geometry upload; texture content update triggers no program rebuild); property tests asserting derived results recompute iff a consumed version changed; quiet-frame test on a 10k-object synthetic scene proving O(dirty) work via counters.
- E2E: `tests/e2e/scene/dirty-tracking.mjs` on H1 static mode: telemetry shows zero derived recomputation on quiet frames and exactly the expected recomputation on scripted edits.
- Logging: per-frame debug dump of dirty bits per kind `{kind, dirty_count}` and derived-result recomputation counts; archived under `evidence/06.3/`.
- Failure artifacts: the dependency graph excerpt for the wrongly recomputed or stale result.

## Considerations

- Versions are compact integers; never hashes of content.
- Attribute upload versions (06.6) are a distinct history from CPU content versions.
acceptance_criteria: Dependency categories (local/world transform, geometry content, geometry bounds, material program identity, material uniform values, texture content, light parameters, shadow inputs, camera state, render-target topology) have independent versions; derived results record consumed versions and recompute only when one changes; a color change does not invalidate a world transform, a camera change does not trigger a geometry upload, and a texture content update does not recompile sampling code; no per-frame cryptographic hashing of live state.

title: Public state materialization and identity preservation after packed updates
description:
## Full scope

Public state materialization and identity preservation: synchronous reads after packed updates, Euler/quaternion relationship, stable nested references, clone/toJSON/serialize/export after optimized updates, callbacks that mutate during render followed by world-matrix reads

## Summary

Packed state must never leak as a behavior change. This bead defines how the JS-visible objects and the packed replicas stay observably identical.

## Background (plan §4.5, §5.2, §5.3, §5.10, §5.13, §6.3)

- "Reconstruction of observable objects is permitted at a declared materialization boundary, but must preserve stable identity and existing references. Replacing a referenced `Vector3` with a newly allocated lookalike is not equivalent."
- "Preserve the observable relationship between Euler rotation and quaternion changes, not just the final orientation in one frame." "Tests must include callbacks that mutate scene state during rendering and subsequent reads of world matrices."
- "Finish or materialize the results at those original boundaries. Do not defer an observable animation update until a convenient frame commit."
- "Export must work after an accelerated update... Never export the initial captured scene while the user sees a newer scene."

## Technical approach

- Define the **materialization boundary** contract: for Wasm-owned regions, public objects expose current values via the generated bindings; the chosen mechanism must not replace public data properties with accessors where descriptors/enumeration/external references can observe the difference (§4.8). Where accessor conversion is unobservable for a given class (proven per class from the upstream source: for example `Object3D.position` is defined via `Object.defineProperties` with non-writable/non-configurable descriptors in upstream, which constrains what may change), the compiler records the proof; otherwise the region is JavaScript-owned with epoch publication.
- Euler/quaternion: upstream's `Euler._onChange`/`Quaternion._onChange` callbacks keep the two in sync; the packed path must invoke the same ordering (write to one updates the other synchronously) and preserve `Euler.order`.
- `matrix`/`matrixWorld` `.elements` arrays keep identity; packed updates write into the existing `Float64Array`/`Array` at the boundary (or the public array is the storage when the ownership mode is JS).
- Callback tests: `onBeforeRender` mutates `position`; subsequent `updateMatrixWorld` observation in the same frame; compare traces with upstream.
- Export hook: exporters read through the public objects; a pre-export materialization ensures Wasm-owned data is published (feeds F3D-19.4).

## Success criteria

- Differential traces vs upstream for the enumerated scenarios on H1/H2 objects.
- Identity assertions (`===`) on nested references across 1,000 updates.

## Test plan

- Unit: identity tests (`===` on nested references across 1,000 updates); Euler/quaternion write-ordering property tests vs upstream; descriptor/enumeration tests (`Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor`, `Object.keys`, `JSON.stringify`) equal to upstream for every recognized class; per-class proof records checked in for any accessor conversion.
- E2E: `tests/e2e/scene/materialization.mjs` on H1/H2 objects: `onBeforeRender` mutates state and a later `matrixWorld` read observes it; `clone()`/`toJSON()`/exporter reads after packed updates equal upstream; run on both browsers.
- Logging: materialization counts per frame as `metric` events (they are a cost in the report); mismatches logged with property path, expected and actual values; archived under `evidence/06.4/`.
- Failure artifacts: serialized object snapshots from both sides.

## Considerations

- Small or frequently observed islands should remain JavaScript when crossing/packing costs dominate (§4.8); this bead's counters feed that decision.
acceptance_criteria: Any public read of position/quaternion/rotation/scale/matrix/matrixWorld/attributes after a packed update returns the upstream-identical value synchronously; object.position and nested references keep their JavaScript identity across updates; clone, copy, toJSON and exporter reads observe current state; the Euler-vs-quaternion write ordering behavior matches upstream; a render callback that mutates scene state followed by a world-matrix read observes the mutation as upstream does.

title: Graphics BVH and the synchronous raycast contract
description:
## Full scope

Graphics BVH and the synchronous raycast contract: robust CPU builder and traversal, refit and measured rebuild heuristic, stable tie-breaking and upstream hit ordering, custom raycast overrides, face/instance identities, conservative bounds for deformed meshes

## Summary

Spatial queries with the plan's picking semantics intact.

## Background (plan §5.10, §7.1, §7.6)

- "Retain synchronous raycasting on CPU-authoritative state. GPU picking may be an additional async API or a proven internal strategy, not a Promise substituted for a synchronous `Raycaster` result. A BVH must preserve custom `raycast` overrides, source traversal/tie ordering, and face/instance identities. Canonical triangle IDs stay separate from any private reordered acceleration structure."
- "A statistical or heuristic culling decision may choose a conservative bound, but must not discard potentially visible geometry. Deformed meshes need conservative bounds or correct refits. Objects outside the main camera frustum may still contribute to shadows, reflections, transmission, or other passes."

## Technical approach

- `f3d-scene::bvh`: binned SAH builder over object bounds (scene level) and optionally per-mesh triangle BVH for large geometries; refit path for transform-only changes; a measured rebuild heuristic (quality degradation threshold) recorded from benchmarks.
- Ray query returns candidates; the actual intersection uses the object's `raycast` (retained JS when overridden, or the Rust equivalent of upstream `Mesh.raycast` when the class is unmodified and recognized), then results are sorted with upstream's comparator including its tie behavior (stable by distance; upstream sorts by `distance` with `ascSort`).
- Identity: hits carry `faceIndex`, `instanceId`, `object` (the JS object handle), `uv`, `normal` as upstream; triangle IDs map through a canonical table if any private reordering exists.
- Culling: frustum culling honors `frustumCulled` and `layers`; shadow/reflection passes use their own frusta (feeds F3D-08/14).

## Success criteria

- Differential tests against upstream `Raycaster.intersectObjects` over random scenes including coincident hits, negative scale, instanced meshes, skinned meshes (with `boundingBox` semantics) and subclass overrides: identical result lists.
- Culling test: no object visible in upstream's render list is culled by the BVH.

## Test plan

- Unit: property tests comparing `intersectObjects` results (order, distances, `faceIndex`, `instanceId`, `uv`, `normal`) with a Node oracle over random scenes including coincident hits, negative scale, instanced meshes, skinned meshes and subclass `raycast` overrides; refit/rebuild heuristic tests; culling test asserting no object in upstream's render list is culled.
- E2E: `tests/e2e/scene/picking.mjs` adds a synthetic picking script to H1 and runs `webgl_interactive_*`-style examples on both browsers, comparing hit lists at logical frames.
- Logging: BVH build/refit `metric` events `{nodes, depth, build_ms, refit_ms, rebuild_reason}`; hit-list diffs logged with the ray and both lists; archived under `evidence/06.5/`.
- Failure artifacts: the minimized scene and ray from the property-test shrink.

## Considerations

- GPU culling is a later optional strategy (F3D-20.6), not a different visibility contract.
acceptance_criteria: A CPU BVH supports frustum culling and ray queries with reference-compatible hit ordering and tie-breaking; Raycaster results remain synchronous on CPU-authoritative state; custom raycast overrides on subclasses are honored; face/instance identities and canonical triangle IDs are preserved independent of any private reordering; deformed meshes use conservative bounds or correct refits; culling never discards potentially visible geometry.

title: Attribute histories: CPU version, upload requests (r186 semantics), GPU-visible shadow
description:
## Full scope

Attribute histories: public CPU content version, source upload-request version and effective update ranges matching r186 WebGLAttributes, last GPU-visible shadow per renderer replica, gap fill from shadow or proven-equal or smaller writes, sub-word padding rule, onUpload callback ordering

## Summary

Implement the plan's "CPU mutation and GPU-visible mutation are different histories" rule as the single attribute-upload authority.

## Background (plan §5.8, §23 [S41]; AGENTS.md "CPU mutation and GPU-visible mutation are different histories")

- "An attribute may have changed in a CPU array while the source deliberately has not requested a GPU upload. Keep the public CPU content version, the source's upload-request/version/range behavior, and the last GPU-visible content separate. Preserve the pinned renderer's effective upload ranges, mutations to those ranges, and `onUpload` callback ordering. The r186 WebGL attribute implementation explicitly tracks versions and performs its own range coalescing; do not substitute an idealized upload model."
- "Coalescing new uploads across gaps must not expose additional CPU edits that the reference would leave GPU-stale. Fill such gaps from the last GPU-visible shadow, prove the bytes equal, or keep the smaller writes. The same rule applies to padding a sub-word update to WebGPU's alignment. A scan detecting a CPU mutation is not permission to upload it early."
- "Track these histories per device/renderer replica when a resource is shared across views or renderer instances."

## Technical approach

- Read the pinned `WebGLAttributes.js` (and the WebGPU backend's attribute utilities) and transcribe its version/`updateRanges`/`clearUpdateRanges` semantics into a spec table in the bead's test file.
- `f3d-scene::attributes`: per attribute: `cpu_version` (bumped by any write barrier or scan), `upload_request` (mirrors `needsUpdate`/`version`/`addUpdateRange` exactly), per-replica `gpu_visible: { version, shadow: Option<Vec<u8>> }`.
- Upload planner: from `upload_request` compute effective ranges per upstream's coalescing rule; for WebGPU 4-byte alignment or when merging adjacent ranges, fill the gap bytes from the shadow (if kept) or verify equality with the current CPU bytes; if neither, emit separate writes. Shadow retention policy is per attribute (size-bounded; report bytes).
- `onUpload` ordering: fire after the replica's upload in the same order upstream does.
- Replica tracking: attributes used by an exact-GL renderer and a new-backend renderer have separate histories and separate GPU allocations (§5.9).

## Success criteria

- Differential tests against upstream: sequences of partial updates with gaps, `needsUpdate` toggles without CPU changes, CPU changes without `needsUpdate`, interleaved buffers, resizes (new array identity), draw-range changes; the GPU-visible bytes on the candidate equal upstream's at every checkpoint.
- Sub-word padding test: a 1-float update at an unaligned offset does not expose neighboring stale CPU edits.

## Test plan

- Unit: planner tests transcribed from the pinned `WebGLAttributes.js` semantics (version bump without `needsUpdate` → no upload; `addUpdateRange` sequences with gaps; `clearUpdateRanges`; resize with new array identity); property tests over random write/request sequences asserting GPU-visible bytes equal the oracle's at every checkpoint; sub-word padding test (a 1-float write at an unaligned offset never exposes neighboring stale CPU edits); per-replica independence test.
- E2E: `tests/e2e/attributes/histories.mjs` uploads through the bridge and reads back on Chrome and Safari for interleaved buffers, instanced attributes and draw-range changes.
- Logging: per-upload range list `{attribute, request_ranges, effective_ranges, fill_source: request|shadow|split, bytes}` in debug; mismatch logs with the first differing byte offset; archived under `evidence/06.6/`.
- Failure artifacts: hex dumps of expected vs actual GPU-visible ranges.

## Considerations

- Shared CPU attributes may require independent GPU allocations when disposal/update lifetimes diverge (§5.9).
acceptance_criteria: For every BufferAttribute/InterleavedBuffer/InstancedBufferAttribute the three histories are tracked separately per device/renderer replica; coalescing never uploads CPU edits the reference would leave GPU-stale; sub-word updates padded to WebGPU alignment are filled from the GPU-visible shadow or split; onUpload callbacks fire in upstream order; array identity, interleaving, normalized/integer interpretation, draw ranges and resize behavior are preserved.

title: Adversarial and property tests for math and scene state
description:
## Full scope

Adversarial and property tests for math and scene state: aliasing, typed-array writes, subclass overrides, reflective access, needsUpdate, empty data, negative scale, shear, singular matrices, degenerate triangles, ray-hit ties, extreme coordinates, NaN/Infinity, integer overflow boundaries

## Summary

The plan's §14.7 adversarial program for the CPU core, written now so later optimizer beads inherit it.

## Background (plan §14.7, §5.2, §7.4; AGENTS.md "Adversarial and property tests")

"Aliasing, typed-array writes, subclass overrides, reflective access, `needsUpdate`, callbacks that reenter rendering, mutable material keys, matrix-read materialization, deoptimization after an assumption changes. Geometry/math: empty data, negative scale, shear, singular matrices, degenerate triangles, ray-hit ties, extreme coordinates, NaNs, infinities, integer overflow boundaries."

## Technical approach

- Test scaffolding in `f3d-conformance` (or the scene crate's tests) that runs the same scenario twice: once through pinned upstream (Node with `three`), once through the candidate facade, then diffs traces.
- Scenarios: alias a `position` vector and write through the alias; write into `attribute.array` directly then toggle `needsUpdate` (and not); subclass `Mesh` overriding `updateMatrixWorld`/`raycast`; `Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor`/`Object.keys`/`JSON.stringify` on public objects; `Reflect.set`; empty geometries; scale `-1`; parent scaled non-uniformly with rotated child (shear); zero scale (singular) then `matrixWorld` inverse use in raycast; degenerate triangles; two coincident hits; coordinates near 1e308 and 1e-308; NaN/Infinity in transforms; `Uint32`/`Int32` attribute overflow cases.
- Property generators for operation sequences over hierarchies and attributes.

## Success criteria

- All scenarios match upstream byte-for-byte (f64) or per the documented transcendental tolerance.
- The suite runs in the functional lane and in the forced-new-backend lane where rendering is involved (later).

## Test plan

- Unit: the adversarial suite itself (aliasing, typed-array writes, subclass overrides, reflective access, `needsUpdate`, empty data, negative scale, shear, singular matrices, degenerate triangles, ray-hit ties, extreme coordinates, NaN/Infinity, integer overflow) run against retained JS and the packed path with a Node oracle; property generators for random op sequences.
- E2E: the same scenarios executed in the browser (`tests/e2e/scene/adversarial.mjs`) in the functional lane and, once rendering exists, in the forced-new-backend lane; never skipped in benchmark mode.
- Logging: each scenario logs the first divergence with the operation index, property path and both values; archived under `evidence/06.7/`.
- Failure artifacts: the shrunk op sequence.

## Considerations

- Deoptimization-after-assumption-change cases are added by F3D-12a/12b as guards exist; the harness must make that easy.
acceptance_criteria: A named adversarial suite exercises every listed case against both retained JS and the packed path with identical observable results as upstream; property tests generate random operation sequences with reference comparison; the suite is part of the functional lane and never skipped in benchmark mode.

title: F3D-07: Initial accurate new WebGPU material/render slice (H1 toon/Inspector and H2 starting materials, no retained renderer submission)
description:
## What this epic delivers

The first real frames from the **new** backend. Plan §19 F3D-07 depends on 05 and 15 (early slice); acceptance: "Complete H1 toon/Inspector and H2 starting materials, no retained renderer submission". F3D-15's early shader work and this epic form "one early vertical slice rather than a circular demand for finished subsystems".

## Why (plan §2.7, §3.3, §6.3, §8.1, §8.5, §9.2, §9.3, §11.7, §16.7)

"H1 uses `MeshToonNodeMaterial` and the Inspector... H2 starts with an environment-lit Standard material and exposes Lambert, Phong, texture/color, and four legacy `ShaderMaterial` choices. A basic unlit renderer cannot preserve those demonstrations and all their application controls." The corrected sequence brings the node/material slice, environment handling and the finite ESSL corpus into the first product gate. "Prevent a compatibility-only wrapper from masquerading as this project": scored workloads execute entirely through the new backend, with a call-path check.

## Children

1. `f3d-gpu` device/resource layer.
2. `f3d-graph` initial pass graph with usage-scope hazards and canvas rules.
3. Built-in material slice for H1/H2 with color management and environment/PMREM.
4. Source-ordered snapshot execution protocol.
5. H1 TSL/node construction path, NodeFrame update frequencies, Inspector hooks.
6. Forced new-backend call-path assertion and ownership assertions.
7. Explicit cost accounting instrumentation.
8. Camera/projection/output conventions.

## Success criteria for the epic

All children closed; H1 (WebGPU setting) and H2 (default + non-legacy materials) render through the new backend in the forced-new-backend lane with equivalence checkpoints passing; `CONTRACT.md` for `f3d-gpu`, `f3d-graph` and the first `f3d-shader` surface written.

## No-claim boundary

Correct frames, not fast frames. Performance is scored only in F3D-11 with the frozen protocol.
acceptance_criteria: The new WebGPU backend renders H1's MeshToonNodeMaterial scene with Inspector hooks and H2's starting materials (environment-lit Standard, Lambert, Phong, texture/color) with source-ordered per-use snapshots, through f3d-gpu/f3d-graph/f3d-shader, with a call-path assertion that no retained renderer submission occurred; outputs match upstream within preregistered tolerances on Safari and Chrome.

title: f3d-gpu device/resource layer: generations, staging rings, budgets, async validation
description:
## Full scope

f3d-gpu device/resource layer: negotiated device profile, generation-tagged resources with explicit lifecycle states, bounded staging rings and frames-in-flight backpressure, pipeline/variant caches with byte and count budgets, asynchronous validation and uncaptured-error collection, device-loss classification hooks

## Summary

The resource half of the new backend, with the plan's lifetime rules built in from the first line.

## Background (plan §6.5, §11.4, §11.5, §11.7, §12.2, §12.5)

- "Maintain bounded staging rings and a configurable small number of frames in flight. Exhaustion creates backpressure, not unbounded allocation. Pipeline variants, transient resources, and asset caches have explicit byte/count budgets and eviction policies."
- "Pending, not-yet-submitted commands must not reference a destroyed or recycled resource." "An in-flight use can outlive that residency's public release event."
- "A failed compilation must not become a published valid cache entry. Scope memory budgets conservatively because out-of-memory handling is not a dependable capacity-discovery algorithm."
- "Treat CPU/Wasm memory, upload staging, and GPU allocations as distinct budgets even on unified-memory hardware."

## Technical approach

- Resource arenas per kind (buffer, texture, sampler, bind group layout/bind group, pipeline, bundle) using `GpuHandle` with device generation; state enum per entry; retirement queue keyed by submission epoch (consumed by F3D-22a.5).
- Staging: N-frame ring of upload buffers sized by budget; `writeBuffer` path (synchronous copy semantics, source released immediately) vs staging-buffer + encoded copy path (mapped lifetime distinct); credit accounting.
- Caches: pipeline variant cache keyed by shader hash + layout + render-state key, with byte/count budget and LRU eviction; transient texture pool (used by F3D-17.2) with usage/format compatibility keys.
- Validation: pipeline creation via `createRenderPipelineAsync`/`createComputePipelineAsync` where available, results recorded per generation; error-scope helper from 05.6; `uncapturederror` and `lost` events feed structured diagnostics with generation tags.
- Device-loss hook: on loss, mark the generation dead; all handles of that generation fail decode; recovery policy is F3D-22a.3's responsibility.

## Success criteria

- Unit tests for lifecycle transitions and budget backpressure; browser tests for async pipeline failure not being cached and for uncaptured-error routing.
- Memory report shows the three budgets separately.
- `f3d-gpu/CONTRACT.md` is written before any other crate depends on `f3d-gpu` (AGENTS.md "Documentation and Contracts"): purpose and position in the dependency direction, public types and semantics, invariants, implementation ownership route, error model, determinism and numeric-fidelity class, cancellation behavior, unsafe boundary if any, feature flags, conformance tests, and no-claim boundaries.

## Test plan

- Unit: lifecycle-state transition tests (CPU-exists → GPU-allocated → initialized → submitted → retired) including illegal transitions; staging-ring backpressure test (exhaustion blocks, never allocates); cache budget/eviction tests; property tests on the retirement queue vs handle generations.
- E2E: `tests/e2e/gpu/resources.mjs` on Chrome and Safari: async pipeline failure is not cached; `uncapturederror` routes to a structured event with the right generation; device-loss hook marks the generation dead and all its handles fail decode.
- Logging: bounded structured events for allocation, retirement, eviction and validation failure `{kind, handle, generation, bytes, reason}`; per-frame memory `metric` events for the three budgets; archived under `evidence/07.1/`.
- Failure artifacts: the resource arena dump at the failing transition.

## Considerations

- No `wgpu` stack; the browser supplies platform translation (§8.1). This crate talks to the ABI/bridge, not to Metal.
acceptance_criteria: f3d-gpu owns GPU resource creation/retirement behind generation-checked handles with states (CPU-exists, GPU-allocated, initialized, submitted-in-use, retired); staging rings and a configurable frames-in-flight limit produce backpressure rather than unbounded allocation; pipeline variants, transient resources and asset caches have explicit budgets and eviction; async validation results and uncaptured errors are collected per generation; a failed pipeline compilation never becomes a valid cache entry; device-loss events transition every resource of that generation.

title: f3d-graph initial pass graph with usage-scope hazards and canvas rules
description:
## Full scope

f3d-graph initial pass graph: resource reads/writes, explicit attachment load/store/clear/resolve, required order and history dependencies, usage-scope hazard tracking over subresource ranges (whole-buffer rule, per-draw writable alias rule), pass splitting, canvas-texture acquisition per render interval, per-canvas output epochs

## Summary

The middle representation of §6.1 ("pass graph") at its initial scope, with hazards defined by API usage scopes rather than intuition.

## Background (plan §6.1, §8.5 "Resource hazards are defined by API usage scopes", "Canvas, media, and projection state", §23 [S48], [S51])

- "Track resource versions and overlapping mip/layer/aspect ranges, not only texture names. For usage-scope validation a buffer is a whole subresource: assigning disjoint byte ranges incompatible roles does not make the shared buffer legal... A render pass has a usage scope whose restrictions can forbid an attachment/sampling combination even when a source scheduler places the corresponding draws in a seemingly safe order. A compute dispatch has its own usage-scope rules. Split passes, use a distinct versioned resource, or select another legal plan when necessary. Do not invent explicit native memory barriers that browser WebGPU does not expose."
- "Attachment load/store/clear/resolve operations are explicit dependencies, never inferred solely from whether a later pass samples the image."
- "Acquire the current canvas texture for the actual rendering interval; do not keep its texture/view in a long-lived scene cache... A zero-sized or hidden canvas follows a defined pause/resize policy without creating illegal resources. Multiple canvases/renderer instances have separate output and resource epochs."

## Technical approach

- `f3d-graph`: `Pass { kind: Render|Compute|Copy, reads: [ResourceUse], writes: [ResourceUse], attachments: [AttachmentOp], order_constraints }` with `ResourceUse { handle, version, subresource: {mips, layers, aspect} | WholeBuffer, usage }`.
- Validator implementing the usage-scope rules: per render pass, the set of (resource, subresource) usages must be compatible (read-only combos vs single write); per dispatch (not per pass) for compute; copy commands validated separately. On conflict: automatic pass split or versioned resource duplication with a report line.
- Scheduler: topological order respecting explicit dependencies and history (previous-frame reads); no reordering across observable boundaries (§6.3).
- Canvas: `CanvasOutput` resource kind whose texture handle is valid only inside a frame's "acquire → submit" interval; the graph refuses to store it; resize/reconfigure/device change invalidates the attachment plan; hidden/zero-size policy documented.
- Output: an "execution plan segment" list consumed by the bridge encoder.

## Success criteria

- Unit tests: an illegal same-pass attachment+sample is split; disjoint byte-range trick on one buffer is rejected; compute per-dispatch alias rule enforced; canvas texture caching attempt rejected.
- Browser test: the plan renders H1's simple single-pass scene and a two-target scene correctly.
- `f3d-graph/CONTRACT.md` is written before any other crate depends on `f3d-graph` (AGENTS.md "Documentation and Contracts"): purpose and position in the dependency direction, public types and semantics, invariants, implementation ownership route, error model, determinism and numeric-fidelity class, cancellation behavior, unsafe boundary if any, feature flags, conformance tests, and no-claim boundaries.

## Test plan

- Unit: validator tests (attachment+sample in one pass is split; disjoint byte-range trick on one buffer rejected; compute per-dispatch writable-alias rule; copy validated separately); canvas-texture caching attempt rejected; scheduler tests for explicit dependency ordering; fuzzed pass sets (feeds 05.3's serialized-plan fuzz target).
- E2E: `tests/e2e/graph/basic.mjs` renders a single-pass and a two-target scene through the plan on both browsers and compares to upstream; resize/reconfigure invalidation test; two canvases with separate epochs.
- Logging: plan dump per frame in debug `{pass, kind, reads, writes, attachments, split_reason}`; validation failures at `error` with the conflicting uses; archived under `evidence/07.2/`.
- Failure artifacts: the serialized plan that failed validation.

## Considerations

- A copy cannot be inserted inside a render pass as though it were a draw (§6.7); copies are their own pass kind.
acceptance_criteria: The pass graph represents render/compute passes with typed resource handles, versions and subresource ranges; validation enforces WebGPU usage-scope rules (a buffer is a whole subresource for scope purposes; distinct per-draw restrictions on writable binding aliases; attachment vs sampling conflicts inside one pass) by splitting passes or selecting another legal plan; attachment operations are explicit dependencies; canvas textures are acquired for the actual rendering interval and never cached across frames; multiple canvases/renderers have separate output epochs.

title: Built-in material slice for H1/H2 (Toon node, Standard+PMREM, Lambert, Phong, texture/color)
description:
## Full scope

Built-in material slice for H1/H2: MeshToonNodeMaterial, environment-lit MeshStandardMaterial with PMREM, MeshLambert, MeshPhong, texture/color variants and required depth/normal paths, with pinned lighting equations, color management, tone mapping, premultiplication and output conversion

## Summary

Exactly the material surface the first product gate needs, implemented accurately, not generically.

## Background (plan §2.7, §9.1, §9.2, §9.6, §15.3)

- "Pin the exact upstream material and lighting behavior. Implement Basic, normal/depth/distance, Lambert/Phong/Toon/Matcap, Standard/Physical... in the order the test/dependency census requires." H1 needs Toon (node material); H2 needs environment-lit Standard by default plus Lambert/Phong/texture/color branches (the four legacy `ShaderMaterial` variants come through 15a.2).
- "Match color-space handling, texture interpretation, exposure/tone mapping, premultiplication, environment filtering, normal/tangent conventions, and output conversion. Use controlled reference scenes and material sweeps, including high-contrast and near-degenerate cases."
- "It is not enough to render a visually plausible generic PBR model."

## Technical approach

- `f3d-shader` material semantics: transcribe the pinned upstream shader chunks/node functions for the listed materials (Lambert/Phong BRDFs, Standard's GGX/Schlick/multiscatter as pinned, Toon's gradient step, PMREM sampling and `envMapIntensity`, `LinearSRGB`/`sRGB` conversions, tone-mapping operators in use by H2's default, `outputColorSpace`) into typed shader IR emitted as WGSL through the F3D-15a pipeline (node path for Toon; ESSL/chunk path for the classic materials).
- PMREM generation: retain the upstream `PMREMGenerator` construction logic where it is JS-only cold code, executing its passes through the new backend (this is "retained construction/baking logic" allowed by §5.12 Lights row), with the call-path check confirming submission goes through the new backend.
- Resource binding: material parameter blocks from the layout schema (05.2); textures/samplers per material map slots used by these materials (`map`, `envMap`, `normalMap` if H2 uses them; verify from the source inventory in 01.6).
- Differential tests: reference scenes (sphere/plane sweeps over roughness/metalness/emissive/opacity, environment intensity, tone mapping on/off) rendered by upstream WebGL and WebGPU renderers and by the candidate; compare with color-space-aware metrics from 03.6; diagnostic targets for normals/depth/albedo.

## Success criteria

- H1's toon scene and H2's default/Lambert/Phong/texture/color branches match upstream at all checkpoints in the forced-new-backend lane.
- Sweep tests pass within tolerance; high-contrast/near-degenerate cases included.

## Test plan

- Unit: shader-IR snapshot tests per material (Toon node, Standard with PMREM, Lambert, Phong, texture/color, depth/normal); parameter-block layout tests; color-space conversion unit tests against upstream's `ColorManagement` values.
- E2E: differential sweeps `tests/e2e/materials/h1h2-slice.mjs` on Chrome and Safari: sphere/plane sweeps over roughness/metalness/emissive/opacity/envMapIntensity/tone mapping compared to upstream WebGL and WebGPU renderers with the 03.6 tolerances; diagnostic targets (normal/depth/albedo) compared; H1 toon scene and H2 branches at checkpoints in the forced-new-backend lane.
- Logging: per-sweep-step `metric` events `{material, params, max_err, mean_err, worst_region}`; diagnostic mismatch events name the channel; archived under `evidence/07.3/`.
- Failure artifacts: reference/candidate/diff images per failing step and the diagnostic target images.

## Considerations

- Do not "fuse" or approximate here (§9.6); this is the conservative reference generation path that later optimizations are compared against.
- Full material closure is F3D-14; do not expand scope beyond the H1/H2 inventory.
acceptance_criteria: The listed materials render through the new backend with pinned upstream lighting equations, color-space handling, texture interpretation, exposure/tone mapping, environment filtering (PMREM), normal/tangent conventions and output conversion; controlled reference scenes and parameter sweeps match upstream within preregistered tolerances; diagnostic targets (normal/depth/channel) match.

title: Source-ordered snapshot execution protocol with per-use buffer slices
description:
## Full scope

Source-ordered snapshot execution protocol: per-admitted-operation guard/execute/materialize, render-boundary consumption at proper versions, per-draw and per-pass snapshots of callback mutations using immutable per-use buffer slices, reentrant logical render contexts, submission at observation boundaries, no coalescing of observable operations

## Summary

The execution protocol that makes queue-ordering correctness structural rather than accidental.

## Background (plan §6.3, §6.7, §5.5, §8.2 "Incremental transforms and uploads")

- "There is no new universal application tick that owns the timing of every animation, callback, and render. The compiled program follows the source call/effect order. A browser presentation frame may contain zero, one, or many logical render/compute operations."
- "A material change between two draws requires two draw-visible values even when both commands share one submission. Reentrant rendering uses nested logical render contexts and restores the outer camera, target, viewport/scissor, callback, and resource state at the same boundaries as the reference. It cannot overwrite an outer operation's scratch packet."
- "No optimization coalesces away an observable render, update, clear, read, callback, or history transition."
- Strategies for per-use values: immutable per-use buffer slices with distinct bindings/offsets, source-indexed parameter tables, legal encoded copies between passes, or separate submissions; optional immediates as an admitted strategy, not a portability assumption.

## Technical approach

- `f3d-runtime::frame`: `LogicalRender` context stack; `render(scene, camera, target)` entry performs upstream's ordered steps (matrix world updates unless auto-update disabled, `onBeforeRender` callbacks in upstream order, render list assembly consuming versions from 06.3, uploads from 06.6 at their request versions, node updates via F3D-07.5, draw emission, `onAfterRender`).
- Per-use snapshots: parameter blocks are written into a per-frame ring region with an offset per (draw, version); a bind group with dynamic offset (respecting the device's uniform offset alignment from 05.2) selects the slice; a changed value between draws allocates a new slice, never overwrites.
- Submission boundaries: a submission is issued at each point the source could observe GPU results or at the end of the host turn, whichever the source's contract requires; readbacks and `onSubmittedWorkDone` credits attach to those epochs.
- Reentrancy: nested `render()` from a callback pushes a new context with its own scratch region; outer state restored on pop; assertion that the outer packet is untouched.

## Success criteria

- Red-A/blue-B passes through this protocol (not just the bridge test); nested-render test with distinct cameras/targets; a callback that mutates a material between two draws produces two values.
- Trace equality with upstream for H1/H2 callback ordering.

## Test plan

- Unit: slice allocation tests (a changed value between draws allocates a new slice; alignment honored); context-stack tests (push/pop restores outer state; outer packet untouched); protocol ordering tests with a scripted fake renderer.
- E2E: `tests/e2e/protocol/*.mjs` in the forced-new-backend lane on both browsers: red-A/blue-B through the protocol; nested render with distinct cameras/targets; callback mutating a material between two draws yields two values; H1/H2 callback-order trace equality with upstream.
- Logging: per-frame `metric` events `{slices_allocated, submissions, materializations, contexts_max_depth}`; ordering violations logged with the two conflicting steps; archived under `evidence/07.4/`.
- Failure artifacts: readbacks of the affected targets and the packet dump.

## Considerations

- Loading callbacks observable before the next animation tick cannot be delayed to a frame boundary (§6.3).
- Optional immediates are a later capability-checked strategy (F3D-20.3).
acceptance_criteria: The frame path implements the §6.3 protocol exactly: validate guards, execute source-ordered updates exactly once, materialize state visible at return; at render boundaries consume source-visible state and upload requests at their versions, perform reference-required matrix/node/callback updates in order, snapshot each draw/pass's required data version including callback mutations, refresh only invalidated plan segments, emit legal ordered queue writes/copies and command work, submit at the required boundary; nested render calls restore outer camera/target/viewport/scissor/callback/resource state; a material change between two draws in one submission yields two draw-visible values.

title: H1 TSL/node construction path, NodeFrame update frequencies, Inspector hooks
description:
## Full scope

H1 TSL/node construction path: JavaScript-constructed node graphs translated to typed shader IR, dynamic uniforms retained as data, structural invalidation, NodeFrame update/updateBefore/updateAfter at FRAME/RENDER/OBJECT frequencies with reference identity and the return-false marker rule, reentrant context stack, Inspector hooks

## Summary

The node/TSL entrance at H1's scope, with NodeFrame semantics preserved exactly.

## Background (plan §9.3, §2.7, §5.14 "Editor/Inspector/devtools", §23 [S42])

- "Let ordinary JavaScript construct TSL graphs, then translate recognized nodes into typed shader IR. Retain dynamic uniforms as data; their changes do not by themselves require rebuilding the shader graph. Structural changes invalidate the affected program and pass dependencies. Do not imply that current Three.js necessarily rebuilds every graph each frame."
- "Preserve `updateBefore`, `update`, and `updateAfter` at the source's FRAME, RENDER, or OBJECT frequency, with the correct renderer/camera/material/object/scene/compute context and update-reference identity. The pinned `NodeFrame` also treats a callback returning `false` specially when advancing update markers. A physical batch must not collapse multiple logically distinct updates or advance a marker before a failed update would have done so upstream. Reentrant rendering uses an explicit context stack."
- Inspector: "Rust source maps and generated shader inspection augment rather than replace existing APIs."

## Technical approach

- Retain upstream's TSL construction modules (cold JS) so the application's node objects are real upstream nodes; add a translator that walks the graph (via the node's public `getNodeType`/`generate`-adjacent structure or a recognized node table) into `f3d-shader` IR; unrecognized node → conservative path: use upstream's WGSL node builder output as the shader source (retained shader-construction helper, allowed and charged, §9.3) submitted through the new backend.
- Uniform data path: `UniformNode` values bound to parameter block slots; version bumps only.
- NodeFrame emulation: implement the pinned `NodeFrame` update-marker semantics (`frameId`, `renderId`, per-object markers, `updateBeforeType`/`updateType`/`updateAfterType`, the `false` return rule) in the runtime; call the node's JS callbacks with the same context object shape upstream provides.
- Inspector: keep upstream's Inspector module and its renderer hooks working against the routed renderer object; where the Inspector reads renderer stats, provide the public contract's values (logical counts) and expose F3D physical telemetry only under the separate F3D namespace (§5.7).

## Success criteria

- H1 renders via node translation with per-object toon colors; uniform-change no-rebuild test; structural-change invalidation test; NodeFrame marker tests transcribed from the pinned source (including `false`).
- Inspector opens on H1 and shows the same public fields as upstream.

## Test plan

- Unit: NodeFrame marker state-machine tests transcribed from the pinned source (FRAME/RENDER/OBJECT frequencies, `updateBefore`/`update`/`updateAfter`, the `false` return rule, reference identity); translator snapshot tests for H1's toon graph; uniform-change no-rebuild and structural-change invalidation tests.
- E2E: `tests/e2e/nodes/h1-toon.mjs` in the forced-new-backend lane: H1 renders via translation with per-object colors; scripted uniform sweeps cause zero recompiles; a structural edit invalidates only affected programs; the Inspector opens on H1 and its panels match upstream's public fields.
- Logging: graph translation report `{node, recognized|retained-builder}` in the build report; per-frame node-update `metric` events `{frequency, count}`; archived under `evidence/07.5/`.
- Failure artifacts: IR dump of the failing graph and the Inspector panel snapshot.

## Considerations

- Full node coverage is F3D-16; do not chase it here.
- Never substitute a constant or silently keep an old graph (§9.3).
acceptance_criteria: H1's MeshToonNodeMaterial graphs constructed by ordinary JS are translated to shader IR and WGSL; changing a uniform node's value does not rebuild the graph, a structural change invalidates only affected programs/passes; node update callbacks run at the pinned NodeFrame frequencies with the correct renderer/camera/material/object/scene context and identity, a callback returning false does not advance the marker, and physical batching never collapses logically distinct updates; the upstream Inspector attaches to the routed renderer and its panels populate with truthful data.

title: Forced new-backend call-path assertion and per-test ownership assertions
description:
## Full scope

Forced new-backend call-path assertion and per-test ownership assertions: prove scored and forced-lane rendering never goes through retained renderer submission

## Summary

The mechanism that keeps a compatibility wrapper from masquerading as this project.

## Background (plan §3.3, §5.16, §6.9, §14.1, §14.2, §16.6 "New-backend ownership"; AGENTS.md "Three production-route lanes")

- "The H1–H8 scored workloads execute entirely through that new GPU backend, with a call-path check that rules out retained renderer submission."
- "Every accelerated test asserts that its designated rendering work uses the new backend; every exact-component test asserts that it receives actual native objects and preserves the source's lifecycle."
- "Lane 2 exists specifically to prevent a compatibility-only wrapper from masquerading as this project."

## Technical approach

- Attribution: the bridge/adapter tags each `queue.submit` with the route (`new-backend`, `exact-backend`, `retained-renderer`) and the logical render context; retained upstream renderers are wrapped at their submission entry (WebGL `gl.drawElements`/WebGPU backend `submit`) only for attribution counting in test builds.
- Lane switch: `F3D_FORCE_NEW_BACKEND=1` makes the router refuse retained renderer submission for all portable families (exact-GL contract cases are excluded from that lane by declaration, not by silent skipping).
- Assertion helpers for tests: `expectRoute('new-backend')`, `expectNativeGL(ctx)`.
- Reporting: per-test owner tags flow into the manifest status updater (F3D-18a.5).

## Success criteria

- H1/H2 in the forced lane render with zero retained submissions; deliberately routing a draw through a retained renderer fails the assertion with a stack.

## Test plan

- Unit: attribution counter tests with a fake adapter (each route increments its own counter; the lane switch refuses retained submission with a stack).
- E2E: H1/H2 in the forced-new-backend lane show zero retained submissions; a deliberate retained draw fails `expectRoute('new-backend')` with the offending call path; an exact-lane test asserts `expectNativeGL`.
- Logging: per-frame route counts `{new_backend, exact_backend, retained}` (bounded) and per-test owner tags; archived under `evidence/07.6/`.
- Failure artifacts: the attribution stack for the offending submission.

## Considerations

- Retained cold helpers (construction/baking logic) are allowed and charged; only *submission* is what this asserts.
acceptance_criteria: A runtime attribution mechanism records which route submitted every command buffer; a test-lane switch disables retained renderer submission entirely; every accelerated test asserts its designated rendering went through the new backend and every exact-component test asserts it received actual native objects; an accidental retained submission fails the test with the offending call path.

title: Explicit cost accounting instrumentation in a separate F3D telemetry namespace
description:
## Full scope

Explicit cost accounting instrumentation (debug/performance build): CPU preparation, bridge encoding, upload bytes/calls, binding changes, bundle rebuilds, draw/dispatch counts, pipeline creation, staging memory, GPU timing where supported; removable/bounded in production; separate F3D telemetry namespace

## Summary

Know where every microsecond and byte goes, without perturbing the thing being measured.

## Background (plan §8.8, §5.7, §16.8; AGENTS.md "Output Style")

- "The debug/performance build records CPU preparation, bridge encoding, upload bytes/calls, binding changes, bundle rebuilds, draw/dispatch counts, pipeline creation, staging memory, and GPU timing where supported. Instrumentation must be removable or bounded in production."
- "Never present the original renderer's logical draw count as the new backend's actual GPU work. F3D telemetry lives in its own diagnostic namespace."
- Ablations (§16.8) and attribution need these counters.

## Technical approach

- `f3d-runtime::telemetry`: fixed-size per-frame counter struct (no allocation), timestamps from the measurement clock, optional GPU timestamp queries when the `timestamp-query` feature is enabled on the device (recorded as unavailable otherwise); ring of the last N frames.
- Exposure: `window.__f3d.telemetry` (or the report API) in debug/perf builds; `f3d bench` consumes it; the build report includes structural estimates separately from measured timings (§3.5).
- Compile-time feature flag to remove the layer; a bounded sampling mode for production diagnostics.

## Success criteria

- Counters validated against known synthetic frames (exact draw/upload counts).
- Overhead of the instrumentation measured and reported (must be small relative to the protocol's noise band).

## Test plan

- Unit: counter validation on synthetic frames with exact expected draw/upload/binding counts; an allocation-counter test proving no per-draw heap allocation; a compile-out test for the production feature flag.
- E2E: `tests/e2e/telemetry/counters.mjs` compares counters with the adapter's actual WebGPU call counts on both browsers; instrumentation overhead measured against the protocol noise band.
- Logging: the counters are the logging; overhead reported as a `metric` event; archived under `evidence/07.7/`.
- Failure artifacts: the counter diff table.

## Considerations

- GPU timestamps: account for timer precision; unavailable telemetry stays unavailable (§16.4).
acceptance_criteria: A bounded instrumentation layer records the listed counters per logical frame and exposes them through an F3D-specific diagnostic namespace and the build/bench reports; production builds compile it out or bound it; the renderer never allocates a JSON event or runs a statistical controller per draw; upstream renderer.info contracts are untouched.

title: Camera/projection/output conventions on the new backend
description:
## Full scope

Camera, projection and output conventions on the new backend: reversed/logarithmic depth, cube-face orientation, viewport/scissor origins, alpha mode, color space, render-target output conversion; never overwrite the public WebGL projection matrix; same camera to a target and to the canvas

## Summary

Coordinate-system correctness at the renderer level (the shader-level treatment is 15a.4).

## Background (plan §8.5 "Canvas, media, and projection state", §9.4 last paragraph)

"Keep public camera/matrix observations consistent with the source backend. A private clip-depth/projection conversion must not overwrite a public WebGL projection matrix with WebGPU conventions. Match reversed/logarithmic depth, cube-face orientation, viewport/scissor origins, alpha mode, color space, and render-target output conversion. Add tests for rendering the same camera to both a target and the canvas; a generic final tone-mapping pass is not automatically equivalent."

## Technical approach

- Projection handling: the public `camera.projectionMatrix` stays as upstream computes it; the backend derives its clip-space adjustment (WebGPU 0..1 depth vs WebGL -1..1) privately in the shader IR (uniform or constant fold), never writing back.
- Depth modes: reversed depth and logarithmic depth per the renderer flags in use by the corpus; cube camera face orientation per upstream's `CubeCamera` conventions; viewport/scissor with the correct origin conventions; `alphaMode`, `outputColorSpace`, premultiplied output.
- Tests transcribed from upstream expectations: render a checker scene to canvas and to a target; compare both to upstream's WebGPU renderer output and to its WebGL output; a scene with `logarithmicDepthBuffer`; a cube camera environment capture compared face by face.

## Success criteria

- All comparisons pass within tolerance on both browsers; public projection matrix equality asserted before and after render.

## Test plan

- Unit: projection-adjustment tests (public `projectionMatrix` unchanged before/after render; private clip-space adjustment applied once); depth-mode tests (reversed, logarithmic); viewport/scissor origin tests; cube-face orientation tests.
- E2E: `tests/e2e/output/conventions.mjs` on both browsers: checker scene rendered to canvas and to a target compared against upstream WebGPU and WebGL output; logarithmic-depth scene; cube camera capture compared face by face; alpha mode/color space/premultiplied output cases.
- Logging: per-case `metric` events `{case, target: canvas|rt, max_err, face}`; archived under `evidence/07.8/`.
- Failure artifacts: per-face/per-target diffs.

## Considerations

- Two full-screen passes are not equivalent to their algebraic composition at higher precision (§5.5); output conversion stays a distinct step.
acceptance_criteria: Public camera/matrix observations remain identical to the source backend while the new backend applies any private clip-depth/projection conversion internally; reversed and logarithmic depth, cube-face orientation, viewport/scissor origins, alpha mode, color space and render-target output conversion match upstream; a test renders the same camera to a render target and to the canvas and compares both against upstream.

title: F3D-08: Legal grouping, per-use uniform versions and render bundles
description:
## What this epic delivers

The first genuine sources of gain, each behind a legality statement. Plan §19 F3D-08 depends on 06, 07 and the early slice of 12; acceptance: "Guards/callbacks/IDs, red-A/blue-B and bundle/direct tests".

## Why (plan §8.2, §8.3, §5.5, §6.7, §14.8, §16.1)

"Render bundles, compute shaders, instancing, and WebGPU support are baseline techniques, not FrankenThreeD's novelty." The gain must come from combining them with program specialization and better ownership/layout, and each optimization needs "a small legality statement, a conservative executable reference, counterexample tests, and an ablation measurement".

## Children

1. Draw buckets, persistent geometry/index buffers, packed transform/material tables, incremental upload range merging.
2. Automatic instance formation legality.
3. Persistent programs and bindings with asynchronous precompilation and bounded caches.
4. Render bundles with a structural key, executeBundles state invalidation and rebuild-cost measurement.
5. Rendering-order legality.
6. Portable indirect draw/dispatch strategy.
7. Extended red-A/blue-B regressions.

## Success criteria for the epic

All children closed; ablation toggles exist for buckets/instancing/bundles so F3D-20.5 can attribute gains; the legality statements live in the crate docs.

## No-claim boundary

Speedups from this epic are measured only under the frozen protocol in F3D-11.
acceptance_criteria: Draw organization (buckets, persistent geometry, packed tables, incremental uploads), automatic instance formation, persistent programs/bindings and render bundles are implemented under explicit legality rules that preserve logical IDs, callback order and rendering order; the red-A/blue-B and bundle-then-direct regressions plus their extensions pass; bundle rebuild cost is measured.

title: Draw buckets, persistent geometry, packed transform/material tables, upload range merging
description:
## Full scope

Draw organization: bounded buckets keyed by pipeline, geometry layout, binding strategy and ordering constraints; persistent geometry/index buffers; packed per-object transform and legal material parameter tables; incremental derived-field updates and upload range merging by measured cost

## Summary

Turn "which objects share a program and which values changed" into packed tables and a stable bucket plan.

## Background (plan §8.2 "Incremental transforms and uploads", §8.3, §4.10, §4.4 last paragraph)

- "Use a bounded set of buckets keyed by pipeline, geometry layout, binding strategy, and ordering constraints. Keep geometry/index buffers persistent. Represent per-object transforms and legal material parameters in packed tables."
- "Update only the derived fields and upload ranges whose input versions changed. Merge nearby ranges when that costs less than issuing many tiny uploads."
- "The compiler must not claim work proportional only to the number of changed fields unless its mutation coverage actually supports that claim."

## Technical approach

- Bucket key = (pipeline variant, vertex layout, binding strategy, ordering class from 08.5); bucket membership recomputed only on structural events (06.3); per-bucket contiguous slices of the transform/material tables so uploads are range-based.
- Tables: `AffineRows` array and material parameter blocks (05.2 layout) in storage buffers or dynamic-offset uniform slices depending on the device profile; per-use versions (07.4) for values that change within a frame.
- Upload merging: a cost model with measured constants per device (from 03.5/05.6 bridge data) deciding merge vs split; must respect 06.6's gap rule when merging across bytes the source has not requested.
- Persistent geometry: residency generations per geometry replica; re-upload only on attribute request versions.

## Success criteria

- On H1 with static toggles: uploads per frame ≈ 0 bytes for transforms; with dynamic: bytes proportional to moved objects; bucket count stable across frames (counters from 07.7).
- Rendering order equals upstream's render list order within each ordering class (verified by trace).

## Test plan

- Unit: bucket-key derivation tests; range-merge cost-model tests with fixed constants (merge only when cheaper; 06.6 gap rule respected); residency-generation tests for persistent geometry.
- E2E: `tests/e2e/grouping/buckets.mjs` on H1 in the forced-new-backend lane on both browsers: static toggle → ~0 transform upload bytes per frame; dynamic → bytes proportional to moved objects; bucket count stable; render order equals upstream's render list order within each ordering class (trace).
- Logging: per-frame bucket summary `{buckets, draws, upload_ranges, upload_bytes}` and the upload range list in debug; archived under `evidence/08.1/`.
- Failure artifacts: bucket assignment dump and the order-trace diff.

## Considerations

- Vertex pulling is not assumed to beat ordinary buffers (§8.3); it is an optional measured strategy later.
acceptance_criteria: The render list is organized into a bounded set of buckets; geometry/index buffers persist across frames with residency generations; per-object AffineRows and material parameters live in packed tables updated only for changed versions; nearby dirty ranges are merged only when measured cheaper than separate uploads; H1's 4,000 objects produce a small stable bucket set with upload bytes proportional to changed fields, without changing rendering order semantics.

title: Automatic instance formation legality (IDs, winding, callback multiplicity)
description:
## Full scope

Automatic instance formation legality: full draw-observation contract, preserved logical object/face/vertex/instance IDs including custom shader uses of indices, no accidental instance ID for originally noninstanced draws, negative-determinant winding buckets, source-ordered per-object callbacks under batching (callback multiplicity counterexample), unknown shader side effects prevent batching

## Summary

Instancing as a legal transformation, not a pipeline-key coincidence.

## Background (plan §8.2 "Automatic instance formation", §5.5, §14.8; AGENTS.md counterexample "Callback multiplicity under batching")

"Merge draw preparation only when the full draw-observation contract permits it, not merely when pipeline keys match. Preserve logical object, face, vertex, and instance IDs, including custom shader uses of instance/vertex indices. An originally noninstanced draw must not accidentally acquire a different logical instance ID after batching. Negative-determinant transforms may require a separate winding bucket. Per-object callbacks remain source-ordered effects; merging physical draws does not erase or reorder them. Unknown shader side effects or callback-dependent state prevent the affected batching."

## Technical approach
