- `f3d bench` cells; ablations for animation batching and update kernels.

## Success criteria

- Results documents per stratum with verdicts vs the 2× floor; feeds G4 and F3D-23.2.

## Test plan

- Unit: none new.
- E2E: build H3 and H5; `f3d verify` equivalence on both browsers; `f3d bench` paired runs on the reserved M5 and phone under protocol v1 with frozen references; ablation toggles for animation batching (H3) and update kernels (H5).
- Logging: raw per-frame bench JSON, analysis reports with intervals, ablation deltas; archived under `evidence/13.8/<stratum>/`.
- Failure artifacts: invalidated runs retained with reasons; verify artifacts.

## Considerations

- A cell below 2× is reported as such; it is not removed.
acceptance_criteria: H3 and H5 build automatically, pass equivalence, and produce paired throughput results with intervals on at least the M5 and phone strata through the new backend; the report attributes gains to animation batching (H3) and update-kernel/upload efficiency (H5) via ablation toggles; no claim beyond the measured cells.

title: F3D-14: Entire standard material/light/texture/renderer format surface through the new backend
description:
## What this epic delivers

Phase 3's rendering closure for the standard surface. Plan §19 F3D-14 depends on 07 and 11; acceptance: "Every inventoried family and options, not only example-selected features".

## Why (plan §5.12 rows Materials, Physical shading, Lights, Textures, Cameras, Modern renderer APIs; §5.16; §8.4–8.6; §9.2; §18 Phase 3)

"Finish every standard material/map/state/light/shadow/texture/camera/render-target path... Run all applicable rendering cases with retained renderer submission disabled, beyond H1–H8. Close color/precision/history/diagnostic/resource-life combinations and port no feature by substituting a simpler visual effect." "A portable material or pass is not marked 'native-backend-bound' merely because implementing it is difficult."

## Children

1. All built-in materials with every parameter/map/state combination.
2. Physical shading closure.
3. Lights, environments and shadows including the clustered path.
4. Textures and media sources including external video lifecycle.
5. Cameras, views and output.
6. Render-target contract.
7. Modern renderer/backend public APIs.
8. Mobile bandwidth and tile behavior.
9. Diagnostic shader targets and material differential infrastructure.

## Success criteria for the epic

All children closed; the forced new-backend lane passes for every portable family; the manifest's new-WebGPU-path status is set for every record in these families; `f3d-shader` line count reported against 30,000 and `f3d-gpu` against 27,000.

## No-claim boundary

Numerical/backend semantics that genuinely require original GL are separately evidenced per record; never a blanket category.
acceptance_criteria: Every inventoried material, physical-shading extension, light/environment/shadow technique, texture/media source, camera/view/output mode, render-target contract and modern renderer/backend API has a working path through the new WebGPU backend (or a separately evidenced exact/native exception) with property sweeps and combination tests, not only example-selected features.

title: All built-in materials with every parameter, map, state and transition through the new backend
description:
## Full scope

All built-in materials through the new backend: Basic, Normal, Depth, Distance, Lambert, Phong, Toon, Matcap, Standard, Physical, Line/LineDashed, Points, Sprite, Shadow; every parameter and map (map, alphaMap, aoMap, bumpMap, displacementMap, emissiveMap, envMap, lightMap, metalnessMap, normalMap, roughnessMap, specularMap, gradientMap, matcap, etc.) and valid combination; alpha test/hash/coverage, blending modes, depth/stencil, sides, clipping planes, shadow/depth overrides, dynamic option changes and state transitions

## Summary

From the H1/H2 slice to the whole built-in material surface.

## Background (plan §5.12 "Materials and render state", §9.2, §14.9)

"Full standard material paths through the new backend; dynamic options and state transitions; genuine backend extensions retain exact execution." Combinations: "clipping+stencil+transparency; instancing+negative scale+custom shader indices+picking; transmission+color management+render targets".

## Technical approach

- Extend `f3d-shader`'s material semantics with every pinned chunk/node for the listed materials; generate variants from the material feature set (08.3 keys); render-state descriptors (blending factors/equations incl. custom blending, depth func/write, stencil ops, cull mode, polygon offset, alpha to coverage, clipping planes as uniforms/discards per upstream).
- Sweep generator in `f3d-conformance`: per material, all boolean flags × representative map sets × pairwise generation with a fixed seed; reference images from upstream WebGL and WebGPU renderers; diagnostic targets (14.9).
- Runtime transitions: mutate flags/maps mid-run; compare.

## Success criteria

- Sweep and transition tests green in the forced lane on both browsers; manifest statuses set.

## Test plan

- Unit: shader-IR snapshot tests per material and feature flag; render-state descriptor mapping tests (blending factors/equations incl. custom, depth func/write, stencil ops, cull mode, polygon offset, alpha-to-coverage, clipping planes); variant-key tests.
- E2E: generated pairwise sweeps `tests/e2e/materials/sweep-<material>.mjs` in the forced-new-backend lane on Chrome and Safari against upstream WebGL and WebGPU references with 03.6 tolerances and 14.9 diagnostic targets; runtime transition script (needsUpdate, blending/side/clipping toggles mid-run); the known high-risk combinations that involve materials.
- Logging: per-step `metric` events `{material, flags, maps, max_err, mean_err, worst_region, diag_channel}`; recompile/rebind events on transitions; archived under `evidence/14.1/`.
- Failure artifacts: reference/candidate/diff images and diagnostic-channel images per failing step.

## Considerations

- Alpha hash/coverage and `alphaToCoverage` depend on sample counts; keep quality settings equal to the reference.
acceptance_criteria: Every built-in material class and node-material counterpart renders through the new backend with all pinned parameters/maps; a generated pairwise sweep over maps/state flags plus the known high-risk combinations matches upstream within tolerance; changing options at runtime (needsUpdate transitions, blending/side/clipping toggles) recompiles/rebinds correctly; the manifest records the new-WebGPU-path status per material property.

title: Physical shading closure (clearcoat, sheen, anisotropy, iridescence, transmission, dispersion, retroreflection)
description:
## Full scope

Physical shading closure: pinned Standard/Physical equations and every extension (clearcoat and clearcoat normal/roughness, sheen, anisotropy, iridescence, transmission/thickness/attenuation/volume, IOR/specular color and intensity, dispersion, and every r186-introduced property including retroreflective controls); all tone-mapping operators, color spaces and premultiplication; reference scenes and sweeps including high-contrast and near-degenerate cases

## Summary

The exact pinned physical model, including the properties no demo exercises.

## Background (plan §5.12 "Physical shading and color", §9.2, §15.4)

"Versioned shader semantics and property sweeps, with texture/animation/light combinations; no generic-PBR substitution." "The physical-material matrix must cover the actual pinned features, including clearcoat, transmission, attenuation, iridescence, sheen, anisotropy, dispersion, and every newly introduced r186 property, including retroreflective controls, whether or not the current demo corpus exercises it."

## Technical approach

- Transcribe pinned `MeshPhysicalMaterial`/node-material physical chunks (BRDF terms, multiscatter, iridescence Fresnel, sheen, clearcoat, transmission with the transmission render target and mip sampling, dispersion sampling, retroreflection) into shader IR; tone mapping operators (`Linear`, `Reinhard`, `Cineon`, `ACESFilmic`, `AgX`, `Neutral`, custom) and color-space conversions.
- Transmission requires the transmission pass (with F3D-17 integration for render targets).
- Sweeps with controlled environments and high-contrast/degenerate inputs (zero roughness, IOR extremes, thickness 0).

## Success criteria

- Sweeps green; `webgl_loader_gltf_transmission` and `webgpu_loader_gltf_dispersion` fidelity cases pass.

## Test plan

- Unit: shader-IR snapshot tests for every physical extension term and tone-mapping operator; color-space conversion tests vs upstream `ColorManagement`.
- E2E: physical sweeps `tests/e2e/materials/physical.mjs` (clearcoat, sheen, anisotropy with tangent conventions, iridescence thin-film, transmission with render-target color management, dispersion, retroreflection, IOR/specular/volume extremes, every tone mapping and output color space) in the forced lane on both browsers; the glTF transmission and dispersion fidelity cases via `f3d verify`.
- Logging: per-step metrics as in 14.1 plus the GPU error-envelope check per case; archived under `evidence/14.2/`.
- Failure artifacts: diff and diagnostic images.

## Considerations

- "Define the allowed GPU error/behavior envelope before optimization and require the source and candidate to stay inside it" (§5.4).
acceptance_criteria: Physical-shading manifest records all have new-WebGPU-path status with sweeps matching upstream within tolerance, including transmission with render-target color management, dispersion, iridescence thin-film math, anisotropy with tangent conventions, and retroreflection; no generic-PBR substitution; the glTF transmission and dispersion fidelity cases render correctly.

title: Lights, environments and shadows closure incl. clustered path with no dropped lights
description:
## Full scope

Lights, environments and shadows: every core/addon light (directional/point/spot/hemisphere/rect-area/ambient/light probes/IES/projector/sun-style addons), environment maps and PMREM, cube maps, all shadow techniques (basic/PCF/PCFSoft/VSM, point-light cube shadows, spot/directional cascades via CSM), contact and progressive shadow techniques, helpers/generators; clustered/Forward+ path with overflow spill and infinite-range separate path; shadow caching only when all inputs unchanged; source callbacks still executed

## Summary

Lighting and shadows at full inventory, with caching that never skips a required effect.

## Background (plan §5.12 "Lights, environments and shadows", §8.4, §8.5 first paragraph)

"Cache shadow work only when all shadow inputs are unchanged, including geometry deformation, visibility, light/camera state, alpha/displacement effects, and render-target contents. Execute any source-required callback or node update even when the GPU result can be reused; skip the entire operation only if its effects are also proven absent." Clustered: "It must include every light that can contribute under the source's model. Finite influence bounds require a valid bound; infinite-range lights need a separate path. Overflow in a tile/cluster light list cannot drop lights. Use an overflow spill or exact slower path."

## Technical approach

- Light uniform structures per pinned layouts; shadow map passes in the pass graph with dependency versions (06.3 categories: light params, shadow inputs); cache validity computed from consumed versions.
- Retain construction/baking logic (PMREM, LightProbeGenerator, progressive light map addons) executing through the new backend.
- Clustered path as an execution strategy selected by the specialization portfolio (F3D-20.2) with the overflow rule and the forward path as the conservative reference.

## Success criteria

- Family suite green; H4 and the shadow examples pass equivalence; a many-light test with forced cluster overflow shows no dropped light.

## Test plan

- Unit: light uniform layout tests; shadow-cache validity tests from consumed versions (deformation, visibility, light/camera, alpha/displacement, target contents each invalidate); clustered-path tests with a CPU reference (overflow spill keeps every light; infinite-range lights take the separate path).
- E2E: sweeps over every light/shadow/environment type in the forced lane on both browsers vs upstream; H4 equivalence; a many-light scene with forced cluster overflow shows no dropped light; a callback-inside-shadow-pass test proves source-required callbacks still run when the GPU result is reused.
- Logging: shadow cache events `{light, reused: bool, invalidation_reason}`; cluster stats `{tiles, max_per_tile, spills}`; per-step error metrics; archived under `evidence/14.3/`.
- Failure artifacts: diff images and the light-list dump for the overflow case.

## Considerations

- Clustered lighting exists in upstream examples; the R1/R2 references include it where applicable (§8.4).
acceptance_criteria: All light/shadow/environment manifest records have new-WebGPU-path status with tests; shadow passes cache only when geometry deformation, visibility, light/camera state, alpha/displacement effects and target contents are unchanged, while source-required callbacks/node updates still run; a clustered path exists for many-light workloads with a proven no-dropped-light rule and the simple forward path retained; H4's shadow workload renders correctly.

title: Textures and media sources closure incl. external video lifecycle
description:
## Full scope

Textures and media sources: all texture/source/sampler classes (2D, cube, 3D, arrays, data/depth/storage/render-target textures, external/video/canvas/HTML sources, compressed formats and mips, partial updates, filters/anisotropy/wrap, color space, flipY/premultiply/unpack alignment); device-lawful formats without quality reduction; external video lifetime (refresh at media/render boundaries, VideoFrame ownership, close exactly once, seeking/pause/replacement/origin tests)

## Summary

Every texture kind, plus the special rules for media.

## Background (plan §5.12 "Textures and media sources", §8.5 "Canvas, media, and projection state", §10.2, §23 [S39])

"External video textures have a source-dependent lifetime and color conversion, not an indefinitely reusable ordinary texture binding. Refresh them at supported media/render boundaries, retain `VideoFrame` ownership until its uses are done, and close it exactly once. Cache only what remains valid; do not retain an expired external texture in a reusable bundle."

## Technical approach

- Texture residency states in `f3d-gpu` (07.1) per source kind; upload paths (`writeTexture` layout rules, `copyExternalImageToTexture` for images/canvas/video frames, `importExternalTexture` for video where supported with the per-frame validity flag that excludes draws from bundles).
- Format selection from the capability record; compressed formats (BC/ETC2/ASTC via KTX2 transcoding in F3D-19.2) with mips/block-edge rules.
- Sampler descriptors mapping upstream filter/wrap/anisotropy/compare semantics.
- Tests transcribed per class; media tests with a local video server.

## Success criteria

- Family suite green; video tests green on both browsers; no bundle retains an external texture.

## Test plan

- Unit: residency/upload-path tests per source kind (`writeTexture` layout rules, `copyExternalImageToTexture`, `importExternalTexture` per-frame validity flag excluding draws from bundles); sampler descriptor mapping tests; format selection tests from capability records (compressed formats, mip/block-edge rules).
- E2E: texture-kind sweeps in the forced lane on both browsers (2D/cube/3D/array, data/depth/storage/RT, canvas/HTML/video sources, compressed formats via 19.2 fixtures, partial updates, filters/anisotropy/wrap, color space, flipY/premultiply/unpack alignment); media lifecycle tests with the local video server (seeking, pause/resume, `srcObject` replacement, frame closure exactly once, origin restrictions); the video fidelity case via `f3d verify`.
- Logging: per-texture events `{kind, format, source, upload_path, bytes}`; media lifecycle events `{event, frame_closed}`; error metrics per sweep step; archived under `evidence/14.4/`.
- Failure artifacts: diff images and the external-texture lifetime trace.

## Considerations

- Multiple renderer residencies + disposal is a mandatory combination test (18b.2).
acceptance_criteria: Every texture-family manifest record has new-WebGPU-path status with tests; compressed formats are used natively where the device supports them and otherwise a justified equivalent representation is used without lossier content; texture partial updates and mip behavior match upstream; external video textures follow the source-dependent lifetime rules with tests for seeking, pause/resume, source replacement, frame closure and origin restrictions; the video fidelity case passes.

title: Cameras, views and output closure
description:
## Full scope

Cameras, views and output: perspective/orthographic/array/stereo/cube cameras, view offsets, custom projections, reversed and logarithmic depth, viewport/scissor/device pixel ratio, multiple canvases and targets, offscreen output; public matrices compared across all views

## Summary

Complete the camera/view surface started in 07.8.

## Background (plan §5.12 "Cameras, views and output")

"Native renderer plus exact native-context route where observed; compare public matrices and all views."

## Technical approach

- View iteration in the execution protocol (07.4) for array/stereo cameras with per-view viewports; cube camera as six passes with orientation conventions; view offsets.
- Multi-canvas: separate output epochs and resource groups (07.2).

## Success criteria

- Family suite green; multi-view examples pass equivalence.

## Test plan

- Unit: view-iteration tests for array/stereo cameras (viewport per view); cube-camera pass sequence and orientation tests; `setViewOffset` tiling tests; multi-canvas epoch separation tests.
- E2E: camera/view sweeps in the forced lane on both browsers (perspective/orthographic/array/stereo/cube, view offsets, custom projections, reversed/log depth, DPR changes, multiple canvases, offscreen targets) with public-matrix comparison for every view; the relevant upstream examples via `f3d verify`.
- Logging: per-view `metric` events `{camera, view, max_err, projection_equal: bool}`; archived under `evidence/14.5/`.
- Failure artifacts: per-view diff images and matrix dumps.

## Considerations

- XR views are F3D-21b.3 but reuse this machinery.
acceptance_criteria: Every camera/view manifest record has new-WebGPU-path status with tests; ArrayCamera and StereoCamera multi-view rendering, CubeCamera captures, setViewOffset tiling, DPR changes, multiple canvases with separate epochs and offscreen targets match upstream; public matrices are compared for every view.

title: Render-target contract closure (cube/array/3D, MRT, depth/stencil, MSAA, explicit ops)
description:
## Full scope

Render-target contract: cube/array/3D targets, layers and mip levels, multiple render targets, depth/stencil attachments and textures, MSAA and resolves, clipping, explicit clear/load/store behavior, formats and usage flags validated in the plan

## Summary

Render targets as first-class pass-graph resources with the full upstream option surface.

## Background (plan §8.5 "Support every applicable rendering contract", §5.6)

"cube/array/3D textures, render-target layers and mip levels, multiple render targets, depth/stencil, viewport/scissor, multisampling/resolves, clipping, and explicit clear/load/store behavior. Resource formats and usage flags are part of the plan's validation."

## Technical approach

- Target descriptors → pass-graph attachments with subresource ranges; MSAA with resolve attachments; depth/stencil formats per capability; `autoClear`/`clearColor/Depth/Stencil` semantics as explicit load ops.
- Async readback through staging buffers (17.4 integrates copies).

## Success criteria

- Family suite green; MRT/cube/array examples pass equivalence.

## Test plan

- Unit: target-descriptor → attachment mapping tests (cube/array/3D, layers/mips, MRT, depth/stencil formats, sample counts and resolves, explicit load/store/clear from `autoClear`/`clear*`); format/usage validation tests; staging-buffer readback tests.
- E2E: render-target sweeps in the forced lane on both browsers vs upstream (MRT, cube/array/3D targets, mip-level and layer targets, MSAA resolves, depth textures, clipping); `readRenderTargetPixelsAsync` correctness; a sync-read attempt on a new-backend renderer is proven to have been routed exactly at construction.
- Logging: per-target events `{target, attachments, format, samples, ops}` and readback checks; archived under `evidence/14.6/`.
- Failure artifacts: readback dumps and diff images.

## Considerations

- Source-visible render targets prevent transient reuse (17.2).
acceptance_criteria: Every render-target manifest record (WebGLRenderTarget variants, RenderTarget, cube/array/3D targets, MRT, depth textures, sample counts, resolve targets, mip-level/layer targets) has new-WebGPU-path status with tests; attachment operations are explicit in the pass graph; formats/usages are validated; readbacks (readRenderTargetPixelsAsync) work on the new backend and synchronous reads remain exact-route only.

title: Modern renderer/backend public API closure (three/webgpu exports)
description:
## Full scope

Modern renderer/backend public APIs: WebGPURenderer/Renderer options and methods, exported Backend classes, BundleGroup, QuadMesh, RenderPipeline/DirectRenderPipeline/PostProcessing, CanvasTarget/BlendMode, readback and storage APIs, backend extension hooks; new WebGPU implementation of standard execution with the exact component for native opaque subclass/handle contracts

## Summary

The modern renderer surface exported by `three/webgpu`, including things no demo calls.

## Background (plan §2.9, §5.12 "Modern renderer/backend APIs", §23 [S53])

"`Three.WebGPU.js` also exports backend classes, node builders, storage objects, render pipelines, and loaders. Those are part of the actual surface, not hypothetical third-party internals." "New WebGPU implementation of standard execution; exact component for native opaque subclass/handle contracts; no forced downgrade of modern features."

## Technical approach

- From the manifest, enumerate the export list; for each: standard execution mapping (BundleGroup → 08.4 bundles with upstream's semantics; QuadMesh; RenderPipeline/PostProcessing → F3D-17; CanvasTarget/BlendMode; storage buffers/textures → F3D-16.3; readbacks → 17.4) or exact/native routing (custom `Backend` subclass instances, `WebGLBackend` explicit use, native device/handle observations).
- Renderer option matrix tests.

## Success criteria

- Family suite green; each export's owner recorded.

## Test plan

- Unit: export-list-driven mapping tests (each `three/webgpu` export → standard execution mapping or exact/native route with the named contract); renderer option matrix tests (antialias, alpha, forceWebGL, requiredLimits, etc.).
- E2E: generated family suite over every `Three.WebGPU.js` public export in the functional and forced lanes on both browsers; custom `Backend` subclass fixtures in the exact lane with real native objects asserted.
- Logging: per-export `{export, owner, route, test}` feeding the manifest; archived under `evidence/14.7/`.
- Failure artifacts: the failing export's test log.

## Considerations

- "For native WebGPU contracts preserve actual device/resource objects through the appropriate component" (§5.6).
acceptance_criteria: Every Three.WebGPU.js public export has an owner and positive tests: standard execution through the new backend, exact/native components for opaque subclass and native-handle contracts; no forced downgrade of modern features; renderer options (antialias, alpha, forceWebGL, requiredLimits, etc.) behave as upstream.

title: Mobile bandwidth and tile behavior without quality reduction
description:
## Full scope

Mobile bandwidth and tile behavior: avoid provably unnecessary stores, clears, copies and full-resolution intermediates; optional transient-attachment support as a capability-specific path; no silent reduction of resolution, shadow size, MSAA, anisotropy, samples, geometry detail or temporal history

## Summary

Bandwidth wins that are purely structural.

## Background (plan §8.6, §23 [S21])

"Reduce attachment traffic by avoiding unnecessary stores, clears, copies, and full-resolution intermediates that are provably unused. Optional transient-attachment support is a capability-specific path; do not depend on it universally. Do not silently reduce render resolution, shadow size, MSAA, anisotropy, samples per pixel, geometry detail, or temporal history to obtain a performance win."

## Technical approach

- Dead-store analysis over the pass graph (explicit dependency edges only, 07.2); load/store op selection; transient attachment flag when the feature exists.
- Quality-invariance test: compare all quality-affecting settings between reference and candidate at plan time.

## Success criteria

- Telemetry shows reduced store bytes on tile-sensitive tests; quality-invariance test passes.

## Test plan

- Unit: dead-store analysis tests over pass-graph fixtures (store elided only for provably unused attachments; explicit dependency edges only); transient-attachment gating test from the capability record; quality-invariance test comparing every quality-affecting setting between reference and candidate at plan time.
- E2E: tile-sensitive scenes on the phone and M5 with telemetry showing reduced store bytes and identical output vs upstream; the quality-invariance check runs in every forced-lane test.
- Logging: attachment traffic `metric` events `{pass, loads, stores, bytes_saved}`; quality-invariance report; archived under `evidence/14.8/`.
- Failure artifacts: the plan diff showing the elided operation on any output mismatch.

## Considerations

- Thermal behavior is measured in F3D-23.3; this bead enables, not claims.
acceptance_criteria: The pass graph elides store operations for attachments proven unused, avoids redundant clears/copies, and uses transient attachments only when the capability record supports them; a test guards that no quality parameter is changed by any optimization; attachment traffic is reported in telemetry.

title: Diagnostic shader targets and material differential infrastructure
description:
## Full scope

Diagnostic shader targets and the material differential infrastructure: intermediate normals, depth, material channels (albedo/roughness/metalness/emissive), world position; color-space-aware comparison, edge/silhouette and region checks, temporal consistency; used by all material/light/pass sweeps

## Summary

Make subtle mismatches findable.

## Background (plan §9.6, §14.6)

"Diagnostic shaders for intermediate normals, depth, material channels, and world position make subtle mismatches much easier to locate than final-color screenshots alone." "Use color-space-aware comparisons, edge/silhouette checks, region checks, depth/normal diagnostic targets, and temporal consistency in addition to aggregate image metrics."

## Technical approach

- Shader IR debug outputs selectable per pass; reference-side equivalents via upstream `MeshNormalMaterial`/depth materials/custom debug materials applied identically.
- Comparison library in the tooling package with the preregistered tolerance model (03.6).

## Success criteria

- Used by 14.1–14.3 sweeps; a synthetic mismatch is localized correctly.

## Test plan

- Unit: comparison-library tests (color-space-aware metric, edge/silhouette, region checks, temporal consistency) on synthetic fixtures; a known-bad fixture localized to the correct channel and region; diagnostic-output selection tests in the shader IR.
- E2E: diagnostic renders of a reference scene compared against upstream debug materials (normal/depth/world position/channels) on both browsers.
- Logging: per-comparison `metric` events `{channel, max_err, region}`; archived under `evidence/14.9/`.
- Failure artifacts: diagnostic images from both sides and the diff.

## Considerations

- Never regenerate goldens from the candidate.
acceptance_criteria: A diagnostic mode renders intermediate quantities from the same shader IR; the comparison library implements the §14.6 checks; sweeps report the first mismatching channel and region; goldens come only from the reference.

title: F3D-15 (early slice): H1/H2 shader preparation, the finite ESSL-to-WGSL spike and toon node lowering
description:
## What this epic delivers

The shader half of the first vertical slice. Plan §19 F3D-15 depends on 04; the early acceptance is "finite spike before 11". "F3D-15's initial work is source analysis/normalization and WGSL generation, not dependence on an already complete renderer. Its rendered acceptance integrates with F3D-07."

## Why (plan §2.7, §9.1, §9.4, §20 "Legacy shader translation becomes a compiler project larger than budget")

"A plan that says 'run all Three.js GLSL through Naga' is incomplete. Naga's documented GLSL frontend targets Vulkan GLSL versions, not a complete turnkey WebGL GLSL ES 1.00/3.00 frontend." The earliest decisive test for the shader-budget risk is "full finite H2 corpus and H1 material spike before the first product gate". The ESSL frontend is the largest single budget uncertainty.

## Children

1. ESSL pipeline skeleton with diagnostics.
2. H2 legacy ShaderMaterial variants and the ShaderLib chunks H2 reaches.
3. H1 MeshToonNodeMaterial TSL lowering.
4. Coordinate-system and interface treatment.
5. Naga admission audit and build-time-only default.

## Success criteria for the epic

All children closed; every H2 shader variant and H1's toon material produce validated WGSL that renders equivalently; the spike's line count is recorded against the 30,000-line `f3d-shader` budget with a forecast for the full frontend (15b).

## No-claim boundary

This is a finite corpus. Unseen runtime shaders are F3D-15b's obligation; nothing here implies full ESSL coverage.
acceptance_criteria: A dedicated bounded ESSL preprocessing/normalization/interface/Naga/WGSL pipeline translates the complete finite shader corpus reachable by H2 (its ShaderLib materials and four legacy ShaderMaterial variants) and lowers H1's MeshToonNodeMaterial graph, with source locations, readable diagnostics, explicit coordinate-system treatment and differential render tests; Naga is admitted as a build-time dependency with an audit record.

title: ESSL compatibility pipeline skeleton (preprocess, normalize, interfaces, Naga, WGSL, diagnostics)
description:
## Full scope

ESSL compatibility pipeline skeleton: Three shader source plus includes/defines/material hooks; ESSL preprocessing (macros, ShaderChunk includes, defines) and semantic normalization; explicit stage interfaces, resources and builtins; supported Naga IR/GLSL entrance; validation and WGSL emission; source locations and readable diagnostics

## Summary

The pipeline of §9.4, built as a real language tool.

## Background (plan §9.4, §9.1, §23 [S20], [S36])

```
Three shader source + includes/defines + material hooks
  -> ESSL preprocessing and semantic normalization
  -> explicit stage interfaces, resources, and builtins
  -> supported Naga IR/GLSL entrance
  -> validation and WGSL emission
  -> browser compilation and differential render tests
```
"The normalization layer must handle actual language constructs, not regex-only syntax substitutions. The first shader spike includes macros, includes, samplers, precision declarations, derivatives, fragment depth, discard, loops, matrix/vector operations, and interface matching."

## Technical approach

- Preprocessor: full C-style macro expansion as ESSL specifies (object/function-like macros, `#if/#ifdef/#elif` with expression evaluation, `#include` resolution against the pinned `ShaderChunk` table and material `defines`), `#extension`/`#version`/precision handling recorded as metadata, line/file mapping preserved.
- Parser/normalizer: an ESSL 1.00/3.00 parser (first-party, bounded to what Three.js and valid application shaders use) producing an AST; normalization passes: resolve implicit `gl_*` builtins to explicit interface variables, attribute/varying/uniform declarations into stage interfaces, combined `sampler2D` uniforms into (texture, sampler) pairs (15a.4), precision qualifiers dropped with a record, legacy syntax (`attribute`/`varying`/`texture2D`) upgraded.
- Emission: prefer Naga's GLSL frontend on the normalized Vulkan-compatible GLSL when it accepts the program; otherwise emit from the first-party AST to Naga IR or directly to WGSL text (decision recorded per program in the report); Naga validation always runs.
- Diagnostics with spans mapped through include expansion to `ShaderChunk` names and application lines.

## Success criteria

- Test corpus translates and validates; diagnostics tested with deliberately broken chunks; fuzz seed corpus started (15b.5).
- `f3d-shader/CONTRACT.md` is written before any other crate depends on `f3d-shader` (AGENTS.md "Documentation and Contracts"): purpose and position in the dependency direction, public types and semantics, invariants, implementation ownership route, error model, determinism and numeric-fidelity class, cancellation behavior, unsafe boundary if any, feature flags, conformance tests, and no-claim boundaries.

## Test plan

- Unit: preprocessor tests per feature (object/function-like macros, `#if/#ifdef/#elif` expressions, `#include` against the pinned ShaderChunk table with material defines, `#extension`/`#version`/precision metadata, line/file mapping); parser/normalizer tests per construct (builtins → interface variables, attribute/varying/uniform declarations, legacy syntax upgrade); golden WGSL snapshots for the initial corpus; diagnostics tests with deliberately broken chunks mapping back to chunk name and line.
- E2E: the corpus programs compile in Chrome and Safari (pipeline creation succeeds) and a smoke render matches upstream.
- Logging: per-program pipeline-stage events `{program, stage, ms, naga_path: glsl-in|first-party, warnings}`; archived under `evidence/15a.1/`.
- Failure artifacts: the normalized GLSL and emitted WGSL for the failing program with the diagnostic.

## Considerations

- Keep it build-time-only for statically closed pages; the runtime inclusion path is 15b.2.
acceptance_criteria: f3d-shader contains a real (not regex-only) ESSL preprocessor and normalizer producing an explicit stage-interface representation, feeding Naga's supported GLSL entrance (or a first-party IR when Naga's frontend cannot accept the normalized form), validating and emitting WGSL; every diagnostic maps back to the original Three.js chunk/line; a first test corpus (a handful of ShaderLib programs) translates and validates.

title: H2 legacy ShaderMaterial variants and ShaderLib chunks translated with differential tests
description:
## Full scope

H2 legacy ShaderMaterial variants and the ShaderLib chunks reached by H2's materials translated to WGSL with differential render tests

## Summary

The finite corpus that the first product gate requires.

## Background (plan §2.7, §15.3, §20 row 5)

"Its default material and every material-selector branch, including the four legacy ShaderMaterial variants, belong in the first product slice; the UI cannot be restricted to an easy shader after the fact."

## Technical approach

- Extract the exact shader sources from the pinned example (they are inline `ShaderMaterial` definitions; record their uniforms/attributes) and the chunk closure of the built-in materials H2 uses (from the pinned `ShaderLib` + `ShaderChunk` tables with the defines those materials set).
- Translate; hook the uniforms into the parameter-block layout (05.2); differential render on the marching-cubes mesh at several control states.

## Success criteria

- All programs green; the variant table lists them as precompiled.

## Test plan

- Unit: golden WGSL snapshots for the four legacy ShaderMaterial programs and every ShaderLib/ShaderChunk program in H2's closure; uniform/attribute interface tests against the parameter-block layout.
- E2E: differential renders `tests/e2e/shaders/h2-corpus.mjs` on the marching-cubes mesh at several control states in the forced lane on both browsers vs upstream with 03.6 tolerances.
- Logging: per-program translation status and per-render error metrics; archived under `evidence/15a.2/`.
- Failure artifacts: WGSL, diff images and diagnostic targets.

## Considerations

- Any ESSL construct in this corpus the pipeline cannot handle is a blocker for F3D-11, not a "legacy-only" reclassification.
acceptance_criteria: The four legacy ShaderMaterial programs in the pinned webgl_marchingcubes.html (as inventoried in 01.6) and every ShaderLib/ShaderChunk program reached by H2's Standard/Lambert/Phong/texture/color branches translate through the pipeline, validate under Naga, compile in Chrome and Safari, and render equivalently to upstream in differential tests with the H2 geometry.

title: H1 MeshToonNodeMaterial TSL lowering
description:
## Full scope

H1 MeshToonNodeMaterial TSL lowering: node semantics for every node in H1's toon graph (gradient step lighting, color/uniform nodes, lighting context nodes) translated to typed shader IR and WGSL with differential tests

## Summary

The node entrance at H1's scope; the full node inventory is F3D-16.

## Background (plan §9.3, §2.7, §5.12 "TSL, nodes and compute")

"Let ordinary JavaScript construct TSL graphs, then translate recognized nodes into typed shader IR."

## Technical approach

- Enumerate the node classes reached by `MeshToonNodeMaterial` in the pinned source (lighting model nodes, `toonLightingModel`-equivalent functions, material reference nodes, uniform/attribute nodes); implement translator entries; compare with upstream's WGSL output as a debugging aid (not as the oracle; the oracle is rendered output).
- Fallback: for any node not yet translated, use the retained upstream node builder to produce WGSL (disclosed in the report as retained shader construction), still submitted through the new backend.

## Success criteria

- Differential render equivalence on H1; translator coverage report for the graph.

## Test plan

- Unit: translator snapshot tests for every node class in H1's toon graph; a coverage test asserting each node is either translated or explicitly recorded as retained-builder fallback.
- E2E: differential render of H1's toon scene in the forced lane on both browsers vs upstream's WebGPU renderer.
- Logging: translator coverage report `{node, status}` and render error metrics; archived under `evidence/15a.3/`.
- Failure artifacts: IR/WGSL dumps and diff images.

## Considerations

- 07.5 handles the runtime update semantics; this bead is the static lowering.
acceptance_criteria: The node graph constructed by H1's MeshToonNodeMaterial (with its per-object colors) lowers to WGSL through the node translator with every node in the graph recognized (or retained via the upstream WGSL node builder output as a disclosed fallback); the resulting shader renders equivalently to upstream's WebGPU renderer on H1's geometry set.

title: Coordinate-system and interface treatment in translation (depth range, winding, samplers, builtins)
description:
## Full scope

Coordinate-system and interface treatment in translation: clip-depth range, framebuffer conventions, winding, texture orientation, fragment coordinates, interpolation qualifiers; combined-sampler splitting, integer/flat varyings, attribute normalization, explicit buffer layout, source vertex/instance builtins; point-size and line behavior expansion where the source contract requires it

## Summary

The semantic differences between WebGL GLSL and WebGPU WGSL, handled explicitly.

## Background (plan §9.4 last two paragraphs)

"Add combined-sampler splitting, integer/flat varyings, attribute normalization, explicit buffer layout, and source vertex/instance builtins." "Coordinate-system differences require explicit treatment: clip-depth range, framebuffer conventions, winding, texture orientation, fragment coordinates, and interpolation. Point-size and line behavior need appropriate geometry/shader expansion when the source contract requires it."

## Technical approach

- Normalization passes with unit tests per difference; clip-depth adjustment coordinated with 07.8 so it happens exactly once; `gl_FragCoord` y-flip policy; texture orientation (`flipY`) handled at upload or sampling consistently with upstream.
- Point sprites: WebGPU has no point size; expand to instanced quads when `gl_PointSize`/`PointsMaterial.size` semantics require it, preserving `gl_PointCoord`.
- Wide lines: `LineBasicMaterial.linewidth` is effectively 1 on WebGL; `Line2`/`LineMaterial` addon geometry expansion retained.

## Success criteria

- Tests per transformation; corpus renders equivalently.

## Test plan

- Unit: per-transformation tests (clip-depth adjustment applied exactly once in coordination with 07.8; `gl_FragCoord` y policy; texture orientation; combined-sampler splitting; flat/integer varyings; attribute normalization; explicit buffer layout; `gl_VertexID`/`gl_InstanceID`/`gl_FrontFacing`/`gl_PointSize`/`gl_FragDepth` mappings; point-sprite and wide-line expansion).
- E2E: convention scenes (point sprites with `gl_PointCoord`, front-facing toggles, flat varyings, integer attributes, fragment depth writes) rendered in the forced lane on both browsers vs upstream.
- Logging: per-transformation application events per program and render error metrics; archived under `evidence/15a.4/`.
- Failure artifacts: WGSL and diff images.

## Considerations

- Implicit-derivative sampling under non-uniform control flow is a 15b.1 category (uniformity).
acceptance_criteria: The normalizer applies explicit, tested transformations for every listed difference; sampler splitting and flat varyings compile under WGSL rules; gl_VertexID/gl_InstanceID/gl_FragCoord/gl_FrontFacing/gl_PointSize/gl_FragDepth map to correct WGSL builtins or emulations with tests; point sprites and wide lines are expanded where upstream's contract requires it.

title: Naga dependency admission audit and build-time-only default
description:
## Full scope

Naga dependency admission audit and build-time-only default: exact revision, used API (GLSL frontend entrance, validator, WGSL backend), wasm32 compile result for the optional runtime path, transitive closure, unsafe boundary, incremental bytes, initialization and allocation cost, demonstrated benefit

## Summary

Naga is the preferred narrow compiler dependency; admit it properly and know its runtime cost.

## Background (plan §9.5 "Naga remains the preferred narrow compiler dependency", §13.3, §13.4, §17.3 "Keep debug instrumentation and runtime shader translation dependency-pruned")

## Technical approach

- Fill the admission record; build Naga with `default-features = false` plus only `glsl-in`, `wgsl-out`, validation; measure the wasm32 artifact size and instantiation time for the runtime path.

## Success criteria

- Record committed; measurements recorded.

## Test plan

- Unit: admission-record completeness test (every §13.3 field present); `cargo tree` allowlist check for Naga's feature set (`glsl-in`, `wgsl-out`, validation only).
- E2E: wasm32 build of the optional runtime translation path with size and instantiation time measured in the browser (both browsers).
- Logging: size/init `metric` events `{artifact_bytes, init_ms, browser}`; archived under `evidence/15a.5/`.
- Failure artifacts: the dependency tree diff.

## Considerations

- Never a per-frame dependency.
acceptance_criteria: The admission record for Naga exists with all §13.3 fields; the build uses Naga natively at build time by default; the optional wasm32 runtime build of the translation path is measured (bytes, init time) so F3D-15b.2 can include it only where reachable source behavior needs it.

title: F3D-15 (closure): Full standard ESSL and runtime shader coverage, dynamic hooks, and correctly retained native semantics
description:
## What this epic delivers

Phase 3's shader closure. Plan §19 F3D-15 closure acceptance: "unseen runtime shaders/hooks and correctly retained native semantics".

## Why (plan §5.12 "Legacy and dynamic shaders", §9.4, §9.5, §9.6, §5.16)

"ESSL-to-WGSL and runtime variant handling for portable behavior; genuine GL-dependent contracts run on exact GL, never placeholder shaders." "No blanket 'static shaders only' product mode counts as full compatibility." "A portable program cannot be classified as permanently legacy-only just to avoid completing translation."

## Children

1. Complete ESSL frontend coverage with uniformity transformations.
2. Runtime shader compiler path and dynamic hooks.
3. Nonportable GL program routing to the exact route.
4. Shader optimization legality and conservative comparison.
5. Shader translation fuzzing.

## Success criteria for the epic

All children closed; the manifest's legacy/dynamic shader family is fully owned and tested; new-backend tests generate shaders after startup and after prior variants executed.

## No-claim boundary

A source whose results depend on undefined GPU behavior is not an exact cross-backend reference (§9.4); such cases are documented, not "fixed".
acceptance_criteria: Every official shader (ShaderLib/ShaderChunk/uniform libraries and all addon shaders), every valid ESSL 1.00/3.00 program a source application can produce at runtime, onBeforeCompile hooks, mutable chunk/lib data, custom cache keys and program diagnostics work through the new backend with uniformity transformations; genuinely GL-dependent contracts route to the exact backend with real native objects; shader translation is fuzzed.

title: Complete ESSL 1.00/3.00 frontend coverage with uniformity transformations
description:
## Full scope

Complete ESSL 1.00/3.00 frontend coverage: every official ShaderLib/ShaderChunk program and addon shader with all defines/includes; WGSL uniformity transformations (implicit-derivative texture sampling under non-uniform control flow as an explicit test category); point-size/line expansion completion; documented undefined-behavior cases

## Summary

From the H2 corpus to everything.

## Background (plan §9.4, §5.16)

"ESSL-valid code may still require substantial transformation to satisfy WGSL's uniformity and resource rules. Implicit-derivative texture sampling under nonuniform control flow is an explicit test category. Silencing a uniformity diagnostic is not proof that behavior became portable; either establish an equivalent legal transformation or retain the genuinely required original backend. An unimplemented transformation of defined portable behavior remains a new-backend coverage gap, not an automatic intrinsic exception."

## Technical approach

- Corpus generation from the manifest: every ShaderLib program × its define combinations reachable from material options (bounded via pairwise where combinatorial), every addon shader (`examples/jsm/shaders/*`, postprocessing shaders, `Line2`, `Water`, `Sky`, etc.), unit-test shaders.
- Uniformity: analysis on the AST; transformations such as hoisting derivative-dependent sampling with explicit gradients (`textureSampleGrad`) computed in uniform control flow, or `textureSampleLevel` where the source semantics permit (documented per case); otherwise mark the program's record with the required native evidence.
- Undefined behavior register: cases where the source depends on UB (e.g., uninitialized varyings) documented with the envelope.

## Success criteria

- Corpus green with per-program status; uniformity category tests pass; register committed.

## Test plan

- Unit: golden WGSL for every ShaderLib program × reachable define combination (bounded pairwise where combinatorial), every addon shader and every unit-test shader; uniformity-transformation tests (implicit-derivative sampling under non-uniform control flow → explicit-gradient or level sampling with the documented equivalence) and a test that a silenced-but-untransformed program is rejected; undefined-behavior register entries validated.
- E2E: differential rendering of the corpus (all ShaderLib programs; sampled addon shaders; full uniformity category) in the forced lane on both browsers vs upstream.
- Logging: per-program status `{program, defines, translated|gap|native-evidenced, uniformity_transform}` feeding the manifest; render error metrics; archived under `evidence/15b.1/`.
- Failure artifacts: WGSL, diagnostics and diff images.

## Considerations

- Budget watch: this is the largest uncertainty; report the forecast continuously (§17.1).
acceptance_criteria: The full official shader inventory from the manifest translates, validates and renders equivalently through the new backend; programs requiring uniformity transformations are transformed by an established equivalent legal transformation (or retained on the genuinely required original backend with evidence) rather than silenced; a corpus of valid application-style ESSL programs (from upstream examples and tests) passes; any remaining gap is a new-backend coverage gap in the manifest, never an intrinsic exception.

title: Runtime shader compiler path and dynamic hooks (onBeforeCompile, mutable chunks, cache keys)
description:
## Full scope

Runtime shader compiler path and dynamic hooks: ShaderMaterial/RawShaderMaterial with runtime-generated strings, onBeforeCompile, mutable ShaderChunk/ShaderLib/UniformsLib data, custom cache keys, program errors/diagnostics, program-generation-after-startup tests; the runtime translator is included automatically when reachable with its load/compile cost measured

## Summary

Dynamic programs are required functionality, not a diagnostic.

## Background (plan §9.5, §10.2)

"Preserve `onBeforeCompile`, mutable ShaderChunk/ShaderLib/uniform data, custom cache keys, runtime shader strings, program errors/diagnostics, node registrations and custom builders. Execute hooks at the original logical boundaries and retain exact ordering, current uniforms and effects... Never keep rendering an old shader, a placeholder, a simpler material or a constant node while reporting success. New-backend tests generate graphs/shaders after startup and after prior variants have executed."

## Technical approach

- Runtime translator: the ESSL pipeline compiled to wasm32 (15a.5 measurement) or a JS build of the first-party normalizer plus Naga-wasm; selected by size/latency; loaded lazily but included whenever the closure analysis finds a reachable dynamic shader path (10.7 policy).
- Hook execution: `onBeforeCompile(shader, renderer)` receives the same mutable `shader` object shape upstream provides (vertexShader/fragmentShader strings, uniforms, defines); after the hook the result is translated; `customProgramCacheKey` respected.
- Mutable chunk data: translation reads the live `ShaderChunk`/`ShaderLib` tables at compile time.
- Error contract: compile errors produce the same console/diagnostic behavior as upstream's WebGL path where the source observes it, plus F3D diagnostics.

## Success criteria

- Tests for runtime strings, hooks, chunk mutation, cache keys, errors; latency measured and reported.

## Test plan

- Unit: hook-execution tests (`onBeforeCompile` receives the upstream `shader` object shape; `customProgramCacheKey` respected; live ShaderChunk/ShaderLib mutation observed at compile time); error-contract tests (compile error reproduces upstream's diagnostic shape plus the F3D report); runtime translator packaging test (included iff reachable).
- E2E: `tests/e2e/shaders/runtime.mjs` on both browsers: runtime-generated shader strings after startup and after prior variants executed; chunk mutation mid-run; hook ordering traces vs upstream; translator load/compile latency measured.
- Logging: runtime compile events `{program, trigger, translate_ms, compile_ms, bytes_loaded}` for the interaction-tail report; archived under `evidence/15b.2/`.
- Failure artifacts: the runtime shader source, WGSL and diagnostics.

## Considerations

- Its cost belongs to interaction-tail measurements (§9.5).
acceptance_criteria: An application that generates shader strings at runtime or mutates chunks/hooks works on the new backend with the translator included by the closure analysis; hooks execute at the original logical boundaries with current uniforms and effects; program errors reproduce upstream's error/diagnostic contract plus F3D's separate generated-source report; tests generate new programs after startup and after prior variants executed; the translator's bytes and compile latency are reported.

title: Nonportable GL program routing to the exact route with real native objects
description:
## Full scope

Nonportable GL program routing: genuinely GL-dependent programs (native shader-object callbacks, GL-specific extensions, program-handle observations) execute on the exact GL route with real native objects for error callbacks; portable programs are never classified legacy-only

## Summary

The honest boundary between "hard to translate" and "genuinely native".

## Background (plan §9.5 last two paragraphs, §5.16, §14.10)

"A nonportable GL program or native shader-object callback uses the exact GL route under Section 6.9 rather than a failed feature. A portable program cannot be classified as permanently legacy-only just to avoid completing translation." "Any intrinsic native-backend exception names the concrete observable contract and its real compatible implementation; it cannot be a catch-all category for unfinished rendering."

## Technical approach

- Extend 12a.6's native-contract detection to shader-level observations (e.g., `renderer.debug.onShaderError` receiving `WebGLProgram`, `gl.getProgramInfoLog` use, GL-only extensions referenced in `#extension`).
- Manifest field for the named contract; the release verifier (18a.5) rejects any exception without it.

## Success criteria

- Fixtures route correctly; verifier rule tested.

## Test plan

- Unit: native-contract detection fixtures at shader level (`renderer.debug.onShaderError` receiving `WebGLProgram`, `getProgramInfoLog` use, GL-only `#extension`); verifier-rule test that an exception without a named contract is rejected.
- E2E: exact-lane tests on both browsers where the error callback receives real native objects; a portable program with a translation gap is asserted to remain a new-backend gap in the manifest (not reclassified).
- Logging: route decisions with the named contract; archived under `evidence/15b.3/`.
- Failure artifacts: the decision log.

## Considerations

- Exact-route execution never counts toward new-backend coverage.
acceptance_criteria: The route analysis identifies programs whose semantics require the original GL backend (documented per concrete observable contract) and routes their renderer group exactly; WebGL error callbacks receive real native objects; every such record in the manifest names the observable requirement; portable programs with translation difficulties remain new-backend gaps.

title: Shader optimization legality and conservative comparison
description:
## Full scope

Shader optimization legality: default-allowed transformations (constant propagation, dead-code elimination, inactive-feature specialization, equivalent resource access simplification) vs separately justified ones (floating-point reassociation, reduced precision, changed filtering, changed sample counts, algorithm substitution); a conservative generation path retained and every optimization compared against it

## Summary

Do not turn shader optimization into approximation.

## Background (plan §9.6, §5.4)

"Allowed default transformations include constant propagation, dead code elimination, specialization of inactive material features, and equivalent resource access simplifications. Floating-point reassociation, reduced precision, changed filtering, changed sample counts, and numerical algorithm substitutions require separate justification. Keep a conservative shader-generation path and compare every optimization against it."

## Technical approach

- Pass classification table in the crate docs; feature flag for the optional mode with a report label; differential tests on 14.9 diagnostic targets.

## Success criteria

- Table complete; tests green; optional mode clearly labeled in reports and never in the primary score.

## Test plan

- Unit: pass classification table test (each optimizer pass is allowed-by-default or requires-justification); per-pass differential tests against the conservative generation path over the corpus with 14.9 diagnostic targets; optional-mode labeling test in the report.
- E2E: forced-lane renders with each allowed pass on/off comparing to the conservative path on both browsers.
- Logging: per-pass `metric` events `{pass, program, max_err}`; archived under `evidence/15b.4/`.
- Failure artifacts: diff images per pass.

## Considerations

- FP16 usage is governed by the precision contract (F3D-20.3).
acceptance_criteria: The shader optimizer's pass list is classified into allowed-by-default and requires-justification; the latter are disabled in the primary comparison and available only in a separately labeled optional mode; each enabled pass has a differential test against the conservative path over the shader corpus.

title: Shader preprocessing and translation fuzzing
description:
## Full scope

Shader preprocessing and translation fuzzing: grammar-aware fuzz targets for the ESSL preprocessor, parser, normalizer and WGSL emitter with validation as the oracle; no panics, bounded time and memory, structured errors for invalid input

## Summary

Shader inputs are application-controlled; the translator must be robust.

## Background (plan §14.7 "Fuzz... shader preprocessing/translation")

"Shader input validation and resource/dispatch limits reduce exposure, but do not claim they prove every GPU program terminates within a hard deadline."

## Technical approach

- `cargo-fuzz` targets with a small grammar-aware mutator; time/memory limits; corpus from 15b.1.

## Success criteria

- Fuzz lane green for the budget; findings fixed at root cause.

## Test plan

- Unit/fuzz: `cargo-fuzz` targets for the preprocessor, parser, normalizer and WGSL emitter with a grammar-aware mutator, time and memory limits, and Naga validation as the oracle; seed corpus from 15b.1.
- E2E: none (fuzz lane; may run on RCH).
- Logging: fuzz lane summary `{target, executions, crashes, timeouts, corpus_size}`; archived under `evidence/15b.5/`.
- Failure artifacts: minimized crashing inputs.

## Considerations

- Keep it proportional; no fuzzing framework beyond the standard tool.
acceptance_criteria: Fuzz targets run for a fixed budget without crashes, hangs or unbounded memory; every produced WGSL either validates under Naga or the pipeline reports a structured error; a checked-in corpus seeds the fuzzer from the real shader inventory.

title: F3D-16: Complete TSL/node/backend extension and compute contracts
description:
## What this epic delivers

Closure of the TSL/node/compute family. Plan §19 F3D-16 depends on 14 and 15; acceptance: "Every standard node/general dynamic path; native custom backend routing; callback frequencies".

## Why (plan §5.12 "TSL, nodes and compute", §9.3, §8.7, §12.3, §15.3 H7/H8)

"Complete general lowering and pinned construction components, dynamic graphs included; preserve native extension routes; test unseen runtime graphs and source-valid errors." H7/H8 are the modern-compute headline cells whose difficulty "is part of the project's go/no-go test".

## Children

1. Every standard node export lowering with NodeFrame frequencies and the context stack.
2. Dynamic graph construction runtime lowering and registration.
3. Compute contracts.
4. Native custom backend routing.
5. H7 end-to-end route.
6. H8 end-to-end route.

## Success criteria for the epic

All children closed; the node family in the manifest is fully owned and tested; H7/H8 measured (results published regardless of outcome).

## No-claim boundary

"Simply relocating JavaScript renderer code cannot be assumed to make [H8] 3× faster" (§15.3).
acceptance_criteria: Every standard node export, NodeMaterial/loader/serialization/registration path, Fn/flow/control/type/operator, shader builder and WGSL/GLSL function path, every update frequency, and all storage/atomics/indirect/query/feature-gated compute operations have general lowering through the new backend; dynamic graph construction and custom node registration work at runtime; opaque custom backends route exactly; H7 and H8 have measured end-to-end routes.

title: Every standard node export lowering with NodeFrame frequencies and context stack
description:
## Full scope

Every standard node export lowering: all three/tsl node classes and functions (math/operators/flow control/Fn/types/accessors/lighting/material/texture/display/utils/parsers), NodeMaterial variants, NodeLoader/serialization, node registration; NodeFrame update frequencies for all nodes; reentrant context stack; retained pinned construction helpers where smaller and disclosed

## Summary

Generalize 07.5/15a.3 to the complete node inventory.

## Background (plan §5.12 "TSL, nodes and compute", §9.3)

"All existing standard nodes and portable custom node/registration behavior need working general lowering... Retaining pinned, cold TSL construction helpers or build-time shader-generation components is permitted when smaller and more reliable than rewriting them. That reuse is independent of the separately permitted exact backend component. New-backend validation and scored frames still forbid retained renderer submission."

## Technical approach

- Translator coverage driven by the manifest's node list; for each node: semantic transcription into shader IR or a documented reliance on the retained node builder's generated code (attributed as retained shader construction with byte cost).
- NodeLoader/serialization tests (`toJSON`/`fromJSON` of node materials).
- Registration APIs (`registerNode`, `addMethodChaining`, custom `Node` subclasses) preserved via retained construction modules.

## Success criteria

- Family suite green; coverage report of translated vs retained-builder nodes.

## Test plan

- Unit: translator entry tests per node export (or an explicit retained-builder record with byte cost); NodeMaterial subclass and NodeLoader `toJSON`/`fromJSON` round-trip tests; NodeFrame frequency and context-stack tests for every node kind; registration API tests (`registerNode`, method chaining, custom `Node` subclasses).
- E2E: generated node family suite in the forced lane on both browsers vs upstream's WebGPU renderer over the node examples; translated-vs-retained coverage report asserted complete.
- Logging: per-node `{node, translated|retained-builder, test}` feeding the manifest; render error metrics; archived under `evidence/16.1/`.
- Failure artifacts: IR/WGSL dumps and diff images.

## Considerations

- Graph-construction callbacks remain JavaScript unless admitted (§9.3).
acceptance_criteria: Every node export in the manifest's TSL family has a translator entry (or a disclosed retained-builder fallback that still submits through the new backend) with a positive test; NodeMaterial subclasses and NodeLoader round trips work; update frequencies and the context stack hold for every node kind; the node family tests run in the forced lane.

title: Dynamic node graph construction runtime lowering and registration
description:
## Full scope

Dynamic graph construction runtime lowering: unseen runtime node graphs, custom node registration and builders at runtime, source-valid errors preserved; never substitute a constant or silently retain an old graph; runtime lowering machinery included automatically when reachable with cost reported

## Summary

The node-side twin of 15b.2.

## Background (plan §9.3 last paragraph, §9.5)

"Genuinely dynamic graph construction requires the needed runtime lowering machinery. Every reachable material/control variant in a claimed standalone application must have a valid path: included ahead-of-time code or a disclosed runtime compiler. A shader seen only in a training trace is not the whole variant set."

## Technical approach

- Runtime translator packaging (shared with 15b.2 where possible); closure analysis includes it when dynamic construction is reachable; fallback to the retained node builder is allowed and disclosed.

## Success criteria

- Runtime graph tests green; report shows inclusion and cost.

## Test plan

- Unit: runtime-lowering tests for graphs constructed after startup and for custom node classes registered at runtime; invalid-graph error tests reproducing upstream's error behavior; inclusion-rule test (runtime lowering machinery included iff dynamic construction is reachable).
- E2E: `tests/e2e/nodes/runtime.mjs` on both browsers: new graphs constructed after prior variants executed render correctly through the new backend; bytes/latency of the runtime path measured.
- Logging: runtime lowering events `{graph, nodes, translate_ms, compile_ms}` and inclusion decision in the report; archived under `evidence/16.2/`.
- Failure artifacts: the graph dump and diagnostics.

## Considerations

- A missing custom-node adapter is not a full-product feature exemption (§9.3).
acceptance_criteria: Applications that construct new node graphs after startup (including custom node classes registered at runtime) render them through the new backend; invalid graphs produce upstream's error behavior; tests construct graphs after prior variants executed; the runtime lowering path's bytes/latency are reported.

title: Compute contracts: storage/atomics/indirect/queries, dispatch splitting, bounds, subgroups, FP16 gating
description:
## Full scope

Compute contracts: storage buffers/textures, atomics, indirect dispatch, queries and feature-gated operations; multi-dispatch dependencies with correct synchronization (workgroup barriers do not synchronize a grid); bounds checks and workgroup-tail handling for logical array domains; reduction-order and atomic-ordering contracts; subgroup algorithms with a portable path and partial-group handling; FP16 only under the precision contract; optional immediates as a capability-checked strategy

## Summary

GPU compute done to the plan's rules.

## Background (plan §8.7, §12.3, §5.12 "TSL, nodes and compute")

"A compute shader with global dependencies often needs multiple dispatches. Fusing them without a valid synchronization model is incorrect. Workgroup barriers do not synchronize an entire grid. Bounds checks and workgroup-tail handling preserve logical array domains, including overflow/empty cases; WebGPU robustness is not a substitute for generating the right computation. Do not use nondeterministic atomic ordering or a different reduction tree without satisfying the admitted numeric contract." "Subgroup algorithms need a portable path and must handle partial groups correctly. FP16 is enabled only when the application's precision contract permits it."

## Technical approach

- Compute passes in the pass graph with per-dispatch usage scopes (07.2); dependency analysis on storage accesses to split dispatches; generated bounds checks from logical sizes; reduction templates with fixed order; atomics mapped 1:1 to WGSL atomics.
- Capability gating for subgroups/FP16/immediates (from the record; requested at device creation).

## Success criteria

- Family suite green; invalid-fusion divergence test; tail/empty-domain tests; capability-gating tests on strata with/without features.

## Test plan

- Unit: dependency-splitter tests (a kernel with global dependencies is split into the required dispatches; an invalid fusion fixture diverges from the CPU reference); generated bounds-check tests for logical array domains including overflow/empty cases; reduction-order and atomic tests against the numeric contract; subgroup portable-fallback and partial-group tests; capability-gating tests for FP16/immediates/subgroups.
- E2E: compute family suite in the forced lane on both browsers (storage buffers/textures, atomics, indirect dispatch, queries, feature-gated operations) with readback comparison vs upstream; the divergence test for invalid fusion; strata with and without optional features.
- Logging: per-dispatch events `{kernel, workgroups, splits, features_used}` and readback diffs; archived under `evidence/16.3/`.
- Failure artifacts: readback dumps and the dispatch plan.

## Considerations

- Moving CPU-authored f64 simulation to f32 compute needs a separately admitted precision contract (§8.7).
acceptance_criteria: The compute node/API family renders/executes through the new backend with tests; a kernel with global dependencies is split into the required dispatches (a test proves an invalid fusion diverges); logical array bounds are enforced in generated code (not by relying on robustness); reductions and atomics follow the admitted numeric contract; subgroup features are used only when present with a portable fallback; FP16 and immediates are gated by capability and contract.

title: Native custom backend routing (Backend/Renderer subclasses to the exact component)
description:
## Full scope

Native custom backend routing: legitimate custom Backend/Renderer subclasses and opaque native-handle contracts route to the exact component with actual device/resource objects; name-based shims forbidden

## Summary

Preserve the extension points that make Three.js a platform.

## Background (plan §5.6 second paragraph, §5.12 "Modern renderer/backend APIs")

"Backend-preserving execution also covers legitimate custom `Backend`/`Renderer` subclasses, source-path integrations, runtime shader/backend extensions... For native WebGPU contracts preserve actual device/resource objects through the appropriate component; do not assume arbitrary subclasses can be reproduced by a name-based shim."

## Technical approach

- Router rule: unknown subclass of the pinned backend/renderer classes → exact component (pinned `Renderer` + the subclass's own backend), with the new backend unused for that group; report the reason.

## Success criteria

- Fixture tests pass; report entries correct.

## Test plan

- Unit: router-rule tests (unknown `Backend`/`Renderer` subclass → exact component; explicit `WebGLBackend` → exact; report reasons).
- E2E: custom WebGL backend subclass and custom WebGPU backend subclass fixtures run through the exact machinery on both browsers with real native objects asserted; manifest records updated.
- Logging: route decisions with reasons; archived under `evidence/16.4/`.
- Failure artifacts: the decision log and the fixture's console capture.

## Considerations

- These groups never count toward accelerated coverage.
acceptance_criteria: Applications subclassing Backend/Renderer or injecting custom backends run through the pinned exact machinery with real native objects; the route decision is made at construction; tests cover a custom WebGL backend subclass and a custom WebGPU backend subclass; the manifest records each such contract.

title: H7 end-to-end route (compute skinning instancing individual) and measured throughput
description:
## Full scope

H7 (webgpu_skinning_instancing_individual) end-to-end route: per-instance skeleton/morph storage-buffer data and custom TSL compute skinning through the new backend; automatic transformation, equivalence, and measured completed-frame throughput; candidate gain from pose/update specialization and cross-pass data reuse

## Summary

The first modern-compute headline cell.

## Background (plan §15.2 H7, §15.3, §16.7 "Generalization gate")

"H7 already computes instanced deformation through storage-buffer data and custom TSL, with per-instance skeleton/morph information. It is a serious compatibility and performance test, not a simple crowd rendered through separate naïve draw calls." Generalization gate requires "a measured end-to-end route for H7/H8".

## Technical approach

- Pipeline as 11.1; reference configurations (R0/R2 are the same modern renderer; R1 recipe applied where applicable) frozen; `f3d bench` cell; specialization ideas: pose caching by (clip,time) sharing across instances where the source's per-instance data permits, reuse of skinned outputs across shadow and main passes (legal only if the pass graph proves identical inputs).

## Success criteria

- Results document; feeds G4 and F3D-23.2.

## Test plan

- Unit: none new.
- E2E: build H7; `f3d verify` (including shadows and individual instance variation) on both browsers; `f3d bench` paired runs on the reserved M5, phone and a discrete-GPU stratum when available under protocol v1 with frozen references; ablations for pose caching and cross-pass reuse.
- Logging: raw bench JSON, analysis reports with intervals, ablation deltas, telemetry breakdown; archived under `evidence/16.5/<stratum>/`.
- Failure artifacts: invalidated runs with reasons; verify artifacts.

## Considerations

- Do not remove H7 after disappointing results (§15.2).
acceptance_criteria: H7 builds automatically, passes equivalence (including shadows and individual instance variation), and produces paired throughput results with intervals on the M5 and phone strata (and a discrete-GPU stratum when available) through the new backend; ablations attribute any gain; a result below 2x is reported as such.

title: H8 end-to-end route (MLS-MPM fluid compute) and measured throughput
description:
## Full scope

H8 (webgpu_compute_particles_fluid) end-to-end route: MLS-MPM multi-kernel compute with atomic cell data, indirect dispatch attributes and runtime particle-count changes (default 32,768; storage for 131,072) through the new backend; equivalent compute/data/scheduling plan; device-loss state class recorded as GPU-only simulation

## Summary

The hardest headline cell, measured honestly.

## Background (plan §15.2 H8, §15.3, §11.5, §20 "Modern compute demos remain GPU-bound and <2×")

"Simply relocating JavaScript renderer code cannot be assumed to make it 3× faster." Response if GPU-bound: "Find an equivalent algorithm/data-path improvement or fail launch gate."

## Technical approach

- Pipeline as 11.1 with the compute contracts (16.3); simulation equivalence per §14.5 (chaotic dynamics need a predefined numerical/behavioral contract from 03.6); reference frozen; bench cell; candidate improvements: scheduling of the kernel chain with fewer redundant passes, packed cell data layout, indirect dispatch sizing, all under the numeric contract; no changes to particle count/quality.
- Device loss: classify as "GPU-only simulation → report state loss and follow reset policy" and test it.

## Success criteria

- Results document; device-loss test; feeds G4/F3D-23.2.

## Test plan

- Unit: none new beyond 16.3's compute tests.
- E2E: build H8; `f3d verify` under the temporal/simulation contract (fixed step, seeded, warmup) at default and stress particle counts with runtime count changes on both browsers; `f3d bench` paired runs on the reserved M5 and phone; device-loss injection during simulation asserting the "GPU-only simulation → state loss reported" policy.
- Logging: raw bench JSON, analysis reports, telemetry per kernel `{kernel, dispatches, ms}`, loss-policy events; archived under `evidence/16.6/<stratum>/`.
- Failure artifacts: readbacks of particle/grid buffers at divergence; invalidated runs with reasons.

## Considerations

- A visually similar image is not a precision contract (§8.7).
acceptance_criteria: H8 builds automatically, passes equivalence under the temporal/simulation contract (fixed-step, seeded, warmup), runs at default and stress particle counts with runtime changes, and produces paired throughput results with intervals on the M5 and phone strata through the new backend; the report identifies any equivalent compute/data-path improvement or documents that the case is GPU-bound; device loss reports state loss per the §11.5 table.

title: F3D-17: All pass/effect families, histories, resource reuse and copies/readbacks
description:
## What this epic delivers

Phase 3's pass/effect closure and the pass-graph optimizer. Plan §19 F3D-17 depends on 14 and 16; acceptance: "Complete new-backend applicable coverage plus exact sync/native integration".

## Why (plan §5.12 "Postprocessing and special effects", §8.2 "Pass/resource planning", §8.5, §8.6, §15.4)

"Execute complete passes conservatively before optimizing; same reset/disposal/resize/order; custom/native pass interaction retains exact resource group." "Reuse compatible texture objects across disjoint lifetimes, eliminate genuinely dead passes, and preserve necessary history."

## Children

1. EffectComposer/Pass family closure.
2. Pass-graph optimization (transient reuse, dead passes, history, hazards).
3. Postprocessing fusion legality.
4. Copies and readbacks contract.
5. Temporal effects and the VXGI Sponza case.
6. H4/H6 end-to-end routes.
7. GPU-history device-loss recovery classes.

## Success criteria for the epic

All children closed; the postprocessing family in the manifest is fully owned and tested in the forced lane; `f3d-graph` line count reported against 14,000.

## No-claim boundary

Fusion and reuse are optimizations behind legality rules; conservative execution is the reference.
acceptance_criteria: The entire EffectComposer/Pass family and every official pass/shader, output conversion, masks/stencil, ping-pong/history, bloom/AO/SSR/SSGI/DOF/AA/upscaling, custom passes and stereo/anaglyph/ASCII/outline effects execute through the new backend with the same reset/disposal/resize/order semantics; pass-graph optimization reuses resources and eliminates dead passes legally; copies and readbacks follow their own validation; temporal effects and VXGI Sponza pass; H4 and H6 have measured routes; GPU-history device-loss classes are implemented.

title: EffectComposer/Pass family closure executed conservatively first
description:
## Full scope

EffectComposer and Pass family closure: every official pass and shader (RenderPass, ShaderPass, all bloom/AO/SSR/SSGI/DOF/AA/upscaling/outline/mask/texture/film/glitch/etc. passes, OutputPass conversion, MaskPass/ClearMaskPass stencil), the node-based PostProcessing/RenderPipeline path, custom passes, stereo/anaglyph/ASCII effects; executed conservatively first with identical reset/disposal/resize/order behavior; custom or native pass interaction retains the exact resource group

## Summary

All the passes, conservatively correct first.

## Background (plan §5.12 "Postprocessing and special effects", §5.16)

"Standard dynamic GLSL/TSL programs, public subclass/registration mechanisms, and custom passes that use portable APIs require the generic new execution path, with original execution preserved for cases whose actual semantics need it."

## Technical approach

- Retain the `EffectComposer`/`Pass` construction modules; each official pass's shaders translate via 15b.1; its render logic maps to pass-graph passes with explicit attachment ops; ping-pong buffers as versioned resources; `MaskPass` stencil ops explicit.
- Node-based `PostProcessing` maps through 16.1.
- Custom pass support: a `Pass` subclass calling `renderer.render`/`setRenderTarget` executes through the general path.

## Success criteria

- Family suite green; H6 equivalence; upstream postprocessing examples pass in the forced lane.

## Test plan
