- Unit: composer semantics tests (read/write buffer swap, `renderToScreen`, `setSize`, `dispose`, `enabled`/`needsSwap`/`clear` flags) against a Node oracle where possible; per-pass shader translation snapshots; `MaskPass` stencil op tests; node-based `PostProcessing` mapping tests.
- E2E: generated pass family suite in the forced lane on both browsers vs upstream over every official pass and the postprocessing examples; a custom `Pass` subclass fixture using portable APIs; a native-contract pass fixture keeping its exact resource group; H6 equivalence.
- Logging: per-pass `{pass, owner, route, max_err}` feeding the manifest; archived under `evidence/17.1/`.
- Failure artifacts: per-pass diff images and the pass-graph dump.

## Considerations

- Conservative execution first (§5.12); fusion is 17.3.
acceptance_criteria: Every postprocessing manifest record has new-WebGPU-path status with a positive test in the forced lane; composer semantics (read/write buffer swap, renderToScreen, setSize, dispose, pass enabled/needsSwap/clear flags) match upstream; custom application passes using portable APIs execute generically; passes that reach native GL contracts keep an exact resource group.

title: Pass-graph optimization: transient reuse, dead passes, history, hazards
description:
## Full scope

Pass-graph optimization: transient texture reuse across disjoint lifetimes, dead-pass elimination, history preservation; reuse only after the old logical contents have no remaining consumers and the queued order is valid; persistent histories, pending readbacks, aliased views and source-visible render targets prevent transient reuse; mapping/staging credits with their own completion requirements

## Summary

Resource-object reuse that respects every consumer.

## Background (plan §8.2 "Pass/resource planning", §8.5 "Resource reuse is allowed only...")

"This is resource-object reuse, not a claim that the browser exposes arbitrary native heap aliasing." "Resource reuse is allowed only after the old logical contents have no remaining consumers and the queued order is valid. Persistent histories, pending readbacks, aliased views, and source-visible render targets prevent inappropriate transient reuse. Mapping/staging credits have their own completion requirements."

## Technical approach

- Lifetime analysis over the scheduled pass list; transient pool (07.1) with compatibility keys; consumers include readback commands and CPU-visible targets (any `WebGLRenderTarget` the application holds is source-visible unless proven unobserved).
- Dead-pass elimination requires proof that no observable effect (callbacks, node updates, readbacks) depends on the pass (§8.5: "skip the entire operation only if its effects are also proven absent").

## Success criteria

- Counterexamples pass; H6 shows reduced transient memory with identical output.

## Test plan

- Unit: lifetime-analysis tests over scheduled pass lists; counterexample tests proving that a source-visible target, a pending readback, an aliased view or a history dependency blocks reuse; dead-pass elimination requires proof of no observable effect (callback/node-update/readback fixtures keep the pass).
- E2E: H6 and postprocessing examples in the forced lane on both browsers with identical output and reduced transient memory (telemetry); ablation toggle verified.
- Logging: reuse decisions `{resource, reused_for, reason}` and transient-pool stats; archived under `evidence/17.2/`.
- Failure artifacts: the plan diff and diff images.

## Considerations

- Copy commands have their own validation (§8.5).
acceptance_criteria: The graph optimizer reuses compatible transient textures across disjoint lifetimes and removes provably dead passes while preserving observable renders, histories and readbacks; counterexample tests prove that a source-visible target, a pending readback, an aliased view or a history dependency blocks reuse; the optimization has an ablation toggle and a legality statement.

title: Postprocessing fusion legality with preserved quantization boundaries
description:
## Full scope

Postprocessing fusion legality: a legality rule covering sampling, precision, blending, history, derivatives and texture-format boundaries; required intermediate quantization and sampling boundaries preserved; register-pressure/duplicate-sampling profiling before enabling a fusion

## Summary

Fusion without changing the picture.

## Background (plan §5.5 last paragraph, §8.6 last paragraph)

"A fused shader must preserve required intermediate quantization and sampling boundaries. Two full-screen passes are not necessarily equivalent to their algebraic composition evaluated at higher precision." "A fusion that increases shader register pressure or duplicate sampling may lose; profile it."

## Technical approach

- Fusion candidates from the graph (adjacent full-screen passes with 1:1 texel mapping, no history, matching formats); explicit re-quantization to the intermediate format inside the fused shader; profiling harness per device.

## Success criteria

- Legality tests; profiles recorded; no fusion in the primary score unless it passes both.

## Test plan

- Unit: fusion legality tests (sampling, precision, blending, history, derivatives, format boundaries); a quantization test showing two full-screen passes composed at higher precision diverge from the reference while the fused path with explicit re-quantization matches.
- E2E: fused vs conservative renders in the forced lane on both browsers with 14.9 diagnostic targets; per-device profiling of each fusion (register pressure/duplicate sampling) recorded and fusions disabled where they lose.
- Logging: per-fusion `metric` events `{fusion, device, ms_fused, ms_conservative, enabled: bool, max_err}`; archived under `evidence/17.3/`.
- Failure artifacts: diff images.

## Considerations

- Keep the conservative path as reference.
acceptance_criteria: Pass fusion is applied only when the rule proves equivalence including intermediate quantization (a test shows two full-screen passes composed at higher precision diverge from the reference and that the fused path preserves the boundary); each fusion is profiled and disabled where it loses; ablation toggle exists.

title: Copies and readbacks contract (encoded copies, mapAsync, sync reads exact-only, real transfers)
description:
## Full scope

Copies and readbacks: buffer/texture copy commands with their own validation and row-pitch rules, copyTextureToTexture/copyFramebufferToTexture equivalents, asynchronous readback via mapAsync with staging lifetimes, readRenderTargetPixelsAsync on the new backend, synchronous readback only on the exact route, explicit real-copy transfer between exact and new-backend groups with measured cost

## Summary

Data movement with the right validation model per operation.

## Background (plan §6.8, §6.9 last paragraphs, §5.6, §23 [S25], [S45])

"Alignment rules belong to the actual operation... encoded buffer-to-texture copies have a separate row-pitch constraint... [do not] assume mapped buffers may simultaneously participate in GPU work." "No zero-copy interchange between `WebGLTexture` and `GPUTexture` is assumed... an explicit supported transfer uses real copies, lawful synchronization and measured costs, not transparent per-draw ping-pong."

## Technical approach

- Copy pass kind with validation; staging lifecycle states; async readback API integration with retirement epochs (22a.5); exact↔new transfer through CPU bytes with telemetry.

## Success criteria

- Tests per operation; the native-context ownership counterexample (05.7) extended with the supported transfer.

## Test plan

- Unit: copy-pass validation tests (bytesPerRow alignment for encoder copies; `writeTexture` layout separate); staging lifecycle-state tests (mapped buffers never participate in GPU work); async readback generation checks; exact↔new transfer accounting tests.
- E2E: copy/readback family suite on both browsers (`copyTextureToTexture`, `copyFramebufferToTexture` equivalents, `readRenderTargetPixelsAsync`, staging reuse); the native-context ownership counterexample extended with the supported real-copy transfer; a sync-read on a new-backend renderer is shown to have been routed exactly at construction.
- Logging: per-copy events `{kind, bytes, alignment, staging_state}` and transfer cost `metric` events; archived under `evidence/17.4/`.
- Failure artifacts: readback dumps.

## Considerations

- Mandatory readback checkpoints for recovery have a real cost (§11.5).
acceptance_criteria: Every copy/readback manifest record has an owner with tests; encoded copies respect bytesPerRow alignment; mapped staging buffers never participate in GPU work while mapped; async readback returns correct data with generation checks; sync readback APIs on a new-backend renderer are routed exactly at construction (never faked); the supported exact-to-new transfer is a real copy with its cost reported.

title: Temporal effects (SSGI/TRAA) and the VXGI Sponza fidelity case
description:
## Full scope

Temporal effects and the VXGI Sponza case: SSGI/TRAA history buffers with correct invalidation, warmup, fixed-step and seeded inputs; temporal consistency comparisons; webgpu_vxgi_sponza (voxel cone-traced GI, MRT, TAA, large assets via the locked external index, first-person control) passes equivalence

## Summary

The temporal fidelity cases that catch history bugs.

## Background (plan §15.4, §14.5 last paragraph, §10.5)

"For temporal renderers and simulations, preserve warmup, history, fixed-step policy, and random inputs. Chaotic dynamics require a predefined numerical/behavioral contract." Sponza "explicitly combines VXGI and temporal antialiasing and fetches its asset through an external model index, so both its render graph and asset closure are material parts of the test."

## Technical approach

- History resources as persistent versioned resources excluded from transient reuse; invalidation events mirrored from upstream's logic; equivalence at logical frames with temporal consistency metrics.

## Success criteria

- Three cases pass; Sponza standalone artifact passes the packaging harness with the index locked.

## Test plan

- Unit: history-resource exclusion tests (never transient-reused); invalidation-event mirroring tests (resize/camera cut as upstream does); temporal-consistency metric tests on synthetic sequences.
- E2E: `f3d verify` on `webgpu_postprocessing_ssgi`, `webgpu_postprocessing_traa` and `webgpu_vxgi_sponza` under the temporal contract (history preserved, warmup identical, invalidation on resize/cut) on both browsers; Sponza standalone artifact through the packaging harness with the index locked.
- Logging: per-frame temporal metrics `{frame, consistency, history_invalidated}` and the standalone request log; archived under `evidence/17.5/`.
- Failure artifacts: frame sequences from both sides and diffs.

## Considerations

- Scored separately from the headline gate (§15.4).
acceptance_criteria: webgpu_postprocessing_ssgi, webgpu_postprocessing_traa and webgpu_vxgi_sponza pass the fidelity profile with the temporal contract from the protocol (history preserved, invalidated on resize/camera cut as upstream does, warmup identical); results are published in the fidelity set.

title: H4 and H6 end-to-end routes and measured throughput
description:
## Full scope

H4 (webgl_shadowmap_performance) and H6 (webgl_postprocessing_advanced) end-to-end routes: automatic transformation, equivalence, and measured completed-frame throughput under the frozen protocol; gains attributed to legal batching/dirty dependencies/shared cross-pass work (H4) and legal graph specialization/traffic reduction (H6)

## Summary

Two more headline cells.

## Background (plan §15.2 H4/H6, §16.8)

H4: "Legal batching, dirty dependencies, shared work across passes." H6: "Legal graph specialization and resource/traffic reduction."

## Technical approach

- As 13.8, with frozen references extended to H4/H6.

## Success criteria

- Results documents; feeds G4/F3D-23.2.

## Test plan

- Unit: none new.
- E2E: build H4 and H6; `f3d verify` on both browsers; `f3d bench` paired runs on the reserved M5 and phone under protocol v1 with frozen references; ablation toggles for shadow caching/batching (H4) and pass-graph optimization/fusion (H6).
- Logging: raw bench JSON, analysis reports with intervals, ablation deltas; archived under `evidence/17.6/<stratum>/`.
- Failure artifacts: invalidated runs with reasons; verify artifacts.

## Considerations

- Shadow caching must still run source-required callbacks (14.3).
acceptance_criteria: H4 and H6 build automatically, pass equivalence, and produce paired throughput results with intervals on the M5 and phone strata through the new backend; ablations attribute gains; results below 2x are reported as such.

title: GPU-history device-loss recovery classes with charged checkpoint costs
description:
## Full scope

GPU-history device-loss recovery classes: immutable/CPU-authoritative resources recreated from current authoritative versions; GPU state with a sufficient checkpoint replayed only under the specified numeric/input-history contract; GPU-only simulation, accumulated history or uncaptured output reported as state loss with an explicit reset/restart/error policy; checkpoint readback cost charged

## Summary

Device loss is not necessarily state recovery, and the plan says exactly how to be honest about it.

## Background (plan §11.5)

| State class | Valid recovery action |
|---|---|
| Immutable packed assets or CPU-authoritative data | Recreate allocations and upload the current authoritative version |
| GPU state with a sufficient checkpoint and admitted replay | Restore/replay only under the specified numeric and input-history contract |
| GPU-only simulation, accumulated render history, or uncaptured output | Report state loss and follow an explicit reset/restart/error policy |
"A snapshot of the initial scene cannot reconstruct the current fluid simulation... A reset is visible application behavior and cannot be described as seamless state preservation."

## Technical approach

- Classification field on graph resources; recovery driver in `f3d-gpu` invoked by 22a.3's device replacement; optional checkpoint policy with measured cost.

## Success criteria

- Tests for each class on SSGI/TRAA history and H8.

## Test plan

- Unit: classification tests (every persistent graph resource assigned one §11.5 class); recovery-driver tests with a fake device (class 1 recreated from authoritative versions; class 2 replayed only under contract; class 3 reports loss).
- E2E: device-loss injection during SSGI/TRAA history accumulation and H8 simulation on both browsers asserting reconstruction success, admitted reset, unrecoverable loss and deliberate teardown outcomes; checkpoint policy cost measured where enabled.
- Logging: recovery events `{resource, class, action, outcome, checkpoint_bytes}`; archived under `evidence/17.7/`.
- Failure artifacts: the resource classification dump and the post-recovery frame.

## Considerations

- Feeds 22b.1.
acceptance_criteria: Every persistent GPU resource in the pass graph is classified into one of the three §11.5 classes; loss during a temporal effect or H8 follows the class policy with tests distinguishing reconstruction success, admitted reset, unrecoverable loss and deliberate teardown; any checkpoint readback cost appears in the results.

title: F3D-18 (early slice): Mapped unchanged upstream tests and the feature-gate machinery, started immediately
description:
## What this epic delivers

The test infrastructure the plan says must "start mapped upstream tests immediately" in Phase 1 and "accrue coverage continuously". Plan §19 F3D-18 early prerequisite is 04.

## Why (plan §2.4, §14.1–14.4, §14.10, §18 Phase 1)

"FrankenThreeD therefore needs both the complete upstream test inventory and a separate real-device comparison harness." "Run separate production-route lanes: full functional routing; forced new-backend execution for all applicable rendering cases; and exact native-backend integration."

## Children

1. Candidate module-resolution tree for unchanged upstream tests
2. Core and addon unit suites against the candidate with strict failure rules and owners
3. E2E screenshot oracle lane (upstream-shaped, thresholds unchanged, never a perf lane)
4. Three production-route lanes in f3d-conformance (functional, forced new-backend, exact)
5. Manifest status updater, release-verifier rules and f3d verify-upstream
6. Semantic utility surfaces for internal-utility tests (WebGLRenderLists etc.)
7. f3d verify: original-vs-candidate equivalence runner with structured evidence and failure artifacts

## Success criteria for the epic

All children closed; the lanes run locally via repository-owned commands (DSR wiring), not hosted CI.

## No-claim boundary

Green upstream suites are necessary and insufficient (§14.1).
acceptance_criteria: A candidate module-resolution tree runs the unchanged upstream core and addon unit suites and the upstream-shaped E2E screenshot lane against the production compatibility exports with strict failure rules and per-result ownership; the three production-route lanes exist in f3d-conformance; the manifest status updater and release-verifier rules are implemented; f3d verify-upstream runs them.

title: Candidate module-resolution tree for unchanged upstream tests
description:
## Full scope

Candidate module-resolution tree for upstream tests: redirect every upstream import path (package names and src-level paths such as those in test/unit/three.source.unit.js) to the production compatibility exports through a mapped working copy/resolver; original test bodies, expected values and assertions untouched; the oracle checkout never edited; resolved implementation recorded per import

## Summary

Run the real tests against the real product without touching either.

## Background (plan §14.2, §2.4, §23 [S27])

"Create a candidate module-resolution tree that redirects the upstream source import paths to the production compatibility exports. Keep the original test bodies, expected values, and assertions intact. Use a mapped working copy/resolver without editing the upstream oracle checkout. Record the resolved implementation for every import. Retained modules and exact renderer components are allowed only as declared production owners in the full functional lane. Hidden/test-only delegation is forbidden."

## Technical approach

- Generate the mapped working copy: symlinks/copies of the test tree plus a resolver (Node loader hook / import map for browser tests) mapping `../../src/...` and `three` paths to the candidate build's corresponding routed modules (04.2 routing table); the mapping is derived from the manifest so every src path has a target.
- Resolution log per import; assertion that no import resolved to the untouched oracle renderer (an accidental oracle import counts toward nothing, §14.2).

## Success criteria

- All unit test modules load under the mapping; log shows owners; an injected oracle import is detected.

## Test plan

- Unit: resolver tests (package name, `../../src/...` relative paths, addon paths → routed candidate modules from the routing table); oracle-import detector test (an injected import of the untouched upstream renderer is flagged).
- E2E: dry run of the mapped working copy loading every unit test module under Node and the browser runner without executing assertions; the resolution log covers every import.
- Logging: per-import `{test_module, specifier, resolved, package, revision, instance, submission_path}`; oracle imports at `error`; archived under `evidence/18a.1/`.
- Failure artifacts: the unresolved/oracle import list.

## Considerations

- Test-only aliases are forbidden; the mapped targets are the production modules.
acceptance_criteria: The upstream test runner executes from a mapped working copy where imports resolve to the candidate's routed modules (retained/facade/exact as declared production owners) without modifying the oracle tree or any test file; a per-import resolution log records package, source revision, instance and (for renderers) submission path.

title: Core and addon unit suites against the candidate with strict failure rules and owners
description:
## Full scope

Core and addon unit suites against the candidate: every active upstream test imported and executed in its required environment; syntax/import/setup errors, assertion-count shortfalls and unhandled rejections fail the inventory; candidate-only skips are failures; upstream skips stay visible as unproven; every result records its implementation owner

## Summary

Strict execution of the whole unit inventory with honest bookkeeping.

## Background (plan §14.3; AGENTS.md "Upstream suite")

"Every active upstream test must be imported and executed in its required environment. Syntax/import/setup errors, assertion-count shortfalls, and unhandled rejections fail the inventory rather than becoming empty successful suites. A candidate-only skip is a failure. An upstream-existing skip remains visible as an unproven upstream case, not a new pass."

## Technical approach

- Runner wrapper around upstream's QUnit setup executing in Node and/or browser as upstream requires; assertion counting compared with 01.4's expectations; owner tagging via the resolution log + runtime attribution (07.6 when rendering is involved).
- Output: JSON results per test with owner and status categories (pass, fail, upstream-skip, candidate-skip=fail, host-blocked with reference evidence).

## Success criteria

- Lane runs; initial results (mostly retained owners) recorded honestly; failures listed.

## Test plan

- Unit: runner-wrapper tests with synthetic modules (assertion-count shortfall fails; candidate-only skip fails; upstream skip stays visible as unproven; unhandled rejection fails; setup error fails).
- E2E: full core and addon unit lanes against the candidate in Node and the browser as upstream requires, on Chrome and Safari for browser-required modules; counts reconciled against 01.4's inventory (no silent shrinkage).
- Logging: per-test results `{test, status: pass|fail|upstream-skip|candidate-skip-fail|host-blocked, owner, route, assertions_expected, assertions_run}`; lane summary by status and owner; archived under `evidence/18a.2/`.
- Failure artifacts: the failing test's output and the resolution log entry for its imports.

## Considerations

- Do not "fix" upstream tests; a failing test is a candidate defect or an honest gap.
acceptance_criteria: The unit lanes run to completion with per-test results tagged by owner (new Rust/WebGPU, general new backend, retained JS, exact component, unresolved); the inventory counts from 01.4 are reconciled against executed tests (no silent shrinkage); the run fails on any of the listed conditions; results feed the manifest status updater.

title: E2E screenshot oracle lane (upstream-shaped, thresholds unchanged, never a perf lane)
description:
## Full scope

E2E screenshot oracle lane: the upstream-shaped regression lane with its fixed configuration (software Vulkan ICD, launch flags), unchanged expected assets and thresholds (per-pixel rule, 0.1% different-pixel limit), running examples through the candidate; never a performance lane; goldens never regenerated from the candidate

## Summary

Keep the upstream screenshot lane exactly as a regression oracle.

## Background (plan §14.4, §14.6, §2.4)

"Keep an upstream-shaped regression lane for reproducibility, including its fixed configuration where appropriate. Do not treat it as a performance lane." "The inspected E2E configuration uses its own per-pixel error rule and a 0.1% different-pixel limit; FrankenThreeD must not loosen that threshold to pass."

## Technical approach

- Reuse the pinned `test/e2e/puppeteer.js` flow through the mapping; the candidate's examples are the routed build's example pages (for accelerated ones, the transformed artifacts); route attribution tagged per example.

## Success criteria

- Lane runs; results honest; exclusions listed for 18b to supplement.

## Test plan

- Unit: configuration-preservation test (ICD selection, launch flags, per-pixel rule and 0.1% limit read from the pinned runner and asserted unchanged).
- E2E: the upstream E2E flow over candidate-mapped examples with the unchanged expected images; upstream exclusions preserved and listed separately; route attribution per example.
- Logging: per-example `{example, route, owner, pixel_diff_ratio, result}` and the exclusion list; a header line stating "regression oracle, not performance"; archived under `evidence/18a.3/`.
- Failure artifacts: candidate screenshot and diff against the upstream expected image (goldens never regenerated).

## Considerations

- Software ICD results can never substantiate a hardware speedup claim.
acceptance_criteria: The upstream E2E runner configuration is reproduced against the candidate-mapped examples with unchanged thresholds and expected images; upstream exclusions are preserved and separately listed; results are tagged with owner/route and labeled "regression oracle, not performance".

title: Three production-route lanes in f3d-conformance (functional, forced new-backend, exact)
description:
## Full scope

Three production-route lanes in f3d-conformance: full functional routing; forced new-backend execution with retained renderer submission disabled; exact native-backend integration with real GL contexts, sync reads, native handles and context loss/restore; separate reporting, no substitution between lanes

## Summary

The lane structure that prevents both hidden gaps and a fake accelerated wrapper.

## Background (plan §14.1 last paragraph; AGENTS.md "Three production-route lanes")

"Run all three separately. They cannot substitute for each other."

## Technical approach

- `f3d-conformance` crate (Rust orchestration + JS harness invocation) with lane definitions, result schemas and the per-family coverage matrix (import/symbol, behavior, new-backend rendering, exact integration, capable-host) kept as separate columns.

## Success criteria

- Lanes run on the current slice; matrix has no merged totals.
- `f3d-conformance/CONTRACT.md` is written before any other crate depends on `f3d-conformance` (AGENTS.md "Documentation and Contracts"): purpose and position in the dependency direction, public types and semantics, invariants, implementation ownership route, error model, determinism and numeric-fidelity class, cancellation behavior, unsafe boundary if any, feature flags, conformance tests, and no-claim boundaries.

## Test plan

- Unit: lane-definition tests (lane 2 refuses retained submission; lane 3 asserts native objects; the coverage matrix keeps five separate columns and refuses to merge them).
- E2E: all three lanes run on the current slice via the repository-owned commands (DSR wiring) with separate result files; a family cannot be marked covered by a lane that did not execute it (test with a synthetic result set).
- Logging: per-lane summaries `{lane, executed, passed, failed, owners}` and the coverage matrix JSON; archived under `evidence/18a.4/`.
- Failure artifacts: lane result files.

## Considerations

- DSR is the required runner for repo-level gates (AGENTS.md); wire the commands.
acceptance_criteria: f3d-conformance exposes three lane runners with separate result files; lane 2 refuses retained submission (07.6) and lists portable families it covers; lane 3 asserts native objects; a family cannot be marked covered by a lane that did not execute it.

title: Manifest status updater, release-verifier rules and f3d verify-upstream
description:
## Full scope

Manifest status updater, release-verifier rules and f3d verify-upstream: per-record functional status, new-WebGPU-path status and owner updated from lane results; blocking states enforced; separate coverage numbers; verifier fails on unmatched source/export path, feature without implementation/behavioral test, candidate-specific valid-input refusal, placeholder/no-op substitution, unexplained extra skip, incomplete runtime codec/variant closure, or known functional regression

## Summary

The manifest as a living, evidence-backed status record, and the verifier that keeps it honest.

## Background (plan §5.15, §14.10; AGENTS.md "THE NO-CUT RULE")

"`unclassified`, `unimplemented`, `untested`, `known-regression`, `stub`, `no-op-substitute`, and `candidate-refusal-on-valid-source` are blocking states. `retained` describes ownership, not an automatic pass. `host-blocked` requires the reference to have the same missing prerequisite... Use separate coverage numbers for import/symbol closure, validated behavior families, new-backend rendering coverage, exact-component integration, and capable-host validation. Do not average them into a single flattering '100%' number."

## Technical approach

- Updater: joins lane results (18a.2/18a.3/18a.4, later 18b) to manifest records by test references; sets statuses; records evidence pointers.
- Verifier rules as a small function list over the manifest; output JSON + text.
- Remember AGENTS.md: the manifest is one data file inside existing tooling, not a service.

## Success criteria

- Verifier runs on the current manifest and reports the (large) honest gap list; each rule has a unit test with a fixture.

## Test plan

- Unit: updater join tests (lane results → manifest statuses with evidence pointers); one fixture per verifier rule (unmatched path, missing test, valid-input refusal, stub/no-op substitution, unexplained extra skip, incomplete codec/variant closure, known regression) that must fail; a test that no output line contains a merged percentage.
- E2E: `f3d verify-upstream --ref r186 --features all --tests all` on the current manifest producing the honest gap list and the five separate coverage numbers.
- Logging: per-record status transitions `{record, from, to, evidence}` and the verifier's rule verdicts; archived under `evidence/18a.5/`.
- Failure artifacts: the rule-violation list with record ids.

## Considerations

- Existing upstream TODO/skips do not waive the corresponding feature's candidate test obligation.
acceptance_criteria: f3d verify-upstream --ref r186 --features all --tests all runs the lanes, updates the manifest statuses from evidence, prints the five coverage numbers separately, and exits non-zero on any §14.10 invariant violation; no averaging into a single percentage exists anywhere in the output.

title: Semantic utility surfaces for internal-utility tests (WebGLRenderLists etc.)
description:
## Full scope

Semantic utility surfaces for internal-utility tests: provide the same semantic utility surface for internal classes the upstream tests import directly (for example WebGLRenderLists, WebGLAttributes-style helpers, node builder internals) without forcing the optimized renderer to use them as its hot-path representation

## Summary

Compatible utilities and a private packed schedule can coexist.

## Background (plan §14.2 second paragraph, §23 [S28])

"For internal utilities such as `WebGLRenderLists`, supply the same semantic utility surface when required by the test contract, without requiring the optimized renderer to use that utility as its hot-path representation. A compatible utility and a private packed render schedule can coexist. The inspected tests assert exact object structure and identity-related behavior, making this distinction necessary."

## Technical approach

- Route those source paths to the retained upstream utility modules (they are cold); ensure identity coherence with the shared core.

## Success criteria

- The relevant upstream tests pass; owner recorded as retained.

## Test plan

- Unit: identity-coherence tests for the retained internal utilities against the shared core (same constructors across facade and utility imports).
- E2E: the upstream tests importing `WebGLRenderLists`, attribute helpers and node-builder internals pass in the mapped lane with `owner: retained-js`; the new backend's private schedule is asserted untouched (07.7 counters show no use of the utility in the hot path).
- Logging: per-test owner tags and utility identity checks; archived under `evidence/18a.6/`.
- Failure artifacts: the failing assertion's object-structure diff.

## Considerations

- Directly importable internal classes get their actual compatibility implementation (§5.11 item 2).
acceptance_criteria: Upstream unit tests that import renderer-internal utilities pass against the candidate's routed modules with exact object structure and identity behavior as asserted, while the new backend keeps its private packed render schedule; the manifest records these utilities as retained public source-path utilities.

title: f3d verify: original-vs-candidate equivalence runner with structured evidence and failure artifacts
description:
## Full scope

`f3d verify <original> --candidate <artifact>`: the original-vs-candidate equivalence runner that executes the shared deterministic harness on both sides, compares visual/state/control/lifecycle profiles at logical checkpoints under the preregistered tolerances, emits structured JSON-lines evidence with owner/route tags and failure artifacts, and exits non-zero on any divergence.

## Summary

The plan's proposed command surface includes `f3d verify ./index.html --candidate ./dist/demo.html` (§3.2) and the gates require "every scored application also passes image/state/interaction checks before timing results count" (§1.3). No bead owned the runner itself; 11.3, 18b.3 and the packaging harness all need it.

## Background (plan §3.2, §14.5, §14.6, §16.6 "Equivalence", §1.3)

Compare event/state traces and visual results at corresponding logical times; specify causal order rather than wall-clock arrival; excluded diagnostic pixels are narrowly identified; goldens come only from the reference; tolerances are preregistered (03.6).

## Technical approach

- `f3d-cli` subcommand wired to `f3d-conformance`: launches original and candidate under the harness (03.1) with the same seed and input script, collects checkpoints, runs the comparison library (14.9's checks: color-space-aware metric, edge/silhouette, region, diagnostic targets when available, temporal consistency), diffs event/state traces with causal-order rules, and applies lifecycle steps (resize, dispose, reload).
- Profiles: a per-case `verify.toml` (from the corpus manifest) listing checkpoints, tolerance set, excluded diagnostic regions, required controls.
- Output: `evidence/verify/<case>/<run>/` with `events.jsonl`, `summary.json`, `artifacts/` (reference/candidate/diff images, trace diffs); text and JSON to stdout; exit code documented.
- Lanes: runs in functional, forced-new-backend (with the route assertion) and exact lanes by flag.

## Success criteria

- `f3d verify` on H1/H2 reproduces 11.3's results; a deliberately perturbed candidate (one wrong pixel region, one reordered event) fails with the correct artifact and message.

## Test plan

- Unit: comparison library tests (metrics, region exclusion, causal-order trace diff) on synthetic fixtures; CLI argument, profile-loading and exit-code tests; a test that tolerances cannot be loosened without the `--unscored` label appearing in output.
- E2E: `tests/e2e/verify/h1.mjs` and `h2.mjs` on both browsers reproducing 11.3's outcomes; perturbation fixtures (one wrong pixel region; one reordered event; one skipped lifecycle step) that must fail with the right artifact and message.
- Logging: per-checkpoint events `{checkpoint, metric, observed, expected, tolerance, artifact}`; summary lists the first divergence; archived under `evidence/verify/<case>/`.
- Failure artifacts: reference/candidate/diff images, trace diff, capability record.

## Considerations

- Never loosen a tolerance to pass (§14.6); tolerances are read from protocol v1 and cannot be overridden on the command line without an explicit `--unscored` label in the output.
acceptance_criteria: f3d verify runs both sides under the shared harness, compares visual/state/control/lifecycle profiles at logical checkpoints under preregistered tolerances, writes JSON-lines evidence and failure artifacts, exits non-zero on divergence, and reproduces the H1/H2 equivalence results; perturbed candidates fail correctly.

title: F3D-18 (closure): Full feature gates and unchanged upstream tests, every source/behavior entry covered, positive tests beyond TODO/skips, no ownership laundering
description:
## What this epic delivers

Phase 4's feature-gate closure. Plan §19 F3D-18 closure "uses 12–17"; acceptance: "Every source/behavior entry covered; positive tests beyond TODO/skips; no ownership laundering".

## Why (plan §14.9, §14.10, §18 Phase 4, §22)

"From the single feature manifest, require an executable positive case for every existing callable/option/behavior family and the relevant invalid-input, mutation, serialization and lifecycle cases." "The release verifier fails on an unmatched source/export path, feature without an implementation/behavioral test..."

## Children

1. Positive behavioral tests for every manifest family.
2. High-risk combination suites and pairwise generation.
3. Original and transformed official examples with all controls/modes.
4. WebGPU screenshot and tree-shaking upstream checks.
5. Genuine GL contract tests and absence-of-WebGPU tests.
6. Release verifier full run with separate counts.

## Success criteria for the epic

All children closed; `f3d-conformance` line count reported against 24,000.

## No-claim boundary

"Function name coverage or one constructor assertion is not full functional coverage" (§5.15).
acceptance_criteria: Every manifest record has a positive behavioral test plus applicable invalid-input, mutation, serialization and lifecycle cases; mandatory family-wide suites and high-risk combinations exist and pass; original and transformed official examples run with all controls; WebGPU screenshot and tree-shaking upstream checks pass; genuine GL contracts and absence-of-WebGPU cases are tested; the release verifier reports zero blocking states in these families with separate counts.

title: Positive behavioral tests for every manifest family
description:
## Full scope

Positive behavioral tests for every manifest family: all import paths/aliases; every loader/exporter/codec; every material/map/state family; each TSL/node and shader entry; every pass/effect; all controls and alternate renderers; audio/media; XR; physics wrappers; Inspector/editor/tool workflows; all native-backend public APIs; runtime inputs not present at build time

## Summary

The mandatory family suites of §14.9, driven from the manifest.

## Background (plan §14.9)

"Add mandatory family-wide suites for: all import paths/aliases; every loader/exporter and codec; every standard material/map/state family; each TSL/node and shader entry; every pass/effect; all controls/alternate renderers; audio/media; XR; physics wrappers; Inspector/editor/tool workflows; and all native-backend public APIs. Include runtime inputs not present at build time."

## Technical approach

- Test generation scaffolds per family from the manifest with hand-written bodies where behavior needs it; each test declares its owner expectation; family beads (13.x, 14.x, 16.x, 17.x, 19.x, 21b.x) contribute their suites here; this bead ensures completeness and fills gaps.

## Success criteria

- Verifier: zero `untested` in all families.

## Test plan

- Unit: the generated per-family scaffolds plus hand-written behavior bodies for every manifest record (positive case; invalid-input; mutation; serialization; lifecycle where applicable); a completeness test that every record has at least one resolving positive test reference; source-error preservation tests (no invented errors).
- E2E: family suites executed in the functional lane (and forced/exact lanes where rendering or native contracts apply) on Chrome and Safari; runtime-input cases (assets/shaders/nodes not present at build time).
- Logging: per-record results `{record, family, owner, route, result, evidence}` feeding the updater; archived under `evidence/18b.1/<family>/`.
- Failure artifacts: per-test artifacts by family convention.

## Considerations

- Preserve source errors; do not demand errors upstream does not produce.
acceptance_criteria: For every manifest record there is an executable positive test (upstream or added) with the relevant invalid-input, mutation, serialization and lifecycle cases where applicable; source errors are preserved rather than inventing errors upstream does not produce; the updater marks each record tested with evidence pointers; no record remains untested.

title: High-risk combination suites and pairwise generation
description:
## Full scope

High-risk combination suites and pairwise generation: skinning+morphs+shadows+export; clipping+stencil+transparency; instancing+negative scale+custom shader indices+picking; transmission+color management+render targets; texture update+multiple renderer residencies+disposal; runtime shader/node registration+readback; CSS/SVG+camera changes+input; XR+skinning+layers+session reset; editor undo/redo+shared materials+serialization; plus generated pairwise combinations

## Summary

Interactions are where compatibility breaks.

## Background (plan §14.9 "Cover known high-risk combinations explicitly")

## Technical approach

- One scenario file per named combination; pairwise generator (fixed seed) over the manifest's option flags per family.

## Success criteria

- All named cases pass; pairwise batch passes or files defects.

## Test plan

- Unit: pairwise generator tests (fixed seed, coverage of every pair of option flags per family).
- E2E: one scenario script per named combination (`tests/e2e/combos/*.mjs`) with trace/image comparison vs upstream in the functional and forced lanes on both browsers; the XR combination on the capable lane; the generated pairwise batch as a lane.
- Logging: per-scenario `{combination, lane, result, first_divergence}`; pairwise batch summary with the failing pairs; archived under `evidence/18b.2/`.
- Failure artifacts: images/traces per failing scenario.

## Considerations

- XR combinations need the capable lane (23.1).
acceptance_criteria: Each named combination has an explicit test comparing traces/images with upstream; a pairwise generator over feature flags produces additional combinations that run in the functional and forced lanes; pairwise tests supplement, never replace, the named higher-order cases.

title: Original and transformed official examples with all controls and modes
description:
## Full scope

Original and transformed official examples: run every pinned example both as the original through the routed build and as a transformed artifact, exercising all actual controls, loaders and mode transitions; unchanged upstream skips retained in the inherited lane with supplemental tests; every otherwise unlisted example/manual/tool workflow reconciled into the inventory

## Summary

Every example, both ways, with every control.

## Background (plan §14.9 last paragraph, §15.5)

"Run original and transformed official examples with all actual controls, loaders and mode transitions exercised. Retain unchanged upstream skips in the inherited lane, but supply additional tests for their functional surface. Reconcile every otherwise unlisted example/manual/tool workflow into the same inventory."

## Technical approach

- Control scripts generated from 01.7's inventory; batch runner across the examples index; per-example owner attribution.

## Success criteria

- Batch passes; defects filed per example.

## Test plan

- Unit: control-script generation tests from 01.7's inventory (every recorded control appears in the script).
- E2E: batch runner over the full examples index, each example run as original-through-routing and as a transformed artifact via `f3d verify` with its control script, on both browsers; supplemental candidate tests for upstream E2E exclusions; crosswalk reconciliation check.
- Logging: per-example `{example, form: original|transformed, owner, route, result}` and a batch summary; archived under `evidence/18b.3/`.
- Failure artifacts: verify artifacts per failing example.

## Considerations

- This is large; run it as a lane, not per commit.
acceptance_criteria: The full examples index runs in both forms with control scripts derived from the inventory (01.7); results tagged by owner/route; upstream E2E exclusions are covered by supplemental candidate tests; the crosswalk shows every workflow reconciled.

title: Genuine GL contract tests and absence-of-WebGPU tests
description:
## Full scope

Genuine GL contract tests and absence-of-WebGPU tests: context identity, external context reuse, extension/state/native-handle access, sync pixels visible immediately on return, raw-GL plus Three.js interleaving and resetState, GLBufferAttribute behavior, context loss/restoration, canvas capture; WebGPU absent with working upstream GL/DOM/audio cases

The exact lane's full contract list, plus the no-WebGPU environment.

title: Release verifier full run with separate coverage counts
description:
## Full scope

Release verifier full run: zero blocking states across the manifest, separate counts for import/symbol closure, validated behavior families, new-backend rendering coverage, exact-component integration and capable-host validation; unavailable-host obligations listed, never counted

## Summary

The gate check for Phase 4's feature closure.

## Background (plan §14.10, §18 Phase 4 exit)

"No unimplemented/unclassified/stubbed valid-source feature, full tests pass, portable-rendering closure passes."

## Technical approach
