title: F3D-19: All loaders/exporters/registrations/runtime codecs and current-state round trips
description:
## What this epic delivers

The complete asset I/O surface. Plan §19 F3D-19 depends on 10 and 14; acceptance: "New inputs, every existing format/options, plugin contracts, import/edit/export/reimport".

## Why (plan §5.12 loader/exporter rows, §5.13, §10.2)

"A loader is not complete merely because one bundled model renders." "Export must work after an accelerated update." "Runtime decoding and transcoding are mandatory whenever a caller can provide previously unseen compressed models, textures, archives, or local files."

## Children

1. Loader family closure.
2. Texture/image/compression loaders and runtime codecs/transcoders.
3. glTF extension and plugin inventory from code registrations.
4. Exporters and current-state round trips.
5. Plugin registration/callback identity, independent instances and dedupe rules.

## Success criteria for the epic

All children closed; the loader/exporter families in the manifest are fully owned and tested; retained codec/engine bytes reported separately with licenses.

## No-claim boundary

Retained loaders are compositional compatibility, not Rust coverage; third-party codec Wasm of C/C++ origin is an inherited dependency, never described as memory-safe Rust (§13.5).
acceptance_criteria: Every loader, texture/compression loader, runtime decoder/transcoder, glTF extension/plugin registration and exporter in the manifest has a production owner with load/loadAsync/parse/async-parse, LoadingManager, headers/credentials/CORS, response type, progress/cancellation/error/caching/relative-dependency and options coverage; unseen runtime inputs decode; import→edit/animate→export→re-import round trips pass in both reference and candidate with cross-loading; plugin registration/unregistration and callback identity/order are preserved.

title: Loader family closure (every core/addon loader; load/loadAsync/parse; manager; network; errors)
description:
## Full scope

Loader family closure: every core and addon loader (glTF/GLB, OBJ/MTL, FBX, Collada, STL, PLY, 3DM, 3MF, 3DS, USD/USDZ, LDraw, AMF, VRML, VTK, VOX, point clouds and splats, volume/scientific data, fonts, SVG, animation and archive formats present in the tree); load, loadAsync, parse and async parse; LoadingManager handlers and URL modifiers; request headers/credentials/CORS; response types; progress, cancellation where offered, errors, caching and relative dependencies; multi-file references and metadata; arrays, cameras, scenes, animations and independent mutable instances preserved

## Summary

All the loaders, tested the way the plan demands.

## Background (plan §5.12 "Model, geometry and scientific loaders", §5.13)

"Retain full loaders/runtime dependencies; load/parse/async/local-file/network variants, multi-file references, metadata and error paths."

## Technical approach

- Retained loader modules routed through the facade; the resolver (10.1) supplies both embedded and networked backends; a generated per-loader test template covering the listed API surface with small fixtures per format (from upstream examples' assets where licensed).

## Success criteria

- Family suite green; manifest updated.

## Test plan

- Unit: generated per-loader test template covering `load`/`loadAsync`/`parse`/async parse, LoadingManager handlers and URL modifiers, headers/credentials/CORS, response types, progress, cancellation where offered, errors, caching, relative dependencies, multi-file references, metadata; small fixtures per format (licensed upstream assets or synthesized).
- E2E: loader family suite in Node and the browser as each loader requires, on both browsers; local-file (file input) and network (local server with CORS/credential toggles) variants; error paths preserve upstream error shapes.
- Logging: per-loader per-behavior results `{loader, behavior, variant, result, owner}`; request logs from the local server; archived under `evidence/19.1/`.
- Failure artifacts: loaded-object semantic dumps and the server request log.

## Considerations

- Cancellation semantics exist only where upstream offers them; do not invent.
acceptance_criteria: Every loader manifest record is owned (retained production loader with its runtime dependencies wired through the resolver) with positive tests for each listed behavior; local-file and network variants tested; error paths preserve upstream error shapes.

title: Texture/image/compression loaders with runtime codecs and transcoders included by closure
description:
## Full scope

Texture/image and compression loaders with runtime codecs and transcoders: HDR/RGBE, EXR, UltraHDR, DDS, KTX, KTX2 (Basis Universal transcoder), PVR, TGA, TIFF, LUT loaders; Draco decoder, meshopt decoder and any other shipped decoder/transcoder; included at runtime when reachable; capability-selected embedded variants; mipmaps, block edges, orientation, premultiplication, color conversion and samplers preserved

## Summary

Codecs are part of full compatibility, at runtime, with honest attribution.

## Background (plan §5.12 "Texture/image and compression loaders", §10.2, §13.5)

"Include runtime codecs when future input needs them; browser/build-time preprocessing is an optimization, not the only supported path."

## Technical approach

- Wire the pinned decoder/transcoder assets (Draco JS/Wasm, Basis transcoder, meshopt) through the resolver with worker support where upstream uses workers (`DRACOLoader` worker pool) under 21b.6's worker rules; closure inclusion per 10.7.
- Texture upload of transcoded formats via 14.4.

## Success criteria

- Family suite green; standalone unseen-asset test passes; report lists codec bytes.

## Test plan

- Unit: codec wiring tests (Draco/Basis/meshopt decoders reachable through the resolver; worker-pool paths under 21b.6's rules); format-variant selection tests from capability records (never lossier than source); mip/block-edge/orientation/premultiply invariants per format.
- E2E: texture/compression loader suite on both browsers (HDR/RGBE, EXR, UltraHDR, DDS, KTX, KTX2 with transcoding to every device-supported family, PVR, TGA, TIFF, LUTs); standalone artifact with file input loading an unseen KTX2/Draco/meshopt asset; codec bytes and licenses in the report.
- Logging: per-asset `{loader, format, codec, transcode_target, ms, bytes}` and inclusion decisions; archived under `evidence/19.2/`.
- Failure artifacts: decoded-texture dumps and diff images.

## Considerations

- "A 'please preconvert your model' error is not full compatibility" (§10.2).
acceptance_criteria: Every texture/compression loader and codec manifest record is owned and tested; an application with runtime input can load an unseen KTX2/Draco/meshopt asset in the standalone artifact because the codec was included by closure; format variants selected by capability never reduce source quality; third-party codec bytes and licenses are reported separately.

title: glTF extension and plugin inventory from code registrations
description:
## Full scope

glTF extension and plugin inventory from code registrations: every built-in registered extension in the pinned GLTFLoader plus shipped/example-registered plugins (instancing, compression, texture formats/transforms, material extensions, animation pointer, variants, progressive/splat integrations as present); parser/plugin callbacks, metadata and unknown/required-extension behavior preserved

## Summary

Inventory code registrations, not doc bullets.

## Background (plan §5.12 "glTF and material extensions", §5.13, §23 [S58])

"Inventory code registrations, not only documentation bullets; preserve parser/plugin callbacks, metadata and unknown/required-extension behavior." "The inspected GLTFLoader registers extensions beyond what a short documentation list can safely establish."

## Technical approach

- Static extraction from the pinned `GLTFLoader.js` (`this.register(...)` calls, `EXTENSIONS` table) and from examples registering plugins; test assets per extension (from the glTF sample repositories where licensed, otherwise synthesized).

## Success criteria

- Inventory committed; tests green.

## Test plan

- Unit: registration extractor tests over the pinned `GLTFLoader.js` (`register` calls, `EXTENSIONS` table) and example registrations; per-extension parse tests with sample assets; unknown/required-extension behavior tests matching upstream.
- E2E: browser loads of every extension asset through the routed build on both browsers with semantic comparison to upstream; exporter cross-check where a counterpart exists.
- Logging: per-extension `{extension, source: builtin|example, asset, result}`; archived under `evidence/19.3/`.
- Failure artifacts: parsed-scene semantic diffs.

## Considerations

- Material extensions interact with 14.2's physical closure.
acceptance_criteria: The extension list is derived from the pinned GLTFLoader's registration code and example registrations (not documentation), each with a positive test asset; required-but-unknown extension behavior matches upstream; GLTFExporter plugin counterparts are cross-checked.

title: Exporters and current-state round trips after accelerated updates
description:
## Full scope

Exporters and current-state round trips: core JSON/object/material/geometry/node serialization and every addon exporter (glTF/GLB, OBJ, PLY, STL, USDZ, Draco, EXR, KTX2 and any additional source entry); export after an accelerated update materializes current CPU-observable transforms, geometry, skin/morph data, animation, textures and metadata at the writer's original boundaries; import→edit/animate→export→re-import in reference and candidate plus cross-loading; byte-exact where specified, semantic compare otherwise; lossy codecs with identical settings and tolerance

## Summary

Export is a read of current state at the writer's boundary.

## Background (plan §5.12 "Exporters and serialization", §5.13)

"Retain production writers, runtime encoding dependencies and CPU materialization; semantic round trips and source-compatible output/options/errors." "Never export the initial captured scene while the user sees a newer scene. Do not promise an exporter captures dynamic GPU-only state that upstream itself does not export."

## Technical approach

- Pre-export materialization hook (06.4) invoked by the exporters' entry points (via the routed modules, not by editing exporters); round-trip harness in `f3d-conformance`.

## Success criteria

- Family suite and round-trip suite green.

## Test plan

- Unit: per-exporter option/error tests; pre-export materialization hook tests (exporter reads observe current Wasm-owned state); semantic round-trip comparator tests (byte-exact where the format specifies it).
- E2E: round-trip suite `tests/e2e/exporters/roundtrip.mjs` for every format pair upstream supports: import → edit/animate (accelerated) → export → re-import on reference and candidate, plus cross-loading, on both browsers; lossy codecs with identical settings and tolerance; runtime encoders (Draco/KTX2) included when reachable.
- Logging: per-round-trip `{format, direction, semantic_delta, byte_exact: bool}`; archived under `evidence/19.4/`.
- Failure artifacts: exported files from both sides and the semantic diff.

## Considerations

- Different lossy encodings are not automatically equivalent.
acceptance_criteria: Every exporter manifest record is owned and tested with options/errors; the round-trip suite passes for every format pair where upstream supports it, after accelerated animation/transform updates; exporters never see stale captured state; runtime encoders (Draco/KTX2 encoding) are included when reachable.

title: Loader/exporter plugin registration, callback identity, independent instances, dedupe rules
description:
## Full scope

Loader/exporter plugin registration and unregistration, callback identity and order, independent mutable instances per load, and asset byte deduplication rules that never share mutable objects

## Summary

The extension-point contract for asset I/O.

## Background (plan §5.13 last sentence, §10.1)

"Preserve custom plugin registration/unregistration and callback identity/order for loaders and exporters." "Deduplicating asset bytes must not accidentally share mutable scene objects, materials, animation state, or callback identities."

## Technical approach

- Tests over registration APIs; identity checks across repeated loads; resolver-level dedupe verification.

## Success criteria

- Tests green.

## Test plan

- Unit: registration/unregistration API tests with callback identity and invocation order asserted; repeated-load independence tests; resolver dedupe tests (bytes shared, objects independent).
- E2E: browser tests on both browsers for plugin lifecycles and repeated loads of the same asset.
- Logging: callback-order traces and identity checks; archived under `evidence/19.5/`.
- Failure artifacts: the callback trace diff.

## Considerations

- Relates to 10.7's dedupe implementation.
acceptance_criteria: Registering/unregistering custom loader/exporter plugins works with callback identity and invocation order equal to upstream; loading the same asset twice yields independent mutable object graphs; deduplicated bytes are shared only at the byte level.

title: F3D-20: Profile-justified new-backend GPU improvements (H7/H8 and the general corpus, with ablations)
description:
## What this epic delivers

Phase 4's "demanding performance" work. Plan §19 F3D-20 depends on 13, 16, 17; acceptance: "H7/H8/general corpus ablations; retained renderers cannot satisfy accelerated closure".

## Why (plan §8.7, §12.3, §12.4, §16.8, §18 Phase 4)

"Apply measured GPU optimizations only after the conservative full behavior works." "Run ablations that disable one optimization at a time... Publish where the gain comes from and where the bottleneck moved. Do not multiply isolated kernel speedups together."

## Children

1. GPU compute offload decisions with CPU paths retained.
2. Specialization portfolio, bounded calibration and plan caching.
3. Optional hardware features (immediates, subgroup-size control, FP16, transient attachments).
4. H7/H8 profile-driven improvements.
5. Ablation suite and attribution.
6. GPU picking as an additional async API and GPU culling with conservative recovery.

## Success criteria for the epic

All children closed; every optimization has an ablation row; H7/H8 results published with attribution.

## No-claim boundary

"A 5× transform kernel and a 2× uploader do not imply a 10× application" (§16.8).
acceptance_criteria: Measured GPU-side improvements (compute offload decisions, the specialization portfolio with bounded calibration, optional hardware features, H7/H8 kernel/data-path improvements, GPU picking/culling as additional strategies) are applied only after conservative full behavior works, each with an ablation measurement attributing gains; retained renderers never satisfy accelerated closure.

title: GPU compute offload decisions with CPU paths retained and precision contracts
description:
## Full scope

GPU compute offload decisions: move work to compute only where it removes a demonstrated bottleneck without costly or semantically invalid readback (already-GPU-authored TSL kernels, culling, large animation batches with appropriate state authority, geometry without CPU observations); keep CPU paths for small batches and synchronous public observations; f64-to-f32 moves only under a separately admitted precision contract

## Summary

Compute offload as a justified decision, not a reflex.

## Background (plan §8.7)

"Move work to compute only when doing so removes a demonstrated bottleneck and does not require costly or semantically invalid readback... Moving CPU-authored `f64` simulation to `f32` compute is not an exact optimization; it requires a separately admitted precision contract and cannot enter the primary score merely because the image initially looks similar."

## Technical approach

- Candidate list from profiles (03.4 and later); per candidate: observation analysis (12b.2), kernel via 16.3, fallback switch, ablation entry (12b.5 registry).

## Success criteria

- Decisions documented with profiles; tests for fallback equivalence.

## Test plan

- Unit: ownership-analysis tests per offload candidate (a synchronous CPU observation blocks offload); CPU-fallback equivalence tests; precision-contract gating tests (f64→f32 only in the labeled optional mode).
- E2E: per-candidate paired runs and ablations on the reserved devices; equivalence via `f3d verify` in the forced lane with the fallback on and off.
- Logging: decision records `{candidate, profile_ref, observations, fallback, mode}` and ablation deltas; archived under `evidence/20.1/`.
- Failure artifacts: readback diffs between offloaded and CPU paths.

## Considerations

- GPU-only state changes device-loss classification (17.7).
acceptance_criteria: Each offload candidate has a profile showing the bottleneck, an ownership analysis proving no synchronous CPU observation is violated, a CPU fallback retained, and an ablation; any precision change is in a separately labeled optional mode.

title: Specialization portfolio, bounded calibration and plan caching (no online ML)
description:
## Full scope

Specialization portfolio and bounded calibration: choose among CPU vs GPU culling, ordinary draws vs bundles, conservative workgroup sizes, a few legal data-layout choices and simple vs clustered lighting by bounded measurement on representative kernels outside the interactive critical path; cache the selected plan against source/runtime/browser/capability identity; persist source-level recipes and WGSL, never GPU handles; conservative defaults; stale-profile invalidation; no online ML optimizer

## Summary

Tuning without a research platform.

## Background (plan §12.3, §12.4)

"Perform bounded calibration on representative kernels, outside the interactive critical path. Cache the selected plan against source/runtime/browser/capability identity. Persist source-level recipes and WGSL, not GPU handles or assumed portable driver binaries... A tuning decision changes how equivalent work is executed, not how much visual or simulation work is required. Do not introduce an online ML optimizer or numerical-policy subsystem into every frame."

## Technical approach

- Portfolio table with legality preconditions per option; calibration harness in a preparation region (02.5); cache in the build cache keyed by capability record; report the chosen options.

## Success criteria

- Policy tests; cache invalidation tests; equivalence across all options.

## Test plan

- Unit: policy tests (each option's legality precondition enforced; conservative default chosen when calibration is absent); cache identity/invalidation tests (capability record, source, runtime, browser changes miss); a test that no option changes visual/simulation work.
- E2E: calibration runs in a preparation region outside interactive frames on each stratum; equivalence via `f3d verify` across every option; chosen options reported.
- Logging: calibration `metric` events `{option, candidate, ms, chosen}` and cache events; archived under `evidence/20.2/`.
- Failure artifacts: the calibration table and diff images for any non-equivalent option.

## Considerations

- "Optional offline analysis may use the sibling scientific libraries, but the chosen policy should remain small and explainable."
acceptance_criteria: A small explainable policy selects among the enumerated implementations using calibration runs bounded in time and executed outside interactive frames; the selection is cached by identity and invalidated when any component changes; defaults are conservative; the policy never changes the amount of visual or simulation work.

title: Optional hardware features as capability-checked labeled variants (immediates, subgroups, FP16)
description:
## Full scope

Optional hardware features as capability-checked, separately labeled variants: immediates for small dynamic binding overhead, subgroup-size control for specific compute kernels, FP16 only under the precision contract, transient attachments where supported; portable paths always retained; unknown capabilities recorded as unknown

## Summary

Use what the device offers without assuming it.

## Background (plan §2.6, §12.2, §12.3, §23 [S21], [S22])

"Current Chrome documentation describes immediates and subgroup-size control. These are useful optional specialization opportunities, not capabilities to assume on every browser or adapter."

## Technical approach

- Feature-gated code paths with the capability record; report labels; primary-score exclusion for precision-changing variants.

## Success criteria

- Tests on strata with and without the features.

## Test plan

- Unit: capability-gating tests per feature (requested only when advertised; used only against enabled features/limits; portable fallback present); report-label tests (optional variants labeled; precision-changing variants excluded from the primary score).
- E2E: runs on strata with and without each feature on both browsers; equivalence for non-precision variants; labeled bench variants.
- Logging: feature usage per run `{feature, available, used, variant_label}`; archived under `evidence/20.3/`.
- Failure artifacts: diff images and the capability record.

## Considerations

- Feature names, WGSL directives and binding APIs are versioned together.
acceptance_criteria: Each optional feature is requested only when advertised, used only against the created device's enabled features/limits, has a portable fallback, and is reported as an optional variant; FP16/relaxed variants never enter the primary score.

title: H7/H8 profile-driven improvements measured end to end
description:
## Full scope

H7/H8 profile-driven improvements: equivalent kernel and data-path changes for the modern-compute cells (pose/update specialization and cross-pass reuse for H7; kernel-chain scheduling, packed cell data layout, indirect dispatch sizing for H8) measured end to end under the frozen protocol; results published whether or not they reach 2x

## Summary

The hardest viability question, answered with measurements rather than postponed.

## Background (plan §16.7 "Generalization gate", §20 "Modern compute demos remain GPU-bound and <2×")

"Profile H7/H8 references during Phase 0 and test promising equivalent kernel/data-path changes early, rather than postponing the hardest viability question until the renderer is complete."

## Technical approach

- Iterate: profile (07.7 + GPU timestamps where available) → candidate change → legality → ablation → paired run.

## Success criteria

- Results documents; feeds G4/F3D-23.2.

## Test plan

- Unit: legality tests per attempted improvement (numeric contract, observation contract) with CPU/GPU references.
- E2E: profile → change → ablation → paired run loops for H7 and H8 on the reserved M5, phone and discrete-GPU strata; `f3d verify` after each change; results documents per stratum.
- Logging: per-iteration `{case, change, profile_before, profile_after, ratio, ci}` with telemetry breakdowns and GPU timestamps where available; archived under `evidence/20.4/`.
- Failure artifacts: readback diffs and invalidated runs with reasons.

## Considerations

- Never reduce particle counts or quality to win.
acceptance_criteria: For H7 and H8, each attempted improvement has a profile motivation, a legality argument (numeric contract, observation contract), an ablation and paired results; the final results document per stratum states the achieved ratio with interval and, if below 2x, says so and records the bottleneck location.

title: Ablation suite and attribution of gains
description:
## Full scope

Ablation suite and attribution of gains: disable one optimization at a time (update compilation, dirty tracking, material-program merging, instancing, bundles, GPU compute selection, pass/resource optimization, optional hardware features) across the corpus; publish where the gain comes from and where the bottleneck moved; no multiplication of isolated kernel speedups

## Summary

Know why it is faster, when it is. This bead turns the pass registry (12b.5) and the bench protocol into a reproducible attribution report.

## Background (plan §16.8, §14.8, §3.5)

"Run ablations that disable one optimization at a time: update compilation, dirty tracking, material-program merging, bundles, GPU compute selection, pass/resource optimization, and optional hardware features. Publish where the gain comes from and where the bottleneck moved. Do not multiply isolated kernel speedups together. A 5× transform kernel and a 2× uploader do not imply a 10× application." The build report distinguishes structural estimates from measured timings; ablation rows are measured timings.

## Technical approach

- `f3d bench --ablate <pass|all>`: for each registered pass, build (or configure at runtime where the switch is a runtime flag) the artifact with that pass routed to its conservative reference, run the paired protocol on the same reserved device, and compute the delta against the fully optimized artifact using the analysis script (03.8) with the same block bootstrap.
- Bottleneck location: for each ablation, record the telemetry breakdown (07.7: CPU preparation, bridge, uploads, command preparation, GPU time) so the report can say "removing bundles moved the bottleneck from GPU to command preparation".
- Ordering caveat: ablations are one-at-a-time by design; interactions are not claimed. If two passes only pay off together, record the pair as a single registry entry rather than inferring it.
- Output: per-cell markdown/JSON table appended to the results package used by F3D-23.2.

## Success criteria

- Attribution tables for H1–H8 and the fidelity set on at least the M5 stratum; every registered pass has a row per cell; the analysis refuses to emit a "combined" multiplicative figure.

## Test plan

- Unit: registry-iteration tests; a synthetic artifact with two known-cost passes verifies ablation deltas within the noise band; a test that the analysis refuses to emit a multiplicative combined figure.
- E2E: `f3d bench --ablate all` over H1–H8 and the fidelity set on the reserved M5 (and other strata as scheduled with 23.2).
- Logging: per-ablation `metric` events `{cell, pass_disabled, ratio, ci_low, ci_high, bottleneck_after}` and the attribution tables; raw runs archived under `evidence/20.5/`.
- Failure artifacts: invalidated runs with reasons.

## Considerations

- Ablation runs consume reserved-device time; schedule them with the scored campaign (23.2) rather than ad hoc.
- Guards and materialization are part of the measured optimized path and are never "ablated away" to inflate a number (§14.8).
acceptance_criteria: f3d bench --ablate runs the registered optimizer passes one-off at a time on every corpus cell and produces an attribution table per cell with paired intervals; each row names the optimization disabled, the throughput delta, and the observed bottleneck location after disabling; the summary never multiplies component speedups.

title: GPU picking as an additional async API and GPU culling with conservative recovery
description:
## Full scope

GPU picking as an additional asynchronous API (never a substitute for synchronous Raycaster results) and GPU culling with conservative recovery for motion/disocclusion that cannot create missing geometry

## Summary

Additive strategies, not contract changes.

## Background (plan §5.10, §7.6)

"GPU picking may be an additional async API or a proven internal strategy, not a Promise substituted for a synchronous `Raycaster` result." "GPU culling is an optional execution strategy, not a different visibility contract. Occlusion based on previous frames requires conservative recovery for motion/disocclusion and cannot silently create missing geometry."

## Technical approach

- ID-buffer picking pass with async readback (17.4); culling compaction kernel (08.6) with a conservative "unknown → visible" rule and disocclusion recovery tests.

## Success criteria

- Tests; portfolio integration.

## Test plan

- Unit: ID-buffer picking correctness tests vs the synchronous raycaster on synthetic scenes; culling compaction tests with a CPU reference and the "unknown → visible" rule; disocclusion recovery tests.
- E2E: browser tests on both browsers for the async picking API and for GPU culling under motion/disocclusion scripts, asserting no missing geometry vs upstream frames.
- Logging: picking results and culling stats `{visible, culled, recovered}`; archived under `evidence/20.6/`.
- Failure artifacts: frames showing missing geometry with the culling decision dump.

## Considerations

- Low priority; only if profiles justify.
acceptance_criteria: An optional async GPU picking API exists under the F3D namespace with documented semantics; the public Raycaster remains synchronous and CPU-authoritative; GPU culling (when selected by the portfolio) is proven never to discard potentially visible geometry, with conservative recovery tests for disocclusion.

title: F3D-21 (early slice): Host and tool integrations needed by Phase 0/1 (CSS/SVG renderers, controls, Inspector/editor smoke, WebAudio route)
description:
## What this epic delivers

The early host-integration slice. Plan §19 F3D-21 early prerequisite is 04.

## Why (plan §5.14, §3.3 "No WebGPU prerequisite", §18 Phase 0)

"DOM/CSS/SVG: Preserve actual nodes, vector elements, style/layout behavior, event targets, focus, selection, visibility, parentage and removal... Flattening labels or SVG into the canvas is not equivalent. A page using only these renderers has no reason to require WebGPU."

## Children

1. CSS2D/CSS3D/SVG renderer routes without WebGPU.
2. Controls and interaction retained route with real DOM events.
3. Inspector/devtools hooks and editor smoke.
4. WebAudio route smoke.

## Success criteria for the epic

All children closed; results tagged retained/browser-owned.

## No-claim boundary

These are retained/browser-owned routes; they are not Rust rewrites and never acceleration evidence.
acceptance_criteria: CSS2D/CSS3D/SVG renderers, the controls used by H1/H2, Inspector/devtools hooks, an editor smoke workflow and a WebAudio smoke path all work through the routed build with real DOM/audio objects and without requiring WebGPU or Wasm initialization where the source does not.

title: CSS2D/CSS3D/SVG renderer routes without WebGPU
description:
## Full scope

CSS2DRenderer, CSS3DRenderer/objects/sprites, SVGRenderer/SVGObject/Projector routes: real DOM/CSS/vector output through the routed build; mixed CSS/WebGPU views share the source's camera/transform observations; no GPU request for non-GPU scenes

## Summary

Alternate renderers are real features with real DOM.

## Background (plan §5.12 "Alternate renderers", §5.14, §23 [S59], [S60])

## Technical approach

- Retained modules; mixed-view test using camera materialization (06.4) so CSS transforms read current matrices.

## Success criteria

- Tests green on both browsers.

## Test plan

- Unit: none (retained JS).
- E2E: `tests/e2e/alt-renderers/smoke.mjs` on both browsers: DOM structure/styles/events of CSS2D/CSS3D/SVG output vs upstream; a CSS/SVG-only page with `navigator.gpu` removed asserting no Wasm instantiation; a mixed CSS+WebGPU page with label positions consistent with the accelerated camera at every frame.
- Logging: structural diff summaries and initialization events (Wasm/GPU absent); archived under `evidence/21a.1/`.
- Failure artifacts: serialized DOM/SVG from both sides.

## Considerations

- Documented upstream limitations preserved, not "fixed".
acceptance_criteria: The alternate renderers work unmodified through the facade with identical DOM structure/styles/events as upstream; a CSS/SVG-only page initializes no Wasm/GPU; a mixed CSS+WebGPU page keeps label positions consistent with the accelerated camera observations at every frame.

title: Controls and interaction retained route with real DOM events (H1-H8 controls)
description:
## Full scope

Controls and interaction retained route: OrbitControls and the controls used by H1/H2/H3–H8 with browser-owned input, real identity, focus, pointer capture/lock and event ordering; no rasterized substitute for interactive DOM

## Summary

Controls stay JavaScript; the boundary is explicit.

## Background (plan §5.12 "Controls and interaction", §4.6 last row)

"Browser-owned input with real identity, focus, pointer capture/lock and event ordering; no rasterized substitute for interactive DOM." "DOM controls and unusual effectful callbacks → Retain JavaScript and synchronize at explicit boundaries."

## Technical approach

- Retained control modules; ownership: camera state JS-owned with boundary snapshots (05.5); scripted input tests (03.1).

## Success criteria

- Trace equality under input scripts.

## Test plan

- Unit: none (retained JS); ownership tests for camera-state snapshots at the boundary (05.5).
- E2E: `tests/e2e/controls/corpus.mjs` on both browsers: the controls used by H1–H8 under scripted real pointer/keyboard/wheel/touch input with event ordering and state traces equal to upstream; pointer capture/lock and focus behavior.
- Logging: event traces per script with logical-frame indices and control state; archived under `evidence/21a.2/`.
- Failure artifacts: the trace diff.

## Considerations

- Full control-family closure is 21b.1.
acceptance_criteria: The corpus's controls operate through the routed build with event ordering and state updates equal to upstream under scripted input; pointer capture/lock and focus behave identically; camera state written by controls is observed by the accelerated path at the right boundary.

title: Inspector/devtools hooks for H1 and an editor smoke workflow
description:
## Full scope

Inspector/devtools hooks for H1 and an editor smoke workflow: the upstream Inspector attaches to the routed renderer with truthful public data; devtools integration points preserved; the upstream editor loads a project, edits, undoes, and exports through the routed build

## Summary

Existing tools keep working from day one.

## Background (plan §5.14 "Editor/Inspector/devtools", §5.7)

## Technical approach

- Retained tool modules; renderer service adaptation limited to what the routed renderer already exposes; `__f3d` namespace for physical telemetry.

## Success criteria

- Smoke tests green.

## Test plan

- Unit: none.
- E2E: Inspector opens on H1 through the routed build with panels populated equal to upstream's public fields; devtools hooks respond; editor smoke workflow (load a project, edit a material, undo, export) via browser automation on both browsers; F3D telemetry visible only under `__f3d`.
- Logging: per-step workflow events and panel snapshots; archived under `evidence/21a.3/`.
- Failure artifacts: editor state dumps and panel snapshots.

## Considerations

- Full editor workflow closure is 21b.5.
acceptance_criteria: Inspector panels populate on H1 through the routed build (retained renderer at this stage; new backend later via 07.5); devtools hooks respond; the editor smoke workflow passes; F3D telemetry appears only in its own namespace.

title: WebAudio route smoke with real activation
description:
## Full scope

WebAudio route smoke: Audio/AudioListener/PositionalAudio with real AudioContext nodes, activation preserved from a real user gesture, no new await inserted before activation-sensitive calls

## Summary

Native audio graphs, untouched.

## Background (plan §5.14 "WebAudio/media", §5.12 "Audio and live media", §23 [S61])

"Connect Asupersync only to operations it actually owns; do not move a user-activation-sensitive call behind a new await."

## Technical approach

- Retained modules; listener transform materialization; gesture-driven test.

## Success criteria

- Test green on both browsers.

## Test plan

- Unit: none.
- E2E: audio example through the routed build on both browsers after a real automated gesture: `AudioContext` graph equals upstream's; autoplay blocked without a gesture behaves as upstream; listener follows an accelerated camera at the right boundary.
- Logging: audio graph dumps and activation events; archived under `evidence/21a.4/`.
- Failure artifacts: graph dump diffs.

## Considerations

- Full audio closure is 21b.2.

title: F3D-21 (closure): All host/tool integrations and complete official workflows (controls, CSS/SVG, audio/media, XR, physics, workers, Inspector/editor/player/devtools)
description:
## What this epic delivers

Phase 4's host and tool closure. Plan §19 F3D-21 closure "uses 17–20"; acceptance: "Controls/CSS/SVG/audio/media/XR/physics/worker/Inspector/editor/player/devtools coverage".

## Why (plan §5.12 rows Controls, Alternate renderers, Audio, WebXR, Misc/physics, Inspector/editor, Deployment/workers; §5.14; §18 Phase 4)

"Close the entire feature manifest and all inherited/additional tests, including previously untested/TODO features, exact WebGL/WebGPU backend APIs, exporters and plugins, media/audio, real XR integrations, physics wrappers, and editor/player/Inspector/devtools workflows. Complete a capable-host matrix; device limitations match the reference and do not delete features."

## Children

1. All controls and interaction closure (every control class, gizmos, HTMLMesh/InteractiveGroup)
2. Audio and live media closure with real WebAudio/media graphs
3. WebXR closure (GL-backed and native WebGPU XR, fallback honored, capable headset lane)
4. Physics wrappers and miscellaneous addons closure (same engines, GPGPU, water/sky, splats)
5. Editor, Inspector, devtools and TSL tools full workflows
6. Workers, offscreen, library and environment flows (generation-tagged worker protocol)
7. Alternate renderers closure (CSS2D/CSS3D/SVG full API and any other shipped output backend)

## Success criteria for the epic

All children closed; manifest families fully owned and tested; `f3d-runtime` line count reported against 12,000.

## No-claim boundary

External engines and tools are reused, never rewritten; they are dependency compatibility obligations (§5.14).
acceptance_criteria: Every controls/interaction, alternate-renderer, audio/media, WebXR, physics/misc-addon, worker/offscreen/library and Inspector/editor/player/devtools/TSL-tool record in the manifest has a production owner with end-to-end tests, including capable-host lanes for XR and permission-dependent behavior; official workflows (author/edit/reload/export/play) work on real projects.

title: All controls and interaction closure (every control class, gizmos, HTMLMesh/InteractiveGroup)
description:
## Full scope

All controls and interaction: every control class (Orbit/Map/Trackball/Fly/FirstPerson/PointerLock/Drag/Transform/Arcball and every other control in the tree), selection/picking helpers, transform gizmos and snapping, HTMLMesh/InteractiveGroup, helper geometry and camera/scene utilities; event ordering under scripted input

## Summary

Close the interaction family: every control class in `examples/jsm/controls/`, the interactive helpers in `examples/jsm/interactive/`, and the helper/utility objects that respond to input.

## Background (plan §5.12 "Controls and interaction", §5.14 "DOM/CSS/SVG", §4.6 last row)

"Browser-owned input with real identity, focus, pointer capture/lock and event ordering; no rasterized substitute for interactive DOM." Controls write camera/object state that the accelerated path reads at explicit boundaries; the ownership model (05.5) keeps that state JavaScript-owned with snapshots.

## Technical approach

- From the manifest, list every control/interaction record; retain the upstream modules through the facade (04.2); no rewrites.
- Input scripts (03.1 format) per control covering its documented gestures: drag/rotate/pan/zoom/dolly, keyboard modes, touch/pinch, wheel, pointer lock enter/exit, `enableDamping` update loops, `TransformControls` modes (translate/rotate/scale, local/world space, snapping, axis constraints), `DragControls` hover/drag events, `ArcballControls` gizmo, `HTMLMesh` DOM events through `InteractiveGroup`.
- Trace comparison with upstream: control state (target/position/quaternion), emitted events (`change`, `start`, `end`, `dragging-changed`, `objectChange`) and their order.
- Gizmo picking runs through the synchronous raycast (06.5) over meshes whose transforms are Wasm-owned; the pick must observe current state.

## Success criteria

- Family suite green on both browsers with identical event traces; pick tests match upstream `intersectObjects` results including gizmo handles.

## Test plan

- Unit: none (retained JS); gizmo-picking tests use the synchronous raycast suite (06.5).
- E2E: generated per-control input scripts (drag/rotate/pan/zoom/dolly, keyboard modes, touch/pinch, wheel, pointer lock, damping loops, TransformControls modes/space/snapping/axis constraints, DragControls hover/drag events, ArcballControls gizmo, HTMLMesh/InteractiveGroup events) on both browsers with real pointer events; event and state traces vs upstream; gizmo picks over Wasm-owned meshes.
- Logging: per-script event traces with logical-frame indices; archived under `evidence/21b.1/`.
- Failure artifacts: trace diffs.

## Considerations

- The CSS/SVG+camera changes+input combination is covered by 18b.2; this bead supplies the controls half.
- Do not "optimize" control math into Rust; it is cold, effectful, and browser-owned by design.
acceptance_criteria: Every controls/interaction manifest record is owned (retained browser-owned JavaScript) and tested with scripted input traces equal to upstream on Chrome and Safari; TransformControls gizmo picking and snapping use the synchronous raycast contract over accelerated meshes; HTMLMesh/InteractiveGroup keep real DOM identity, focus and event targets; pointer capture/lock and keyboard focus behave identically.

title: Audio and live media closure with real WebAudio/media graphs
description:
## Full scope

Audio and live media closure: Audio/AudioListener/PositionalAudio/AudioAnalyser/AudioContext helpers, filters/nodes/playback/loop/rates, live sources (microphone/media streams) and audio loaders; video/frame/canvas sources; activation, seeking, source replacement, permission and cleanup tests; upstream unsupported-environment behavior preserved

## Summary

Complete the audio/media family started by the 21a.4 smoke path.

## Background (plan §5.12 "Audio and live media", §5.14 "WebAudio/media", §23 [S61])

"Actual WebAudio/browser media graphs, not simulated values; activation, seeking, source replacement, permission and cleanup tests." "Preserve native audio nodes, scheduled playback, filters, rate/loop/positional behavior, analyser data, source ownership and activation. Connect Asupersync only to operations it actually owns; do not move a user-activation-sensitive call behind a new await. Keep browser autoplay/origin restrictions and the upstream's actual unsupported-environment behavior."

## Technical approach

- Retain upstream audio modules; verify the node graph structure by inspecting the real `AudioContext` graph (node types, connections, parameters) against upstream for each API: `setBuffer`, `setMediaElementSource`, `setMediaStreamSource`, `setNodeSource`, `setFilter(s)`, `setPlaybackRate`, `setLoop`, `setDetune`, `play/pause/stop` with offsets, `PositionalAudio` panner parameters and `setDirectionalCone`, `AudioAnalyser.getFrequencyData/getAverageFrequency`.
- Transform boundary: the listener and positional sources read object matrices via materialization (06.4) at the same update points as upstream (`updateMatrixWorld`).
- Media sources for textures (14.4) share the lifecycle tests: seeking, pause/resume, `srcObject` replacement, cross-origin restrictions.
- Permission flows (microphone) tested with granted and denied outcomes through the automation harness; unsupported environments (no `AudioContext`) produce upstream's behavior.

## Success criteria

- Family suite green on Chrome and Safari; graph-structure diffs empty; activation tests pass only from real gestures.

## Test plan

- Unit: none (retained JS).
- E2E: per-API tests on both browsers inspecting the real `AudioContext` graph (node types, connections, parameters) vs upstream for buffers, media elements, media streams, node sources, filters, playback rate/loop/detune, play/pause/stop with offsets, positional panner parameters and cones, analyser data; media lifecycle (seeking, pause/resume, `srcObject` replacement, cross-origin); permission granted/denied flows; no-`AudioContext` environment behavior.
- Logging: audio graph dumps per test and activation/permission events; archived under `evidence/21b.2/`.
- Failure artifacts: graph dump diffs.

## Considerations

- Never bypass autoplay policies to make a test pass; a blocked autoplay must match upstream's observable state.
acceptance_criteria: Every audio/media manifest record is owned and tested with real WebAudio/media graphs (no simulated values); activation, seeking, source replacement, permission prompts/denials and cleanup behave as upstream on both browsers; PositionalAudio follows accelerated object transforms at the correct boundary; AudioAnalyser data comes from the real analyser node.

title: WebXR closure (GL-backed and native WebGPU XR, fallback honored, capable headset lane)
description:
## Full scope

WebXR closure: WebXRManager/XRManager sessions, reference spaces and resets, cameras/views/layers/framebuffers, controllers/hands/haptics/buttons/models, hit testing/planes/depth/camera/lighting where upstream supports them; capability-qualified native WebGPU XR and exact GL-backed sessions; WebGLXRFallback honored; real XRFrame lifecycle; capable headset/browser lane with real-device evidence

## Summary

XR through both routes, with honest evidence.

## Background (plan §5.12 "WebXR/AR/VR", §5.14 "WebXR", §14.9 last paragraph, §23 [S56], [S62])

"The existing XR fallback helper explicitly constructs and installs a new renderer; honor that contract instead of secretly switching an already-exposed canvas/device. A capable headset/browser lane is required for behavior that a phone cannot exercise." "Emulators/mocks are additional tests, not successful hardware feature evidence."

## Technical approach

- Session lifecycle in the runtime for the new backend (XRGPUBinding where available) and pass-through for exact GL; fallback helper unchanged; capable lane in 23.1.

## Success criteria

- Family green on the capable lane; obligations listed if hardware unavailable.

## Test plan

- Unit: session lifecycle state-machine tests with a fake XR system (spaces, resets, layers, controllers/hands/haptics).
- E2E: capable headset/browser lane scripts for GL-backed sessions (exact component, including the construction-time fallback installing a new renderer) and native WebGPU XR where supported; XR+skinning+layers+session-reset combination; emulator lane labeled as additional only.
- Logging: XR frame/session events `{event, space, layers, inputs}` tagged with the lane; archived under `evidence/21b.3/`.
- Failure artifacts: session traces and frame captures.

## Considerations

- Lack of headset access is an outstanding obligation, never a pass.
acceptance_criteria: Every XR manifest record is owned and tested; GL-backed sessions use the exact component (including the construction-time fallback installing a new renderer); native WebGPU XR is used only where the browser supports it; XR+skinning+layers+session-reset combination passes; evidence comes from a real headset/browser lane, with emulator results labeled as additional only.

title: Physics wrappers and miscellaneous addons closure (same engines, GPGPU, water/sky, splats)
description:
## Full scope

Physics wrappers and miscellaneous addons: Ammo/Jolt/Rapier wrappers with the same engine version, inputs, solver/time-step semantics and public adapter behavior; GPUComputationRenderer and GPGPU helpers, water/sky/reflectors/refractors, splats, volumes, progressive light maps, sculpting/painters, official path-tracing integrations and every other misc/helper/utility/worker object

## Summary

Reuse the engines; optimize only the graphics.

## Background (plan §5.12 "Miscellaneous addons and physics integrations", §5.14 "Physics", §7.7 last paragraph)

"An acceleration pass cannot replace Rapier/Ammo/Jolt simulation with a visually plausible approximation."

## Technical approach

- Retained wrappers and engine Wasm as disclosed dependencies (13.5); GPGPU render-target ping-pong via the pass graph; splats/volumes via 14.4/16.3 paths.

## Success criteria

- Family green; simulation traces identical.

## Test plan

- Unit: none for external engines; GPGPU helper mapping tests (render-target ping-pong through the pass graph).
- E2E: scripted simulations through the routed build with identical results to upstream (same engine versions); GPGPU/water/sky/reflector/splat/volume/progressive-lightmap/sculpting/path-tracing examples via `f3d verify` in the appropriate lanes on both browsers; a test that graphics optimization leaves wrapper state untouched.
- Logging: per-record results with owners and engine versions; simulation state hashes per step; archived under `evidence/21b.4/`.
- Failure artifacts: state dumps and diff images.

## Considerations

- Third-party Wasm of C/C++ origin is never described as memory-safe Rust.
acceptance_criteria: Every misc/physics manifest record is owned and tested; physics wrappers run the pinned external engine versions with identical simulation results for scripted scenes; GPGPU helpers execute through the new backend (portable) or exact route (native contract) as their semantics require; graphics optimization never alters authoritative simulation state.

title: Editor, Inspector, devtools and TSL tools full workflows
description:
## Full scope

Editor, Inspector, devtools and TSL tools full workflows: import/edit/undo-redo/serialize/script/player/export/publish/XR paths and renderer changes in the upstream editor; Inspector hooks/panels and devtools integration; TSL transpiler/editor tools; editor-authored scripts execute with original host/security requirements; Rust source maps and generated-shader inspection augment existing APIs

## Summary

The tools are consumers; they must keep working completely.

## Background (plan §5.12 "Inspector, tooling and editor workflows", §5.14 "Editor/Inspector/devtools", §23 [S57])

## Technical approach

- Workflow scripts from 01.7; renderer service adaptation; source-map/generated-shader panels as additions.

## Success criteria

- Workflows green.

## Test plan

- Unit: none.
- E2E: workflow scripts from 01.7 executed against the upstream editor on the routed build and the pinned original (import, edit, undo/redo, scripts, animation, persistence, player, export/publish, XR entry, renderer changes); Inspector/devtools panels compared to upstream's public data; TSL tools exercised; editor-authored script execution verified.
- Logging: per-workflow step events and panel snapshots; archived under `evidence/21b.5/`.
- Failure artifacts: project state dumps and exports.

## Considerations

- The engine's policy against introducing `eval` does not prohibit the editor's scripting feature (§5.14).
acceptance_criteria: Every editor/tool manifest workflow is tested end to end on real projects against the pinned original (author, edit, undo/redo, script, play, export, publish, reload); Inspector/devtools panels show truthful public data plus separate F3D diagnostics; editor scripting works as upstream.

title: Workers, offscreen, library and environment flows (generation-tagged worker protocol)
description:
## Full scope

Workers, offscreen, library and environment flows: existing worker/offscreen/library examples; dedicated-worker ownership of supported CPU/GPU tasks preserving input ordering and observation semantics; device/resources/submission stay in their owner realm (no GPUDevice transfer assumption); OffscreenCanvas selection tested before relying on main-thread fallback; worker messages carry task/region identity, sequence, scene/device generation and ownership; cancelled jobs retain drain obligations; MIME/URL/loading policies, credentials/errors, server-side utility imports; SharedArrayBuffer pools only as the later isolated option with real design and target tests

## Summary

Off-main-thread execution without changing semantics.

## Background (plan §11.6, §5.12 "Deployment, workers and environment behavior", §10.4)

"A synchronous public read cannot become an asynchronous worker round trip without an admitted transformation." "SharedArrayBuffer pools are a later, isolated-deployment option. They require a real scheduler/memory-safety design and target tests, not a `std::thread::spawn` call in an ordinary Wasm build."

## Technical approach

- Worker job protocol in `f3d-runtime` with generation-tagged messages (05.1 handles); OffscreenCanvas capability probe; retained worker examples (`DRACOLoader` workers, offscreen example) through the resolver; isolated option gated on 10.3's headers.

## Success criteria

- Family green; ABA/delayed-response test (05.7) extended to workers.

## Test plan

- Unit: worker protocol tests (task/region identity, sequence, scene/device generation, ownership tags); delayed-response-after-ID-reuse rejection; OffscreenCanvas capability probe tests; drain-obligation tests for cancelled jobs.
- E2E: worker/offscreen/library examples through the routed build on both browsers; DRACO worker pools; ordering/observation tests for worker-hosted execution; isolated option (if implemented) under real headers with additive measurement.
- Logging: worker message traces `{job, region, sequence, generation, event}`; archived under `evidence/21b.6/`.
- Failure artifacts: message traces around the violation.

## Considerations

- Force-terminating a worker is not proof its committed effects were rolled back (§11.6).
acceptance_criteria: Every deployment/worker/environment manifest record is owned and tested; worker-hosted execution (where selected) passes ordering/observation tests; delayed worker responses after ID reuse are rejected; the isolated shared-memory option, if implemented, has its own scheduler/memory-safety design and target tests and is measured additively.

title: Alternate renderers closure (CSS2D/CSS3D/SVG full API and any other shipped output backend)
description:
## Full scope

Alternate renderers closure: the complete public API of CSS2DRenderer/CSS2DObject, CSS3DRenderer/CSS3DObject/CSS3DSprite, SVGRenderer/SVGObject/Projector and any other shipped output backend discovered by the census; real DOM/CSS/vector output with documented upstream limitations preserved; mixed views with accelerated cameras; no GPU request for non-GPU scenes; every method/option/event tested.

## Summary

21a.1 established the routes for Phase 0/1. This bead closes the family: every manifest record for the alternate renderers has an owner and positive tests, including options (`setSize`, `render` ordering, `domElement` structure, sorting, `overdraw`, quality settings, `SVGObject` node handling, `Projector` results) and interaction with accelerated scenes.

## Background (plan §5.12 "Alternate renderers", §5.14, §23 [S59], [S60])

"Keep real DOM/CSS/vector output and documented limitations; no mandatory GPU request for non-GPU scenes." "Flattening labels or SVG into the canvas is not equivalent."

## Technical approach

- From the manifest, enumerate the family records; retained modules through the facade; positive tests per record comparing DOM/SVG structure, computed styles/transforms and event targets with upstream at logical frames; mixed-view tests with a Wasm-owned camera/object set (materialization 06.4).
- Absence-of-WebGPU tests reuse 18b.5's profile.

## Success criteria

- Family suite green on Chrome and Safari; manifest updated; no Wasm/GPU initialization on non-GPU pages.

## Test plan

- Unit: none (retained JS); the census drives the test list.
- E2E: `tests/e2e/alt-renderers/*.mjs` per renderer with DOM/SVG snapshot comparison and event-target checks; mixed CSS+WebGPU script.
- Logging: per-record events with structural diff summaries; `owner: retained-js`; archived under `evidence/21b.7/`.
- Failure artifacts: serialized DOM/SVG of both sides and the diff.

## Considerations

- Documented upstream limitations (for example SVGRenderer's material support) are preserved, not "fixed".
acceptance_criteria: Every alternate-renderer manifest record is owned and tested with DOM/SVG structural equality to upstream, mixed accelerated views keep camera observations consistent, and non-GPU pages never initialize Wasm or WebGPU.

title: F3D-22 (early slice): First-backend fault injection (queued effects, error scopes, device loss during compile/upload/submit, cancellation at every boundary, submission-epoch retirement)
description:
## What this epic delivers

The lifecycle safety that must exist before the first performance claim. Plan §19 F3D-22 depends on 02 and 05 (early); acceptance: "Queued effects/error scopes/loss, exact native lifetime and stale-result safety".

## Why (plan §11.4, §11.5, §11.7, §14.7, §19 "No task defers the safety or semantic precondition of an earlier claimed performance result")

"These checks are part of the initial backend, not late release instrumentation. Include red-A/blue-B uniform snapshots, cancelled queued uploads, invalid pipeline creation, bundle/direct state transitions, and delayed errors after device replacement in the first integrated tests."

## Children

1. Queued-effect commit boundaries; cancellation is not rollback.
2. Error-scope serialization, asynchronous validation, failed-compile-not-cached, delayed errors after replacement.
3. Device loss during compile/upload/submit; fresh device path; state-class table.
4. Lifecycle cancellation matrix.
5. Submission-epoch retirement and credit window.

## Success criteria for the epic

All children closed before F3D-11's scored runs (F3D-11 depends on it).

## No-claim boundary

Recovery of GPU-only state is explicitly not promised here (see 17.7/22b.1).
acceptance_criteria: The first backend distinguishes preparation, issued transfers, submission, completion and publication; cancellation never pretends to roll back issued queue effects; error scopes are serialized; device loss during compilation, upload and submission never publishes stale results into a replacement device; cancellation at every supported await/publication boundary, disposal while pending, Wasm memory growth and delayed worker responses after ID reuse are tested; retirement uses coarse submission epochs with a bounded credit window.

title: Queued-effect commit boundaries; cancellation is not rollback
description:
## Full scope

Queued-effect commit boundaries: track preparation, each issued transfer (writeBuffer/writeTexture/external-image copies are already queue effects before submit), command submission, completion and logical publication separately; cancellation prevents stale publication and records terminal outcomes but never claims rollback of issued effects; private/versioned destinations preferred until publication where the source allows

## Summary

"A policy saying that everything before submission is rollback-safe is incorrect."

## Background (plan §11.4; AGENTS.md "Cancellation is not rollback of issued effects")

## Technical approach

- Job state machine in `f3d-runtime` integrated with Asupersync regions (02.5); versioned private staging destinations (07.1) with publication at epoch boundaries; telemetry of outcomes.

## Success criteria

- Tests: cancel before issue (nothing issued), cancel after issue before submit, cancel after submit; each with the documented outcome.

## Test plan

- Unit: job state-machine tests (preparation → issued transfer → submission → completion → publication) with cancellation at each state asserting the documented outcome; private-destination publication tests.
- E2E: `tests/e2e/fault/queued-effects.mjs` on both browsers: cancel before issue (nothing issued), after issue before submit (effect issued, publication cancelled, shared-buffer state per contract), after submit (not retractable); no stale publication; no false rollback claim in telemetry.
- Logging: job events `{job, state, outcome, effects_issued}`; archived under `evidence/22a.1/`.
- Failure artifacts: buffer readbacks and the job timeline.

## Considerations

- "After submission the GPU work is not generally retractable."
acceptance_criteria: The runtime's GPU job model has explicit states for the five boundaries; a cancelled upload task whose writeBuffer was already issued is recorded as "effect issued, publication cancelled" and the shared buffer's visible state is handled per the source contract; tests demonstrate no stale publication and no false rollback claims.

title: Error-scope serialization, async validation, failed-compile-not-cached, delayed errors
description:
## Full scope

Error-scope serialization and asynchronous validation: push/issue/pop without intervening awaits or user callbacks, results awaited afterwards; operation-specific result promises and error provenance under concurrent setup; a synchronously returned GPU object is not evidence of validity; failed pipeline compilation never becomes a cache entry; delayed errors after device replacement attributed to the old generation

## Summary

GPU validation is asynchronous and error scopes are shared state.

## Background (plan §11.7, §23 [S38], [S44])

## Technical approach

- Extend 05.6's helper into the job model; per-operation promise registry keyed by generation; cache insertion only after async success.

## Success criteria

- Tests listed pass on both browsers.

## Test plan

- Unit: error-scope helper tests (no `await` inside the body; nesting per operation); promise-registry tests keyed by generation; cache-insertion-after-success tests.
- E2E: `tests/e2e/fault/validation.mjs` on both browsers: concurrent preparation tasks cannot interleave scopes; invalid pipeline creation produces attributed errors and no cache entry; an error arriving after device replacement is logged against the old generation and ignored by the new device.
- Logging: validation events `{operation, generation, scope_kinds, error, attributed_to}`; archived under `evidence/22a.2/`.
- Failure artifacts: the error-scope timeline.

## Considerations

- Out-of-memory handling is not a capacity-discovery algorithm; budgets are conservative (07.1).
acceptance_criteria: Concurrent preparation tasks cannot interleave error scopes (assertion in tests); pipeline/validation errors are attributed to the right operation and generation; an invalid pipeline creation test shows no cache pollution; an error arriving after device replacement is logged against the old generation and ignored by the new device's state.

title: Device loss during compile/upload/submit with fresh-device path and state-class table
description:
## Full scope

Device loss during compilation, upload and submission: every resource/pipeline of the lost generation invalidated; fresh adapter/device acquisition with bounded retries (never re-requesting from a consumed/expired adapter); fresh device-generation handles; explicit canvas/history reconfiguration; stale compile/decode/worker results cannot publish into the replacement; committed source callbacks are not automatically rerun; tests distinguish reconstruction success, admitted reset, unrecoverable loss and deliberate teardown

## Summary

Device loss handled by generation, not by hope.

## Background (plan §11.5, §6.5, §23 [S51])

"Use a fresh adapter/device acquisition path, bounded retries, fresh device-generation handles, and explicit canvas/history reconfiguration. Do not repeatedly request replacement devices from an already consumed or expired adapter. A stale compile/decode/worker result cannot publish into the replacement. Do not automatically rerun already committed source callbacks."

## Technical approach

- Loss handler in `f3d-runtime`: bump device generation (05.1), tear down the session region's GPU children with drain (02.3), acquire a new adapter+device (05.6), recreate class-1 resources, apply class-2/3 policies (17.7 later extends), reconfigure canvas; expose the source-visible event contract (upstream's `webglcontextlost`/`device.lost` behaviors as applicable to the route).
- Injection via `device.destroy()` in tests at each point.

## Success criteria

- Tests pass; policies documented.

## Test plan

- Unit: loss-handler tests with a fake device (generation bump; region drain; class-1 recreation from authoritative versions; bounded retries; consumed-adapter rule).
- E2E: `tests/e2e/fault/device-loss.mjs` on both browsers injecting `device.destroy()` during compilation, upload and submission on H1/H2: recovery or policy outcome per resource class; stale old-generation results rejected; source-visible event contract preserved; the four outcome classes asserted.
- Logging: loss/recovery events `{point, generation_old, generation_new, resources_recreated, outcome}`; archived under `evidence/22a.3/`.
- Failure artifacts: the resource arena dump before/after and the first frame after recovery.

## Considerations

- Loss is a terminal cleanup outcome for in-flight frames, never a successful completion (§11.4).
acceptance_criteria: Injected device loss at each of the three points leads to the documented recovery path with immutable/CPU-authoritative resources recreated from current versions, and every other resource class handled per the §11.5 table; a stale result from the old generation is rejected; H1/H2 recover or report per policy; the four outcome classes are asserted by tests.

title: Lifecycle cancellation matrix (every boundary, dispose pending, memory growth, delayed worker)
description:
## Full scope

Lifecycle cancellation matrix: cancel at every supported await/publication boundary; dispose resources while work is pending; grow Wasm memory mid-operation; deliver delayed worker responses after ID reuse; assert no leaks, no stale publication and correct terminal outcomes

## Summary

The §14.7 lifecycle program, executed systematically.

## Background (plan §14.7 "Add lifecycle tests")

## Technical approach

- Boundary enumeration from the job model (22a.1) and region model (02.5); scenario generator; leak detection via resource arena accounting (07.1) and Asupersync region drain checks.

## Success criteria

- Matrix green.

## Test plan

- Unit: scenario-matrix generator tests (boundary enumeration from the job/region models; bounded sampling when combinatorial).
- E2E: the generated matrix (cancel at each await/publication boundary × dispose while pending × memory growth mid-operation × delayed worker response after ID reuse) on H1/H2 scenes on both browsers; leak detection via arena accounting and region drain checks; every scenario ends in a documented terminal state.
- Logging: per-scenario `{boundary, action, terminal_state, leaked_resources}`; archived under `evidence/22a.4/`.
- Failure artifacts: the leaked-resource list and the scenario timeline.

## Considerations

- Keep scenario count bounded; sample when combinatorial.
acceptance_criteria: A generated matrix of (boundary × action) scenarios runs against the first backend with H1/H2 scenes; every scenario ends in a documented terminal state with cleanup counters balanced; the matrix is part of the functional lane.

title: Submission-epoch retirement and bounded credit window via onSubmittedWorkDone
description:
## Full scope

Submission-epoch retirement and bounded credit window: track retirement in coarse submission epochs; use queue.onSubmittedWorkDone as a high-water-mark acknowledgement (not a per-command-buffer fence) to release eligible credits without serially awaiting every frame; loss/failure is terminal cleanup, not completion

## Summary

Completion tracking that is both correct and fast.

## Background (plan §11.4 last paragraph, §16.3, §23 [S49])

## Technical approach

- Epoch counter per submission; ack callbacks map to epochs; retirement queue (07.1) drains up to the acked epoch; credits released; bench lane (03.2) uses the same mechanism.

## Success criteria

- Tests: window enforcement, retirement timing, terminal path; H1 steady state shows two frames in flight.

## Test plan

- Unit: epoch/credit accounting tests (window enforced at two; retirement drains to the acked epoch; terminal cleanup releases credits without counting a completed frame).
- E2E: `tests/e2e/fault/retirement.mjs` on both browsers: H1 steady state shows two frames in flight with no self-await; a failed/lost submission takes the terminal path; staging-ring reuse only after ack.
- Logging: per-submission `{epoch, submit_ts, ack_ts, credits, retired}`; archived under `evidence/22a.5/`.
- Failure artifacts: the credit timeline.

## Considerations

- Do not busy-spin or starve the event loop (§16.3).
acceptance_criteria: Resource retirement and staging-ring reuse are driven by acknowledged submission epochs; the credit window bounds frames in flight to the protocol's value (two) for scored runs; no frame awaits its own completion; a failed/lost submission releases credits via the terminal-cleanup path without counting as a completed frame.

title: F3D-22 (closure): Final context/device recovery, page lifecycle, exact native lifetimes, memory budgets
description:
## What this epic delivers

Lifecycle closure. Plan §19 F3D-22 closure "uses 17"; acceptance extends the early slice to "final context/device recovery".

## Why (plan §11.5, §12.5, §18 Phase 5, §22 "The foundation is real")

"Verify host/CSP constraints, cold startup, memory pressure, device/context loss, mobile thermal behavior, integration permissions and interaction tails."

## Children

1. GPU-history/simulation recovery classes with charged costs.
2. Page lifecycle behaviors.
3. Exact native context loss/restore, XR session reset, canvas identity across replacement.
4. Memory budgets, address-space checks and OOM policy.

## Success criteria for the epic

All children closed; lifecycle suites in the functional, forced and exact lanes.

## No-claim boundary

"A terminated page or noncooperative foreign operation has no universal finalization-time guarantee" (§11.5).
acceptance_criteria: GPU-history and simulation recovery classes are implemented and tested with charged checkpoint costs; page lifecycle transitions (hide/show, suspension, resize, scene replacement, timer-policy restoration, bounded obsolete-frame backlog) behave as upstream; exact native context loss/restore, XR session reset and canvas identity across replacement are correct; CPU/Wasm, staging and GPU memory budgets are enforced with address-space checks and an explicit OOM policy.

title: GPU-history and simulation recovery classes end to end with charged costs
description:
## Full scope

GPU-history and simulation recovery classes end to end: checkpoint/replay under the numeric and input-history contract where admitted, visible admitted reset otherwise, unrecoverable-loss reporting; checkpoint readback bandwidth/latency/memory charged to results; no seamless-preservation claims

## Summary

Close the recovery story for state the CPU never had.

## Background (plan §11.5)

"Mandatory readback checkpoints have a real bandwidth/latency/memory cost and must be included in results; they are not a free recovery guarantee. A reset is visible application behavior and cannot be described as seamless state preservation."

## Technical approach

- Policy configuration per resource class; optional checkpoint scheduling through the pass graph with cost telemetry; user-facing event/error shape aligned with upstream's context-loss behavior where the source observes it.

## Success criteria

- Tests per class and case; cost lines in results.

## Test plan

- Unit: policy-configuration tests per resource class; checkpoint scheduling tests in the pass graph with cost accounting.
- E2E: device-loss injection during SSGI/TRAA and H8 on both browsers with each class policy; checkpoint policy enabled runs show the cost in bench results; user-facing event/error shape compared to upstream's context-loss behavior.
- Logging: recovery events with class, action, outcome and checkpoint bytes; archived under `evidence/22b.1/`.
- Failure artifacts: post-recovery frames and the policy decision log.

## Considerations

- Deterministic clocks do not make arbitrary GPU replay bit-deterministic.
acceptance_criteria: For the temporal fidelity cases and H8, device loss follows the class policy with tests for each outcome; if a checkpoint policy is enabled its cost appears in the benchmark results; the report never describes a reset as seamless.

title: Page lifecycle: hide/show, suspension, resize, scene replacement, timer policy, backlog
description:
## Full scope

Page lifecycle: hide/show, page suspension and resume, resize, scene replacement, restoration of the source's timer policy; bounded processing of obsolete-frame backlogs without rewriting a source simulation's time step; teardown ordering with drained regions

## Summary

The browser lifecycle, respected.

## Background (plan §11.5 last paragraph)

"Test hide/show, page suspension, resize, scene replacement, and restoration of the source's timer policy. Avoid processing an unbounded obsolete-frame backlog, but do not silently rewrite a source simulation's time step to accomplish it."

## Technical approach

- Runtime hooks on `visibilitychange`/`pagehide`/`resize`; region policies; trace comparisons under scripted lifecycle events.

## Success criteria

- Tests green on both browsers and on the phone (backgrounding).

## Test plan

- Unit: lifecycle hook tests with fake events (`visibilitychange`, `pagehide`, resize) and region policies.
- E2E: scripted lifecycle events on both browsers and on the phone (real backgrounding): rAF pause/resume semantics, resize, scene replacement with drain, timer-policy restoration, bounded backlog after a long background period with the same logical updates as upstream (no time-step rewrite).
- Logging: lifecycle events `{event, backlog_frames, processed, policy}`; archived under `evidence/22b.2/`.
- Failure artifacts: trace diffs around the transition.

## Considerations

- Interacts with thermal protocol runs (23.3).
acceptance_criteria: Lifecycle transitions behave observably as upstream (rAF pause/resume semantics, resize handling, scene replacement with region drain); after a long background period the candidate processes the same logical updates upstream would (no silent time-step rewrite) within a bounded backlog policy documented in the report.

title: Exact native context loss/restore, XR session reset, canvas identity across replacement
description:
## Full scope

Exact native context loss/restore, XR session reset and canvas identity across replacement: WebGL context loss/restoration through the exact component with upstream event contract; XR session end/reset with reference-space resets; renderer replacement at source-supported boundaries only; stale worker/compile/decode results rejected across replacement

## Summary

The exact route's lifetimes and the replacement boundary.

## Background (plan §5.6, §6.9, §20 "Late backend choice breaks canvas identity or native resources")

## Technical approach

- Tests extending 04.3/04.4; XR reset via the capable lane; generation checks across replacement.

## Success criteria

- Tests green.

## Test plan

- Unit: replacement-boundary tests (a new renderer instance is a new decision; switching an exposed canvas fails); generation checks across replacement for worker/compile/decode results.
- E2E: exact-lane forced context loss/restore with upstream's events and re-upload behavior on both browsers; XR session end/reset on the capable lane; `WebGLXRFallback` replacement pattern; stale results after replacement rejected.
- Logging: loss/restore and replacement events with generations; archived under `evidence/22b.3/`.
- Failure artifacts: GL error logs and the decision log.

## Considerations

- Never counts toward new-backend coverage.
acceptance_criteria: Exact-lane tests cover forced context loss/restore with upstream's events and resource re-upload behavior; XR session reset tests pass on the capable lane; a renderer replacement at a source boundary (WebGLXRFallback pattern) creates a new route decision while an attempt to switch an exposed canvas fails; stale results are rejected by generation.

title: Memory budgets: CPU/Wasm, staging and GPU distinct; address-space checks; OOM policy
description:
## Full scope

Memory budgets: CPU/Wasm memory, upload staging and GPU allocations as distinct budgets even on unified memory; individual allocations and total live reservations bounded below tested device budgets; checked address arithmetic and chunking within the wasm32 address space (no memory64 assumption); explicit OOM policy; bounded caches proven under pressure

## Summary

Memory realism.

## Background (plan §12.5, §16.6 "Startup and memory")

"Browser WebGPU does not make arbitrary Wasm memory directly usable as a GPU buffer. Bound individual allocations and total live reservations below the tested application/device budget; a large GPU buffer limit is not available RAM."

## Technical approach

- Budget enforcement in 07.1/05.4; pressure tests; phone runs.

## Success criteria

- Tests green; results feed 23.4.

## Test plan

- Unit: budget-enforcement tests per budget (CPU/Wasm, staging, GPU) driving each to its limit and asserting backpressure/eviction; checked address arithmetic tests at the wasm32 boundary; OOM policy tests with a fake allocator.
- E2E: memory-pressure runs of each headline artifact on the phone and M5 with peak accounting vs the frozen budgets; base64 decoding transients included.
- Logging: per-run memory `metric` events per budget and pressure events `{budget, action: backpressure|evict|oom-policy}`; archived under `evidence/22b.4/`.
- Failure artifacts: the allocation timeline at the overage.

## Considerations

- Base64 decoding transients count (10.2).
acceptance_criteria: The three budgets are enforced with tests that drive each to its limit and observe backpressure/eviction rather than OOM; address arithmetic is checked; a memory-pressure run of each headline artifact on the phone stays within the frozen budget or reports the exact overage.

title: F3D-23: Complete feature-host and performance hardware validation
description:
## What this epic delivers

Phase 5's validation campaign. Plan §19 F3D-23 depends on 18–22; acceptance: "Capable-host parity plus unchanged paired performance/thermal/startup/memory gates".

## Why (plan §16.6, §18 Phase 5, §22)

"Run held-out workloads and final full-feature/forced-new-backend/exact-native suites on appropriate reserved hardware."

## Children

1. Capable-host matrix runs and unavailable-host evidence classes.
2. Full scored benchmark campaign.
3. Thermal sustained phone protocol.
4. Startup/memory validation against frozen budgets.
5. Build cost and developer-experience measurements.
6. Held-out final workloads and final suites on reserved hardware.

## Success criteria for the epic

All children closed with published results.

## No-claim boundary

"Neither finite corpus establishes a universal 3× guarantee for all Three.js applications" (§16.6).
