acceptance_criteria: All lanes run on all strata and capable hosts with unavailable-host obligations listed; the full scored benchmark campaign across H1–H8, controls and the fidelity set on all four strata meets or fails the unchanged §16.6 gates with published intervals; thermal, startup/memory and build-cost validations complete; held-out workloads and final suites run on reserved hardware.

title: Capable-host matrix runs and unavailable-host evidence classes
description:
## Full scope

Capable-host matrix runs: functional, forced-new-backend and exact lanes on every stratum and browser, XR headset lane, permission-dependent lanes (media, file input, pointer lock, fullscreen); device-specific blocks accepted only when the reference cannot exercise the same operation with the same permissions/capabilities; unavailable hosts recorded as outstanding obligations

## Summary

Every feature, on every capable host, honestly.

## Background (plan §14.10, §18 Phase 4 "Complete a capable-host matrix")

## Technical approach

- Orchestrate the lanes across 03.7's device inventory plus the XR/permission lanes; aggregate into the matrix.

## Success criteria

- Matrix published.

## Test plan

- Unit: matrix aggregation tests (five separate columns per host; `host-blocked` requires reference evidence; obligations listed, never counted).
- E2E: functional, forced-new-backend and exact lanes on every stratum/browser from the device inventory plus the XR headset lane and permission-dependent lanes (media, file input, pointer lock, fullscreen).
- Logging: per-host lane summaries and the matrix JSON with evidence pointers; archived under `evidence/23.1/`.
- Failure artifacts: lane result files per host.

## Considerations

- Product labels never determine capabilities; probe at runtime.
acceptance_criteria: A per-stratum/per-host results matrix exists with the five coverage numbers per host; every host-blocked record has reference evidence; obligations for unavailable hosts are listed explicitly and never counted as passes.

title: Full scored benchmark campaign H1-H8 on all four strata under protocol v1
description:
## Full scope

Full scored benchmark campaign: H1–H8 on iPhone 17 Pro Max (Safari; Chrome separately), M5 (Safari and Chrome), NVIDIA and AMD discrete GPUs (Chrome/Windows; Linux lanes separate); frozen protocol v1; per-cell 2x floor with 95% lower bounds, per-stratum 3x geomean; H7/H8 required; tail budgets; controls within 5%; negative and startup controls; fidelity set; all-valid-cases aggregate; every reference configuration published; new-backend ownership asserted for all scored frames

## Summary

The launch performance contract, executed exactly as frozen.

## Background (plan §16.6, §15.4, §15.6, §16.4)

## Technical approach

- `f3d bench` across strata on reserved devices per 03.7 discipline; analysis via 03.8; publication template.

## Success criteria

- Results package; verdict table.

## Test plan

- Unit: protocol-loading and cell-set tests (required cells from the corpus manifest; a missing candidate run produces a FAILED_CELL row).
- E2E: `f3d bench` across all four strata on reserved devices per 03.7 discipline for H1–H8, controls (negative and startup controls) and the fidelity set; on-screen companion runs; ownership assertion on all scored frames; analysis via 03.8 with per-cell and per-stratum verdicts.
- Logging: raw per-frame JSON per run, capability records, telemetry breakdowns, the analysis reports and the all-valid-cases aggregate; archived under `evidence/23.2/<stratum>/`.
- Failure artifacts: invalidated runs retained with reasons; failed cells reported, never excluded.

## Considerations

- "A changed product decision or benchmark corpus requires a newly labeled plan/results version."
acceptance_criteria: The complete results package exists: raw paired runs, analysis outputs, per-cell and per-stratum verdicts against every §16.6 row, control and fidelity results, the all-valid-cases aggregate, and the reference configurations; any failed cell or stratum is reported as a failure; nothing is excluded or relabeled.

title: Thermal sustained phone protocol (20-minute sessions, steady segment scored)
description:
## Full scope

Thermal sustained phone protocol: 20-minute sustained sessions with paired cooldown/recovery and recorded power/charging policy; final steady segment reported separately from the initial cool segment; phone floors evaluated on the sustained segment; energy per frame only with a supporting instrument

## Summary

A phone that wins for thirty seconds and then throttles has not won. This bead runs the sustained protocol the gate requires.

## Background (plan §16.5, §12.5, §16.6 "Thermal"; AGENTS.md "Thermal")

"Run a sustained mobile session, provisionally 20 minutes, with paired cooldown/recovery conditions and a recorded power/charging policy. Report the final steady segment separately from the initial cool segment. The phone's scored performance floor must hold in the declared sustained segment; a brief cool-start win does not satisfy a sustained-use claim." "Report energy per frame only with an instrument or counter that supports that claim. Do not infer a precise power improvement from CPU timings or a noisy change in battery percentage."

## Technical approach

- Use the thermal script from 03.7: per cell, run reference then candidate (order alternated across repeats) for the protocol's sustained duration with periodic completed-frame throughput samples (03.2 lane in on-screen and offscreen forms), matched cooldown between runs until the device returns to the recorded baseline temperature proxy, identical brightness/DPR/charging policy.
- Segmentation rule from the protocol (03.6): the steady segment is the final N minutes; report both segments and the transition.
- Analysis (03.8) on steady-segment blocks; pacing/input-latency companion numbers from the on-screen runs.
- Record OS thermal-state signals where exposed; otherwise mark unknown.

## Success criteria

- Sustained results table per cell with steady-segment verdicts; cool-segment numbers published alongside, clearly labeled.

## Test plan

- Unit: segmentation tests (steady segment = final N minutes; cool/steady separation cannot manufacture a difference on reference-vs-reference data).
- E2E: sustained paired sessions per headline cell on the phone (Safari; Chrome lane separately) with alternating order, matched cooldown to the recorded baseline proxy, identical brightness/DPR/charging policy; analysis on steady-segment blocks; on-screen pacing/input-latency companions.
- Logging: throughput time series `{t, frames, throughput, thermal_proxy, charging}` and segment summaries; archived under `evidence/23.3/`.
- Failure artifacts: the full time series for any failing cell.

## Considerations

- Reserved device: no other agent work on the phone or its host Mac during runs.
- Chrome on iOS is a separate lane with its actual engine and capabilities recorded (§12.1).
acceptance_criteria: For every headline cell on the iPhone 17 Pro Max stratum, sustained paired sessions (candidate and frozen reference, alternating order, matched cooldown) produce throughput series segmented into initial-cool and steady segments; the 2x cell floor and 3x stratum geomean are evaluated on the steady segment with intervals; thermal state and charging policy are logged; any energy claim cites the instrument used or is absent.

title: Startup and memory validation against frozen budgets (cold/warm, hitches, no OOM)
description:
## Full scope

Startup and memory validation against frozen budgets: cold (document acquisition, decoding, Wasm compilation, shader/pipeline compilation, asset preparation, first correct frame, first interactive frame) and warm startup per artifact class and stratum; reachable-variant compilation hitches; peak memory; bounded caches; no OOM

## Summary

Startup and memory are gates, not footnotes.

## Background (plan §16.4, §16.6 "Startup and memory", §17.4, §10.3)

## Technical approach

- Harness startup timeline; memory accounting (10.2/07.1); interaction scripts hitting unvisited variants.

## Success criteria

- Results; verdicts.

## Test plan

- Unit: startup-timeline parser tests; budget-comparison tests with fixture numbers.
- E2E: cold (cleared caches, fresh document) and warm startup runs for every headline artifact, the small closed scene and the runtime-extensible application on every stratum; interaction scripts hitting unvisited variants to capture compile hitches; peak memory via 10.2/07.1 accounting plus browser-reported values.
- Logging: startup phase `metric` events `{phase, ms}` per run, memory peaks per budget, hitch events `{variant, compile_ms}`; archived under `evidence/23.4/`.
- Failure artifacts: the timeline of any run exceeding a budget.

## Considerations

- Embedded Wasm gets no streaming compilation; report it.
acceptance_criteria: Every headline artifact, the small closed scene and the runtime-extensible application meet or fail the frozen startup/memory budgets on every stratum with the component breakdown published; interaction-tail hitches from lazy variant compilation are reported.

title: Build cost and developer-experience measurements
description:
## Full scope

Build cost and developer-experience measurements: clean and incremental conversion time, Rust/Wasm and shader compilation time, cache hit correctness, generated bytes, latency of changing a common material or update function; source maps and reports identify the original span for rejections and expensive synchronization boundaries

## Summary

Whether the compiler is pleasant and predictable to use is part of whether it is useful. This bead measures it on the real corpus.

## Background (plan §16.9, §3.5, §10.6)

"Measure clean and incremental conversion time, Rust/Wasm and shader compilation time, cache hit correctness, generated bytes, and the latency of changing a common material or update function. These are separate from the frame-throughput score but part of whether the compiler is useful. Rebuilding every generated kernel for a color-only edit is a design regression even if the deployed frame is fast." "Source maps and reports must identify the original application span that caused a rejection or expensive synchronization boundary. Runtime tuning, lazy material compilation, and deoptimization pauses all remain visible in the corresponding cold/interaction measurements."

## Technical approach

- Scripted edit set applied to each corpus application (H1–H8, fidelity cases, held-out set): (a) change a material color literal, (b) change an arithmetic expression in the update loop, (c) replace an asset file, (d) add a GUI control; measure `f3d build` wall time, per-stage timings (ingest, analysis, codegen, Rust/Wasm compile, shader translation, packaging), cache statistics (10.6), and output bytes.
- Cache correctness: after each edit, verify the rebuilt artifact equals a clean build byte-for-byte (determinism) and that untouched units were served from cache.
- Span verification: for a sample of report entries (barriers, exact-route reasons, synchronization boundaries), resolve through the emitted source maps and assert the original file/line.
- Output: `docs/dx-report-v1.md` plus JSON.

## Success criteria

- Report published; the color-only edit rebuilds only material-variant units (assert by cache logs); span checks pass.

## Test plan

- Unit: measurement-script tests on a fixture project (stage timings parsed; cache statistics read; span resolution through source maps).
- E2E: the scripted edit set (material color; update-function expression; asset swap; control addition) applied to every corpus and held-out application on the build machine with clean and incremental timings, cache hit/miss logs and artifact bytes; span checks for a sample of report entries.
- Logging: per-edit `{app, edit, stage, ms, cache_hits, cache_misses, units_rebuilt, bytes}`; archived under `evidence/23.5/`.
- Failure artifacts: the cache log showing over-rebuilding.

## Considerations

- Separate from the throughput score; never merged into it.
- If incremental builds are slow because of a design choice, file a defect bead rather than tuning numbers.
acceptance_criteria: A developer-experience report per corpus application records clean build time, incremental build time after scripted edits (material color change, update-function change, asset swap, control addition), Rust/Wasm compile time, shader translation/compile time, cache hit/miss counts with correctness verification, and artifact bytes; a color-only edit demonstrably rebuilds only the affected content-addressed units; every rejection and synchronization boundary in the report resolves through source maps to the original application span.

title: Held-out final workloads, final suites on reserved hardware, upstream drift check
description:
## Full scope

Held-out final workloads and final full-feature/forced-new-backend/exact-native suites on reserved hardware; latest stable upstream reconciled against the tested r186 target with immutable earlier results retained

## Summary

The last validation pass before the final audit: fresh workloads, all lanes, all strata, and an honest look at what upstream has shipped since the pin.

## Background (plan §18 Phase 5, §5.17, §14.8, §16.7 "Final gate")

"Run held-out workloads and final full-feature/forced-new-backend/exact-native suites on appropriate reserved hardware. Reconcile latest stable upstream changes against the tested version; retain immutable earlier results." "Check the latest stable release before a new FrankenThreeD release and state its tested Three.js version explicitly... A newer unverified release may be used only with its actual retained component and truthful unverified-version status, never as an already-certified accelerated version."

## Technical approach

- Final held-out selection: add workloads not present in any earlier tuning or held-out batch (record the selection date and rationale in `benchmarks/heldout-final-v1.toml` before running anything).
- Run functional, forced-new-backend and exact lanes (18a.4) across the device matrix (03.7) on reserved hardware; archive logs under `evidence/final/`.
- Measure the held-out workloads with the same paired protocol and analysis as the headline cells; publish as held-out results, separate from the headline score.
- Drift: run the census generator's drift mode (01.3) against the latest stable upstream tag; produce the immutable diff (exports, options/properties, shader chunks, registrations, backends, addons, examples, tests); record as `compatibility/drift-r186-to-<latest>.json` for F3D-24.5.

## Success criteria

- Lane results green (or defects filed) on every stratum; held-out results published; drift diff recorded; r186 artifacts and results untouched (hash check).

## Test plan

- Unit: hash-manifest test proving r186 evidence immutability before/after; drift-diff determinism test.
- E2E: all three lanes on reserved hardware across the strata; `f3d verify` and `f3d bench` on the preregistered and final held-out sets; the census drift mode against the latest stable upstream producing the diff.
- Logging: per-lane per-stratum result files; held-out results with intervals; drift report; archived under `evidence/23.6/`.
- Failure artifacts: lane failures and verify artifacts.

## Considerations

- "Do not shift the benchmark oracle midway through an experiment" (§5.17): the drift check is informational for this release.
acceptance_criteria: The preregistered held-out set (12b.4) plus a final set of additional held-out workloads chosen before this bead starts pass functional equivalence and are measured under protocol v1 with published intervals; all three production-route lanes pass on reserved hardware across the strata with the run logs archived; the census drift check against the latest stable upstream release is executed and its diff recorded as a separate unverified target without modifying the r186 oracle or any r186 result.

title: F3D-24: Final full-functionality, accelerated-coverage, deployment, size and version audit (Definition of done)
description:
## What this epic delivers

Kill gate 5 and the definition of done. Plan §19 F3D-24 depends on 23; acceptance: "All Section 22 gates; no feature gap hidden by a narrowed manifest or exact renderer".

## Why (plan §22, §16.7 "Final gate", §14.10 last paragraph)

"The product promise is full Three.js functionality plus independently demonstrated acceleration, not 'a fast supported subset' and not 'the same upstream renderer under a new name.'" "Failing it means no performance-replacement launch claim, even if the implementation is otherwise impressive."

## Children

1. Functional closure audit.
2. Accelerated-rendering closure audit.
3. Deployment audit.
4. Size, ownership and license audit.
5. Version-drift reconciliation.
6. Final report and kill gate 5 decision.

## Success criteria for the epic

All children closed; the decision recorded.

## No-claim boundary

If any gate fails, the release is not labeled a performance replacement or full compatibility; the report says exactly what holds.
acceptance_criteria: All §22 gates hold and are documented: full functionality is real, the product is real, both compatibility and new-backend coverage are real, performance is real, the foundation is real, the implementation remains focused, completeness remains maintainable; no feature gap is hidden by a narrowed manifest or exact renderer; the final report is published.

title: Functional closure audit (zero blocking states, obligations listed, no single percentage)
description:
## Full scope

Functional closure audit: every feature in the pinned source/package/addon/tool universe has a working production implementation under the same source-host prerequisites; no permanent cuts, stubs, placeholder shaders, unimplemented codecs/exporters, omitted runtime variants, missing browser/tool integrations or candidate-specific valid-input refusals; a narrowed application profile cannot change this

## Summary

"Full functionality is real." This audit verifies the first clause of the definition of done against the manifest, the lanes and the plan's family map, and refuses to be summarized as one number.

## Background (plan §22 first paragraph, §5.11, §5.15, §14.10, §18 Phase 4 exit; AGENTS.md "THE NO-CUT RULE")

"Every existing feature in the pinned source/package/addon/tool universe has a working production implementation under the same actual source-host prerequisites. No permanent feature cuts, stubs, placeholder shaders, unimplemented codecs/exporters, omitted runtime variants, missing browser/tool integrations, or candidate-specific valid-input refusals remain. A narrowed application profile cannot change this requirement." Blocking states: `unclassified`, `unimplemented`, `untested`, `known-regression`, `stub`, `no-op-substitute`, `candidate-refusal-on-valid-source`.

## Technical approach

- Run `f3d verify-upstream --ref r186 --features all --tests all` on the final build; export the manifest status table.
- Manual review checklist per §5.12 family row: owner route recorded, positive test references resolve to executed tests in the final lane logs (23.6), invalid-input/mutation/serialization/lifecycle cases present where applicable, runtime-input tests present for loaders/shaders/nodes, host prerequisites match the reference's.
- Spot-check by random sampling of manifest records: open the referenced test, confirm it executes real behavior (not a constructor-existence assertion), confirm its owner tag.
- Deprecated aliases shipped in r186 confirmed present with warning behavior; removed pre-r186 APIs confirmed absent (not invented).
- Write `docs/audits/functional-closure.md` with counts by family and status, open obligations, and reviewer sign-off.

## Success criteria

- Zero blocking states; sampling finds no name-only tests; obligations listed; no aggregate percentage anywhere in the document.

## Test plan

- Unit: none new (verifier rules tested in 18a.5); the sampling script has a fixture test.
- E2E: the verifier run on the final build plus the random-sample review script opening referenced tests and asserting real behavior (not constructor-existence) and owner tags; deprecated-alias presence and removed-API absence checks.
- Logging: the audit document with counts by family and status, the sample list with verdicts, and the open-obligation list; archived under `evidence/24.1/`.
- Failure artifacts: the list of records failing the sample review.

## Considerations

- "A symbol census is not an implementation" (AGENTS.md); the audit cites executed tests, never the census alone.
acceptance_criteria: The release verifier (18a.5) reports zero blocking states across every manifest family with evidence pointers, and a family-by-family manual review confirms each row of §5.12 has a real production owner and positive behavioral tests; the audit document lists every capable-host obligation still open, states explicitly that an obligation is not an exclusion, and records the separate import/symbol, behavior-family, and exact-integration counts.

title: Accelerated-rendering closure audit (forced lane covers every portable family)
description:
## Full scope

Accelerated-rendering closure audit: every portable standard rendering family passes through the new WebGPU backend with retained renderer submission disabled; every exact/native exception names its concrete observable contract and has a validated exact implementation; a renamed upstream renderer cannot pass

## Summary

"Both compatibility and new-backend coverage are real." This audit is what prevents a compatibility-only wrapper from shipping under this project's name.

## Background (plan §5.16, §14.10, §16.6 "New-backend ownership", §22, §3.3)

"Every portable standard rendering family also passes through the new WebGPU backend with retained renderer submission disabled. Genuine native-backend contracts have separately validated exact implementations. A compatibility-only wrapper cannot pass." "Any intrinsic native-backend exception names the concrete observable contract and its real compatible implementation; it cannot be a catch-all category for unfinished rendering. Exact-component presence alone is not functional completion until its integration tests pass."

## Technical approach

- Collect lane-2 results (18a.4) from 23.6: per family, the list of executed cases and the route attribution counters; any case with a nonzero retained-submission count is a failure.
- Exception review: for every manifest record marked exact/native, verify (a) the named contract (sync readback, `getContext`, native handles, custom backend subclass, GL-backed XR session, nonportable GL program per 15b.3), (b) the passing exact-lane test, (c) that no portable material/pass/node hides under the label.
- Scored-frame attribution: confirm from the 23.2 results package that every scored frame carried `route: new-backend`.
- Write `docs/audits/accelerated-closure.md` with family counts, the exception list, and verdict.

## Success criteria

- Zero portable families outside lane 2; every exception justified; scored attribution confirmed.

## Test plan

- Unit: audit-script tests: a synthetic "renamed upstream renderer" fixture (all submissions retained) must be rejected; an exception record without a named contract must be rejected.
- E2E: lane-2 results and attribution counters from 23.6 reviewed per family; exception-by-exception review with passing exact-lane tests; scored-frame attribution confirmed from 23.2's package.
- Logging: the audit document with family counts, the exception table `{record, contract, exact_test}` and the scored-frame attribution summary; archived under `evidence/24.2/`.
- Failure artifacts: the list of families/records failing the audit.

## Considerations

- Retained cold helpers (construction/baking) are allowed and charged; only submission ownership matters here (§9.3).
acceptance_criteria: The forced-new-backend lane results from the final runs cover every portable material/texture/light/shadow/camera/render-target/node/compute/pass family with zero retained submissions (attribution counters from 07.6 attached); the exact-exception list is reviewed record by record and each names an observable native contract with its passing exact-lane test; the audit states the new-backend rendering coverage count separately from functional coverage and confirms the H1–H8 scored frames were attributed to the new backend.

title: Deployment audit (standalone closure, CSP, networked/library modes, pruning, iframe contexts)
description:
## Full scope

Deployment audit: strict standalone closure with no undeclared subresources or isolation prerequisites, every reachable compatibility component and navigation mode included and verified; CSP allowances published; networked/module/library modes verified; small closed artifacts exclude unneeded compatibility code without removing reachable features; iframe/permissions contexts tested

## Summary

"The product is real." The deliverable is a file that works everywhere the plan promised and says so honestly where it cannot.

## Background (plan §10.3, §10.4, §10.6, §16.6 "Deployment" and "Standalone validity", §18 Phase 5, §22)

"Verify normal package/networked/library delivery and strict standalone closure, including reachable native modes and runtime codec/shader paths. Verify host/CSP constraints... Confirm small closed artifacts exclude unneeded compatibility code without removing reachable features." "Test deployment in the intended iframe/permissions context as well as a top-level page; isolation and worker permissions are host conditions, not compiler promises."

## Technical approach

- Re-run 10.5 on the final artifacts for the whole corpus; archive results.
- Pruning check: for the small ordinary scene control artifact, list embedded components and confirm each is reachable per the closure analysis (10.4) and that every reachable component (including exact components reachable through UI branches) is present.
- Context tests: iframe with sandbox/permissions policies, top-level HTTPS, localhost; document which features are host-gated (WebGPU secure context, isolation headers for the isolated profile, permissions for media/XR).
- Networked/library outputs: run the 10.3 verifications and the Node import tests.
- Publish `docs/audits/deployment.md` with the CSP set per mode and the host matrix.

## Success criteria

- All artifacts pass; pruning check passes; contexts documented; no false offline claims.

## Test plan

- Unit: pruning-check tests on a fixture artifact (a reachable component missing fails; an unreachable one present is flagged).
- E2E: packaging harness re-run on every final artifact; iframe (sandbox/permissions policies), top-level HTTPS and localhost contexts; networked/library verifications and Node import tests; CSP directive verification per mode.
- Logging: per-artifact composition tables, request logs with dispositions, context results; archived under `evidence/24.3/`.
- Failure artifacts: blocked-request logs and composition diffs.

## Considerations

- "Isolated/shared-memory results are additional and cannot rescue [the portable] launch score" (§16.6).
acceptance_criteria: For every corpus, fidelity, control and held-out artifact the packaging verification (10.5) results are reviewed and archived; the small closed scene's artifact composition is compared against its dependency closure to show only provably unreachable components were pruned; standalone artifacts are additionally verified inside an iframe with restricted permissions and as a top-level page; networked/module and library outputs pass their verification; the CSP directive set and host requirements per deployment mode are published; no artifact for a live-service application is labeled offline-equivalent.

title: Size, ownership and license audit (245k ceiling, budgets, allowlist, notices)
description:
## Full scope

Size, ownership and license audit: pinned line-count method applied to new Rust (incl. tests and generated engine source), charged Asupersync work, new JS/TS, authored WGSL, generated per-artifact code, retained upstream modules, third-party dependencies; 245k Rust ceiling, 12k JS/TS and 15k WGSL budgets checked; eleven crates; dated nightly; forbid(unsafe_code) boundary; licenses and provenance for every retained/third-party component; no clean-room claims

## Summary

"The implementation remains focused."

## Background (plan §13.5, §17.1, §17.2, §22)

## Technical approach

- Run the pinned line-count script; dependency tree audit; notices check.

## Success criteria

- Audit document.

## Test plan

- Unit: line-count script test on a fixture tree; allowlist and unsafe-boundary checks; notices completeness test (every retained/third-party component has a license entry).
- E2E: the pinned line-count run over the final tree, `cargo tree` audit, and the notices check on every artifact.
- Logging: the code-count report by category, the dependency tree, the notices index; archived under `evidence/24.4/`.
- Failure artifacts: the list of components missing notices or the overage table.

## Considerations

- "A source-inspected implementation is not described as a legally 'clean-room' rewrite merely because it is written in Rust."
acceptance_criteria: The code-count report lists every category with numbers and no category missing; the ceiling and budgets are met or the overage is stated; the dependency allowlist and unsafe boundary are verified; every retained/third-party component has its license and provenance recorded in the artifact notices.

title: Version-drift reconciliation against the latest stable upstream
description:
## Full scope

Version-drift reconciliation: state the tested Three.js version explicitly; immutable diff of exports, options/properties, shader chunks, registrations, backends, addons, examples and tests against the latest stable release; new contracts listed as required parity items for a future target; tested vs unverified targets distinguished; no semver inference

## Summary

"Completeness remains maintainable." The oracle does not move silently, and neither does the claim.

## Background (plan §5.17, §2.2, §22 "Completeness remains maintainable"; AGENTS.md "Upstream Pin Discipline")

"Support the actual pinned stable release, then track upstream changes through an immutable diff of exports, public options/properties, shader chunks, registrations, render/backends, addons, examples and tests. Do not infer compatibility from a semver/version string or a stale docs page. Check the latest stable release before a new FrankenThreeD release and state its tested Three.js version explicitly. Preserve prior completed version targets while an updated target closes its new/changed contracts. New functionality remains a required parity item, not an automatic exception."

## Technical approach

- Take the drift diff from 23.6; categorize entries (added export, changed signature/option/default, removed/deprecated, changed shader chunk, changed registration, new example/test); map each to a §5.12 family.
- Produce the future-target work list (`compatibility/targets/<latest>/parity-items.md`) with counts by family; no beads are created for it in this release (that is a new target decision for the user).
- Update README/status text to name the tested version and the unverified status of anything newer.
- Verify immutability: hash manifest of `compatibility/three-r186.json`, benchmark results and evidence directories unchanged since 23.6.

## Success criteria

- Drift report published; parity list produced; version statement correct; hashes unchanged.

## Test plan

- Unit: drift categorization tests on a synthetic diff; determinism test (re-run yields the same diff); hash check of r186 artifacts.
- E2E: the drift report and parity list generated from 23.6's diff; README/status text validated to name r186 and label newer versions unverified.
- Logging: the drift report and parity list; hash manifest comparison; archived under `evidence/24.5/`.
- Failure artifacts: the hash mismatch list if any r186 artifact changed.

## Considerations

- "A newer unverified release may be used only with its actual retained component and truthful unverified-version status, never as an already-certified accelerated version."
acceptance_criteria: The drift report produced in 23.6 is reviewed and published with a categorized list of new/changed/removed contracts between r186 and the latest stable release; each new contract is recorded as a required parity item for a future explicit target (not as an exception); the release documentation names r186 (commit 148ef33ecb6d2502ff796d4554abd1549c95d519) as the tested version and labels any newer version as unverified with its retained-component status; all r186 results remain immutable.

title: Final report and kill gate 5 decision (Definition of done)
description:
## Full scope

Final report and kill gate 5 decision: pinned version, all inventory counts, new-backend vs exact ownership, completed and unavailable-host evidence, remaining known defects, benchmark results with intervals and raw runs, separately; no plan/static inspection/name census labeled as implemented compatibility; explicit PASS/FAIL against every §22 clause

## Summary

The last honest document.

## Background (plan §14.10 last paragraph, §16.7 "Final gate", §22)

"The final report states the pinned version, all inventory counts, new-backend versus exact ownership, completed and unavailable-host evidence, remaining known defects, and benchmark results separately. It must not label a plan, static source inspection, or symbol-name census as implemented '100% compatibility.'"

## Technical approach

- Assemble from 23.x and 24.x outputs; review with the user.

## Success criteria

- Report published; decision recorded.

## Test plan

- Unit: report assembly test (every §22 clause present with PASS/FAIL and an evidence link; no aggregate percentage; tiers distinguishable).
- E2E: none; the report is reviewed with the user.
- Logging: the final report and `docs/gates/gate-5-final.md`; archived under `evidence/24.6/`.
- Failure artifacts: n/a.

## Considerations

- Solid/frontier/optional tiers remain distinguishable in the report (§18).
acceptance_criteria: docs/gates/gate-5-final.md and the published report exist with every §22 clause marked PASS or FAIL with evidence links; the README status section is updated to reflect exactly what holds; on FAIL the release is not labeled a performance replacement.

title: KILL GATE 1 (Foundation): real browser task execution and cleanup through Asupersync plus a legal WebGPU bridge on Safari and Chrome
description:
## Summary

The first of five kill gates. It exists so the project can stop before any rendering engine is built.

## Background (plan §16.7 "Foundation gate", §2.3, §11.2, §21; AGENTS.md "Early Kill Gates")

"Foundation gate: actual browser task execution/cleanup and a legal WebGPU bridge work on Safari and Chrome. No fake ledger-only execution or native-thread dependency." "Passing a `cargo check` for Wasm, or closing an ownership ledger, is not equivalent to proving that browser tasks actually executed and drained."

## What the decision must cite

- 02.2: polled futures, timer and host-turn wakeups, nonreentrant pump, bounded microtask bursts (Safari + Chrome logs).
- 02.3: cancellation delivered, fetch cancelled, drain before teardown, no late publication, unsupported-host behavior.
- 05.6: first correct frame through the bulk bridge, pixel-identical to direct JS WebGPU, negotiated device profile, serialized error scopes.
- 05.7: the seven counterexamples passing with mutation checks.
- Budget line for charged Asupersync work (02.4) vs the 10,000-line allocation.

## Procedure

Write `docs/gates/gate-1-foundation.md` with the evidence table and verdict. If any item is missing on either browser, the verdict is FAIL and the response per §20 is "Complete the upstream host; no alternate runtime hidden in F3D". This gate blocks F3D-06 and F3D-07 (no engine before the foundation is proven).

## Verification and logging

- The decision cites, by run id, the archived evidence directories of 02.2, 02.3, 05.6 and 05.7 on installed Safari (M5 and iPhone) and Chrome (M5); each cited run's `summary.json` must show every probe passing and the `events.jsonl` must contain the lifecycle events named in those beads.
- A checklist in the decision document maps each foundation requirement to the exact test name and run id; a missing browser or a probe with a `warn`/`error` event is a FAIL.
- Logging: the decision document itself plus a `metric` summary of the charged Asupersync line count vs the allocation; archived under `evidence/G1/`.

## No-claim boundary

Passing says nothing about performance.
acceptance_criteria: A decision document records executable evidence (archived logs from installed Safari and Chrome on physical devices) that Rust futures are polled, woken, cancelled and drained through Asupersync with no native-thread dependency and no ledger-only execution, and that the production bulk bridge renders correct frames and passes the first counterexample suite; verdict PASS or FAIL; on FAIL development stops pending the user's decision.

title: KILL GATE 2 (Bridge): the selected Wasm/host bridge shows an advantage opportunity after its own overhead on matched workloads, given the reference critical-path decomposition
description:
## Summary

The second kill gate: does the architecture's boundary cost leave room for the thesis?

## Background (plan §16.7 "Bridge gate", §1.2, §20 row 2)

"Measure direct JavaScript WebGPU, simple Wasm-to-host calls, bulk command transfer, and generated host submission for matched workloads. The selected path must demonstrate an advantage opportunity after its own overhead; no fixed numeric win is assumed before measurement." Response on failure: "Change granularity/ownership; abandon per-method Wasm wrapping."

## What the decision must cite

- 03.5 tables (throughput, bridge CPU time, copies, calls per variant per browser).
- 03.4 decompositions (p and implied best case per H1/H2/H7/H8).
- 05.6 production-bridge measurements confirming the prototype numbers hold.
- The arithmetic: `speedup = 1 / ((1 - p) + p/k + h)` evaluated with measured h and plausible k per case.

## Procedure

Write `docs/gates/gate-2-bridge.md`. If no variant leaves room on the phone and M5 strata for H1 and H2, the verdict is FAIL; the user decides whether to change ownership granularity or stop. This gate blocks F3D-07 and F3D-08.

## Verification and logging

- The decision cites 03.5's per-browser/per-workload tables, 03.4's decompositions and 05.6's production-bridge measurements by run id, and reproduces the `speedup = 1 / ((1 - p) + p/k + h)` evaluation per case and stratum with the measured `h` and plausible `k`.
- A table lists the selected variant per workload class with its overhead and the resulting room for the 2x/3x targets; any case without room is marked and the verdict reflects it.
- Logging: the decision document plus the computed table as JSON; archived under `evidence/G2/`.

## No-claim boundary

An "advantage opportunity" is a structural estimate, not a result.
acceptance_criteria: A decision document combines the bridge measurements (four variants, per browser, per workload class) with the reference decompositions (removable fraction p per headline case) and states, per case and stratum, whether any bridge variant leaves room for the required 2x/3x after its overhead h; verdict PASS or FAIL with the selected variant per workload class; no fixed numeric win was assumed.

title: KILL GATE 4 (Generalization): repeat the result on held-out applications and at least one discrete-GPU stratum, with measured end-to-end routes for H7 and H8
description:
## Summary

The fourth kill gate: is the first result general, or a two-app trick?

## Background (plan §16.7 "Generalization gate", §14.8, §18 Phase 2 exit)

"Repeat the result on held-out applications and at least one discrete-GPU stratum, with a measured end-to-end route for H7/H8. Profile H7/H8 references during Phase 0 and test promising equivalent kernel/data-path changes early... Microbenchmark improvements alone cannot pass."

## What the decision must cite

- 12b.4 held-out corpus results (functional).
- 13.8, 17.6 (H3–H6) and 16.5/16.6/20.4 (H7/H8) measured routes.
- A discrete-GPU stratum run (03.7 provisioning) for H1/H2 and the held-out set, using the frozen protocol and analysis (03.6/03.8).

## Procedure

Write `docs/gates/gate-4-generalization.md`. If H7/H8 remain below 2× after the profile-justified improvements, record it; the plan's response is "find an equivalent algorithm/data-path improvement or fail launch gate" and the decision is the user's. This gate blocks F3D-23's scored campaign.

## Verification and logging

- The decision cites 12b.4's held-out verify results, the measured routes of 13.8/17.6/16.5/16.6/20.4, and at least one discrete-GPU stratum's paired runs by run id; microbenchmark-only evidence is rejected by the checklist.
- The verdict is computed by the analysis script (03.8) over the cited runs; per-cell and per-stratum rows are reproduced in the document.
- Logging: the decision document plus the analysis outputs; archived under `evidence/G4/`.

## No-claim boundary

Passing here is still not the launch contract (§16.6).
acceptance_criteria: A decision document records: held-out applications transformed by the same compiler passing equivalence with measured paired results; at least one discrete-GPU stratum (NVIDIA or AMD, Chrome/Windows) with paired results for H1/H2 and the held-out set; H7 and H8 end-to-end routes with measured results (whatever they are); verdict PASS or FAIL against the unchanged 2x floor logic; microbenchmark-only evidence is rejected.

title: PARKED: Optional research tier must not start before the core gates pass
description:
## Full scope

PARKED: Optional research tier (geometric algebra kernels, neural rendering, differentiable scene optimization, novel ray tracing, general JavaScript compilation) must not start before the core gates pass

## Summary

The plan's optional research tier, recorded so it is not forgotten and so nobody starts it early.

## Background (plan §18 "Solid, frontier, and optional research", §7.2, §20 "Scope boundaries"; AGENTS.md "Implementation Sequence")

"Optional research: generic geometric-algebra optimization, neural rendering, differentiable scene optimization, novel ray tracing, and more general JavaScript compilation. None is needed to declare the primary product complete, and none should consume the compatibility reserve before the core gates pass." "Use geometric-algebra or exterior-algebra kernels only when a specific operation becomes demonstrably simpler, more robust, or faster, and retain the conventional implementation as a differential oracle."

## Rules

- Deferred until F3D-24.6 passes.
- Never consumes the 30,000-line reserve.
- Must remain distinguishable from Solid and Frontier work in docs, feature gates and status reports.

## No-claim boundary

Nothing in this tier is part of the product promise.
acceptance_criteria: This bead is a placeholder and stays deferred; it may be undeferred only after kill gate 5 records PASS, and any research item must then be split into its own beads with a differential oracle against the conventional implementation.
